What happened overnight

The Chancellor will have woken up to jittery markets after Google-owner Alphabet revealed higher spending on AI.

Alphabet dropped 10pc in after-hours trading, wiping nearly $400 billion off its market value. Microsoft, by contrast, beat forecasts with better-than-expected cash flows that lifted its shares by 3pc.

MSCI’s broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan dropped 0.7pc, while Japan’s Nikkei fluctuated between gains and losses and was last ⁠up 1pc.

Oil prices retreated as investors latched onto hopes that peace talks to resolve the Middle East conflict could be back on the table.

European stocks were on track to edge higher at the open after the US Federal Reserve held interest rates steady as widely expected on Wednesday. The European Central Bank announces its next interest rate decision on Thursday.

News.title: Risk of Ebola spread in UK is low, experts stress
News.content:
Infectious disease experts have stressed the likelihood of Ebola spreading to the UK is low after the head of Africa’s health agency warned that the haemorrhagic fever could reach Britain.

The Democratic Republic of Congo is struggling to contain an outbreak of the Bundibugyo strain of the deadly virus that began in the volatile eastern region of the country. There have been 10,000 cases, including nearly 5,000 deaths, since the outbreak was first reported in May and it has now become the second largest Ebola epidemic in history.

In recent weeks the virus has spread to Kenya, where there have been nine cases including two deaths, and Nigeria. The case in Nigeria is concerning because the patient, the wife of a Swiss diplomat based in Abuja, the country’s capital, had no history of travel to the affected region of DRC. She has now been evacuated to Switzerland.

In comments reported by the Guardian Jean Kaseya, head of the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention, described the outbreak as “unprecedented” as it was the first time that the disease had spread to three geographic regions of the continent. He warned that there was scope for further spread.

“We shouldn’t forget that at the beginning of Covid, many countries said there was zero risk of being affected, but a few months later, they became the hotspot,” he said. “We don’t want to see the UK and other countries become the hotspot.”

On Wednesday the United States announced that travellers arriving by air would have to sign a statement affirming that they had not been in the DRC within the previous 21 days. Anyone found to provide false or misleading information would face imprisonment or a fine.

The UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) stressed that the risk to the UK is low. Dr Sam Collins, head of guidance, clinical and public health response at the agency, said the Ebola outbreak in DRC is serious but “the UK is well prepared to respond safely and effectively to the risk of imported cases arising here”.

UKHSA is monitoring travel routes from the affected countries and is providing information on symptoms.

The UKHSA said it is rare for Ebola to occur in returning travellers and the NHS has “well established procedures in place” for such a situation.

News.title: Wesley Fofana’s Chelsea nightmare continues as Liverpool win shoot-out
News.content:
It is an all-Premier League tie at Anfield as Liverpool host Chelsea in the last 16 of the League Cup, with a place in the quarter-finals at stake. This will be the first managerial meeting between childhood friends Andoni Iraola and Xabi Alonso.

Liverpool beat Tottenham 3-1 at Anfield in the last round of this competition, which included a stunning goal from Dominik Szoboszlai to seal progression to the last 16. They earned their first home Premier League win of the season on the weekend as they beat Brighton 2-0. Iraola’s men come into this game off the back of four straight wins in all competitions.

“There will definitely be changes, but we want to win the game and we want to be competitive,” Iraola said ahead of this tie. “We have to see how the legs; we are not just in the Carabao Cup, but also in the Champions League and we have been trying to make changes from game to game. We want to be in the next round. We have been unlucky in the draw, playing Chelsea, and they have been unlucky also. But we want to be in the draw again and that only happens if you win. We need to rotate, all the top teams need to rotate when you are playing every three days. Sometimes you are forced to rotate due to injury or sometimes different demands in different games tactically. I am happy that everyone is involved. When we have had to use someone who has not played a lot of games, they have helped us. The more players we have in a good place, the easier my selection will be, even if it is hard to leave players out.”

News.title: Burnham rules out calling early election
News.content:
Thanks for joining me. John Healey has promised to offer households “breathing space” in his maiden Budget today.

The Chancellor insisted the economy has shown “resilience” in the face of the energy shock from the Iran war.

However, he admitted the conflict has pushed up the cost of living, “piling pressure on the families, on businesses, and on our public finances”.

Among the measures the Chancellor is expected to announce are plans to scrap standing charges on household gas bills – saving families up to £50 a year.

Mr Healey said: “We can’t stop these shocks that hit Britain, but we can make Britain more resilient when they do.

“So, this Budget is designed to give households breathing space from some of the everyday costs, provide targeted support for businesses and self-employed people, and to start the long-term action needed to get energy costs down for good.” Here is what you need to know.

5 things to start your day

1) Healey prepares to slash household gas bills by £50 | Chancellor to scrap standing charges on gas bills and curb Energy Secretary’s power

2) Minimum wage rise will drive up food prices, Healey warned | Manufacturers say they are already struggling to cover soaring production costs

3) Poundland directors quit in stand-off over administration | Board members fear owner wants to steer retailer into insolvency

4) Google attacks UK over ‘unlawful’ AI plans | Search giant fights plans by competition regulator to force it to promote rivals

5) Netherlands to cut 25,000 civil service jobs in AI push | Police and defence will be exempt from plans to trim 15pc of government workforce in next decade

What happened overnight

Ahead of the Budget, oil prices rose after an attack on a refinery in Saudi Arabia, the world’s biggest crude exporter, which has renewed concerns around the risks to supply in the Middle East.

Brent crude was up 1.7pc to nearly $116 a barrel, maintaining inflationary pressure on the global economy. It traded around $70 before the start of the Iran war.

Meanwhile, Asia stocks rallied amid fresh enthusiasm about AI.

South Korea’s Kospi surged more than 6pc and was on track for its largest one-day gain since July, after chipmaker SK Hynix reported a more than seven-fold jump in quarterly profit and said it would return about $75 billion to shareholders this year.

The AI rally faces its next test when technology giants Alphabet and Microsoft report earnings after market close later today, with investors looking for evidence of returns that would justify the hefty cost of the AI build-out.

In Asia, MSCI’s broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan was up 1.7pc, with Japan’s Nikkei adding 1.1pc and ⁠China’s CSI300 blue-chip index climbing 0.7pc.

News.title: Government remains tight-lipped on aid spending in Autumn budget
News.content:
The government made no mention of plans to restore aid spending in the Autumn budget and is on track to miss its current aid commitment.

It had been rumoured that a Burnham government planned to reverse the overseas aid cuts made by Sir Keir Starmer, who reduced an already shrunken aid budget from 0.5 to 0.3 per cent of gross national income (GNI) in February 2025.

The current 0.3 per cent allocation is the lowest proportion of national income spent on aid since 1999.

It was expected the reversal would be drawn up as part of a wider shake-up of the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO) under Ed Miliband as foreign secretary, The Telegraph reported in September.

But there was no mention of any timeline for restoring Britain’s overseas development assistance to the legally enshrined 0.7 per cent of gross national income GNI target on Wednesday.

The UK is now also on track to miss its 0.3 per cent aid spending commitment, equivalent to £9.2 billion per year, following a failure to confirm any upwards adjustment to the UK aid budget to account for inflation.

The shortfall is estimated to fall at £410 million this year, an analysis from the Centre for Global Development (CGD) found.

Britain’s aid money is spent across the world in sectors like health, education, disaster relief, and helping to promote democracy.

Sports.title: Angry Everton vs Newcastle viewers claim Sky Sports commentators ‘stuck in cupboard’ as clash shown without presenters
Sports.content:
Next

FURIOUS fans hit out at Sky Sports’ coverage of Everton’s Carabao Cup win over Newcastle.

The Toffees notched a 3-1 victory over their Premier League rivals to book their place in the quarter-finals.



And the showdown was televised on Sky Sports Plus instead of the broadcaster’s usual football channels.

The decision resulted in there being no presenter, pundits or commentators at the Hill Dickinson Stadium.



But it did not go down well with those tuning in to see Everton – who were without Jack Grealish after a breach of club discipline – knock Newcastle out of the Carabao Cup.

Fans rushed onto social media to slam Sky Sports bigwigs for the controversial call.

One said: “Now we’re having to listen to two commentators stuck in a cupboard somewhere because Sky are too tight to send them to the game! Can barely hear the crowd.”

Another added: “So Sky Sports have the rights to show the Everton v Newcastle EFL Cup game but have chosen to hide it behind the red button whilst showing League Two highlights on their dedicated Sky Sports Football channel?! Bizarre!!!”

A third raged: “Am I a f***ing idiot? I’m on Sky Sports Plus, I’ve got the red button and there’s only the choice of f***ing tennis courts. Why’s Everton v Newcastle not on a normal channel?”

A fourth chimed in: “Sky Sports have two football channels, and they are not showing the Everton vs Newcastle game on either one and are instead hiding it behind Sky Sports Plus. Make it make sense.”

And a fifth claimed: “Cheap night for Sky with no presenters. Why couldn’t they get one ex-Everton and one ex-Newcastle? Player on to host.”

Everton – who have been handed a trip to giant-killing Fleetwood – put themselves in the driving seat thanks to goals from James Garner, Hayden Hackney and Thierno Barry.

Sports.title: Estevao receives major boost as Carlo Ancelotti calls Chelsea star up for Brazil squad after Xabi Alonso snub
Sports.content:
Next

ESTEVAO has received a major boost after being called up to the Brazil national team.

The Chelsea star received the call from boss Carlos Ancelotti less than 48 hours after his most recent snub by Xabi Alonso.



Estevao, 19, was left to rot on the bench as the Blues were dumped out of the Carabao Cup at Anfield.

The winger has played just 163 minutes this season under the former Bayer Leverkusen and Real Madrid manager.



The majority of his time on the pitch had come in the League Cup, which is why his snub for the Liverpool game came as such a shock.

But the lack of match action has not deterred Ancelotti from calling Estevao up for international duty.

The teenager will be in the Selecao squad for the friendly matches against Japan and Singapore in November.

Ancelotti, 67, has defended the selection of Estevao despite his lack of minutes this season.

Sports.title: Glazers ‘in Sir Jim Ratcliffe rift with Man Utd owners convinced Ineos chief couldn’t have engineered a worse situation’
Sports.content:
Next

THE GLAZERS are in the midst of a rift with Sir Jim Ratcliffe over the running of Manchester United, according to reports.

Ratcliffe completed his purchase for a minority stake in the Red Devils back in 2024 with the promise of running the sporting operation at the club while the much-maligned Glazer family stayed on as majority owners.



However, the Daily Mail claims the American family, which bought United in 2005 through a leveraged buyout putting debt against the club, are unhappy with the way Ratcliffe has managed the club.

A source is said to have told the outlet of the Ineos era at United: “It’s a travesty and not what they expected or were promised. They have never run the club this way.”



Another family source told ESPN Ratcliffe “couldn’t have masterminded a worse situation”.

United have hit new lows under Ineos, finishing a record-low 15th in the Premier League, being eliminated by League Two Grimsby in the Carabao Cup last season and currently going through their worst-ever start to the Prem season.



That being said, it had been coming for a while thanks to the club’s estranged owners.

Only the brilliance of Sir Alex Ferguson and former CEO David Gill kept the club together in the early Glazer years despite the asset stripping and lack of investment being plain to see.

The current situation is merely the product of years of negligence championed by the ownership that simply does not care about the club from far away in America.

Ratcliffe paid £1.5billion for his minority stake purchase of just over a quarter of the shares when the Glazers asked for £6bn to be bought outright.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

They retain control of any sale, with a possible scenario being Ineos being shunned entirely if a third party comes in to buy the club from the Glazers – though such a scenario is unlikely.

The current share price of United is £15.60, almost £10 less than the £25 per share Ratcliffe paid.

Ineos are cutting their losses in football after putting Lausanne-Sport up for sale and slashing their asking price for Nice amid a crumbling empire which seems long past its heyday.

Yet United are always an afterthought for the Glazers, who are NFL-mad and own the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

Well over £1bn has been drained out of Old Trafford and Carrington in the form of debt repayments and dividends to the owners.



Fan protests fall on deaf ears, except for in the aftermath of the Super League fallout, when fans broke into the stadium and invaded the pitch ahead of a clash with Liverpool that was ultimately suspended until a later date.

Ineos can say one thing the Glazers can’t, that they have actually invested money into the club.

That has come in the form of an upgraded Carrington training centre and drawing up plans for a new 100,000-seater stadium.

Although most fans say that doesn’t excuse the mountain of poor decisions made on the football front.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

That includes the appointment of five different managers – a sixth surely soon to come as well – botched transfers, the sacking of hundreds of club staff to cut costs and the controversial ticket touting operation.



Fans gave Ratcliffe’s Rat Pack more grace than they ever gave the Glazers – with protests even before the completion of that infamous takeover more than 20 years ago – but they are also now firmly in the sights of disgruntled and fed up fans.

Sports.title: ‘Sad and depressing’ – San Siro to be DEMOLISHED as AC Milan and Inter unveil 71,500-seater ‘washing machine’ stadium

FANS have been left divided after it was revealed that the iconic San Siro would be DEMOLISHED and replaced with a new stadium.

AC Milan and Inter Milan will be leaving their home of over 80 years for a state-of-the-art ground in 2031.



The two Serie A giants have revealed images of what the new Generali Stadium will look like.

The 71,500-seater stadium will be constructed just meters from the site of the existing San Siro.



This means that the much-loved football cathedral will be DEMOLISHED to make way.

The naming rights for the new ground have already been sold to Italian insurer Generali.

That 20-year deal is reportedly worth a staggering £540million.

The Milan-based clubs have released a video which has shown projections of the new ground.



Gone are the winding columns and the red girders that had become synonymous with the stadium.

Instead, the stadium will have a much more modern appearance with a double-curved roof and a concrete X-frame structure around it.

SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

The video has also shown that there could be a see-through tunnel to bring fans closer to the players before kick-off.

It also shows that the new stadium will be used for events other than football, such as concerts and fashion shows.

But the plans have left fans divided with many sad to know the historic San Siro will be demolished to make way for it.



One posted: “Another soulless bowl.”



A second wrote: “I’m glad I got to see the San Siro before they take it down.”

A third commented: “Sad and depressing.”

A fourth said: “There’s no way the historic San Siro is getting demolished, the games gone.”

A fifth argued: “Time to move on and it looks amazing.”



Another added: “Shame to see the San Siro go, but this new stadium looks great.”

Other fans honed in on the new stadium’s look.

One commented: “Tearing down the football ladder to build a 70,000-seat washing machine.”

Another meanwhile compared it to a lemon squeezer.



And a third fan posted: “Nice shopping mall. But for cheering on the team, where do we go?”

The San Siro will remain in use while the new stadium is constructed.

The new home of AC Milan and Inter was originally planned to hold 60,000 people but has now been revealed to be more.

The 71,500 seats will include 13,000 premium seats as well as other modern amenities.

It will be the fifth-largest stadium in Europe after it is finished being built.

Sports.title: How Arsenal’s ghost runners will HAUNT Virgil van Dijk in Halloween clash at Liverpool
Sports.content:

ARSENAL head to Anfield this Halloween weekend looking to banish their Merseyside demons.

The defending Premier League champions haven’t won away at Liverpool in a whopping 14 YEARS.



A win at Anfield could put Mikel Arteta‘s troops top of the table for the FIRST TIME this season.

But they’ll face a massive test against the well-drilled Reds, who dumped Chelsea out of the Carabao Cup earlier this week.



And ahead of Sunday’s mouthwatering showdown, SunSport’s tactical guru Dean Scoggins is on hand to break down how the north Londoners can leave Merseyside with all three points in the latest episode of our hit show, ‘Tactics Exposed‘.

Target Van Dijk

This one might surprise you because what I actually want to say with Arsenal is target Virgil van Dijk.

I know he’s world-class, but actually, I think you can expose Liverpool by giving him too much to do.

When they’re in much more of a mid shape, where they get more in a transitional phase of play, this is where they have a problem.

What happens is [Milos] Kerkez gets dragged across one way, teams have been pinning [Jeremy] Jacquet over here, and that leaves Van Dijk with far too much to do.

Which way does he go? Does he stay close to his centre-back, or does he go out to his left-back?



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

You open up gates for teams to run through.

Kerkez is obviously a more attacking option on that side, but that gives that right-hand space for Arsenal to target.

A ball goes inside, and then you’ve got a runner off the back of Mac Allister.



Now think Declan Rice here, Arsenal fans. Think [Martin] Odegaard; think runners running off the ball in behind.

Those ghost runners will be what Arsenal are trying to target. Go for it, Declan Rice.

They can really hurt Liverpool and catch them in that sort of transitional phase.

Battle of the playmakers: Odegaard vs Wirtz

The flow state that Odegaard is in at the moment, he’s ticking and it’s lovely.

Confidence is high; he’s setting the tempo. He’s the press setter and he just lends the ball to others before getting it back.



Here is where I think Odegaard can really target a little weakness of Liverpool.

He has come off a defender who doesn’t want to jump out of this back line to come and receive the ball.

Because they’re man-v-man in midfield, that’s where the space is. That’s where you can turn and get at Liverpool.

If the ball is in an outside area, then you’re targeting those underlap runs when you’ve opened up the centre-back corridor. That is absolutely where Martin Odegaard will target.



Barcola vs Calafiori

To play as a winger in this [Andoni Iraola’s] system, you have to work your cojones off.

[Bradley] Barcola has actually done that quite well this season.

But he’s working so hard going that way back into a defensive position that it takes away from him affecting the game a little bit more.

You’re going to look at a scenario where it’s going to be Barcola against Calafiori.



Barcola is going to have to work very, very hard going back.

Calafiori likes to get into that area, so we’ve got a race between those two guys to be the extra man that supports the winger and overloading the defender.

All that in the background of a man up front in Alexander Isak, who is going to really cause problems and peel off onto a centre-back.

It is not going to be easy for Arsenal.

However, I do think with Declan Rice and deep runners coming off the back of Mac Allister and Gravenberch, Arsenal can go away and get their first win at Anfield since 2012.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick acting as if its business as usual amid Man Utd sack threat – with Jason Wilcox far from safe either
Sports.content:
Next

TO LISTEN to Michael Carrick, you would think the circus surrounding Manchester United had packed up and left town.

The Red Devils’ under-fire boss carried himself in his press conference to preview the trip to Chelsea as if it were business as usual, apparently not living on a game-by-game basis, and his job was not on the line.



While debate rages about his future, Carrick, 45, desperately holds on to an illusion of calm, acting as though it were all quiet on the Old Trafford front.

The former United midfielder said he always expected the board’s backing this week despite Sunday’s 3-0 thrashing by Bournemouth leaving the team 16th in the Premier League and only a point above the relegation zone.



But with that coming days just after the 4-1 Champions League humbling in Como, the rest of us were primed for his P45.

He now seems like an interim manager again, on a zero-hours contract.



For Carrick, this was a waking nightmare of deja vu.

Facing another round of journalists and Amazon cameras, he was asked for the third time in a week about his job.

Couple that with more questions on his spiky relationship with rebellious captain Bruno Fernandes and how the pair have apparently made up.

Quizzed on the growing pressure, Carrick said: “I don’t really see it. I see the things that I need to see. I don’t look for it. It doesn’t really help in any way.”



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Clearly, midfielder Fernandes’ one-match exile is over after he called out Carrick’s tactics in Italy last Wednesday — and now the manager must deliver wins.

Carrick appeared to embark on a farewell lap of Old Trafford at full-time, as the Stretford End cheered him before unleashing blood-letting boos at the players once their teary-eyed manager was out of sight down the tunnel.

The owners and board also brutally copped it throughout the dismal game.

Carrick admitted: “The reception drew mixed feelings. My responsibility is to the players. Outside is not for me to focus on.

“I know what help the group needs, guidance at certain times and dealing with things, that’s part of my direct role. We have held a meeting, we’ve spoken.



“The boys are hungry. We’re hurting because we haven’t won enough football games. But there is an intensity, an edge, a hunger to do better.”

We are yet to see any intensity from United and failure to beat Chelsea will stretch the team’s winless run to NINE matches and could plunge the crisis club into the relegation zone.

The Red Devils are two points above basement side Sunderland, level on points with Crystal Palace and just one point ahead of Nottingham Forest and Coventry.



Despite 13 years of chaos and seven different managers, United have somehow suffered their worst league start in 40 years, with their sole league victory coming against new boys Ipswich in August.

Overall, it has been six defeats in 12 games in all competitions, 22 goals shipped and no sign of another win since they beat Euro minnows Sabah 49 DAYS ago.

Co-owners Sir Jim Ratcliffe, Avram Glazer and Joel Glazer held a conference call on Monday with chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox to weigh up their options as fans express their frustrations.

United are not yet sold on ex-Newcastle boss Eddie Howe, 48, or 39-year-old former Germany manager Julian Nagelsmann.

Boardroom figures are also mindful that the international break after home matches against Roma in the Champions League on Tuesday and Aston Villa five days later offers a natural, cleaner window for a new manager to take charge.



Public enemy No1 Wilcox’s future has also come under intense scrutiny.

It feels inevitable the former Leeds and Blackburn winger, 55, will eventually lose his job if a third managerial change in as many seasons occurs under his watch.

Externally, the drama has focused on recruitment — or lack of it, specifically at left-back and up front — United’s finances and massive debt levels, Carrick’s relative inexperience and, other than assistant boss Steve Holland, that of his coaches.



Carrick confirmed United’s only natural striker Benjamin Sesko would be out until New Year with a shin injury picked up last term.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

In a bid to clear the air, Carrick called a squad and staff summit — with no directors invited — to ensure everyone was singing from the same hymn sheet.

A private meeting with out-of-sorts skipper Fernandes, 32, was said to be productive but Carrick urgently needs his reigning Prem Player of the Season to step up and deliver if he is to keep his job.

Karl Vilips used two long birdie streaks to take the first-round lead Thursday in the Mexico Open, the first of two straight PGA Tour events in the country.

Vilips shot a nine-under 62 in the afternoon round on the Vidanta Vallarta layout, making five straight birdies on Nos. 11-15 on his opening nine and finishing with four in a row. In between, he had another birdie and a bogey.

The 25-year-old Australian pointed to his driver.

"Had it on a string for the first nine," Vilips said. "Got a little loose in the middle and got it back on course toward the end of the round. It was lift, clean and place today so being in the fairway was a must for me and I took advantage of those drives that I hit."

Alvaro Ortiz of Mexico opened with a 65. He earned his PGA Tour card for next year through the Korn Ferry Tour.

"It was lovely," Ortiz said. "Bogey-free, played really solid. I felt like I was just flowing the whole day. Gave myself a lot of chances. I think I did very well from tee to green, which makes it very nice on this golf course."

Ortiz won the event in 2021 when it was part of the PGA Tour Latinoamerica schedule. The World Wide Technology Championship is next week at El Cardonal at Diamante in Los Cabos.

Vilips won the 2025 Puerto Rico Open for his lone PGA Tour title, making him exempt on the tour through next season.

Sports.title: Love leads Packers past Panthers in vital win
Sports.content:
Jordan Love threw three touchdown passes, Josh Jacobs scored twice and the Green Bay Packers withstood three turnovers and the Carolina Panthers' late comeback attempt to win 27-19 at Lambeau Field.

Love went 30 of 41 for 288 yards with touchdown passes to Tucker Kraft, Matthew Golden and Jacobs plus an interception. Although Jacobs rushed for only 39 yards on 21 carries against the NFL's lowest-ranked run defense, he scored on a 4-yard catch and 1-yard run.

That was more than enough for the Packers on a night when they sacked Bryce Young six times. Green Bay hasn't allowed any of its last five opponents to exceed 20 points.

Image: The Packers beat the Panthers 27-19

"This defense is really special," safety Javon Bullard said.

Trailing 27-10 in the third quarter, Carolina cut Green Bay's lead to 27-19 on Young's 26-yard touchdown pass to Jalen Coker on a fourth-and-three play with 5:37 remaining. Young's ensuing 2-point conversion pass was incomplete.

"Late in the game, it wasn't good enough," Love said. "We weren't able to finish the way we wanted. That's something we've got to improve on, clean up as an offense and be better there."

The Panthers (3-4) got the ball back at their own 45 before losing the ball on downs at midfield with 2:41 remaining. Carolina got one last chance from its own 20 with 22 seconds and no timeouts remaining, but Dani Dennis-Sutton's sack essentially ended any comeback hopes.

Image: Carolina Panthers wide receiver Coker (18) scores a touchdown over Green Bay Packers linebacker McDuffie

Young went 23 of 41 for 209 yards with one touchdown and one interception. Carolina's Chuba Hubbard had 22 carries for 81 yards and a touchdown and seven catches for 38 yards.

Green Bay's Christian Watson returned to the game after hurting his chest while making a 53-yard catch in the second quarter, causing him to be taken to the hospital. Carolina cornerback Will Lee hurt his hamstring while diving to make a tackle on the same play, and he got carted into the locker room.

Watson said he got clearance to return to the game after a CT scan didn't show any internal bleeding. Watson did say he broke a rib on the play.

"I felt like I was watching 'WWE Smackdown vs. Raw' or something, seeing the cameras on me when I was coming out of the ambulance," said Watson, who caught eight passes for 113 yards. "That was a little crazy. It was a surreal experience, no doubt."

Image: Golden (0) runs after the catch

After fumbling the opening kickoff to set up a Carolina field goal and going three-and-out on their first series, the Packers (5-3) scored touchdowns on three of their next four possessions to take command.

Love threw a 12-yard touchdown pass across the middle to Kraft on a third-and-8 play to put Green Bay ahead 6-3, as struggling rookie Trey Smack's extra-point attempt bounced off the left upright.

Image: Green Bay running back Jacobs scored two touchdowns

Watson's 53-yard catch set up a Jacobs touchdown run that put Green Bay ahead for good, 13-10 early in the second quarter. One play after dropping a potential touchdown pass, Golden caught a 24-yarder in the left corner of the end zone on third-and-13 to make it 20-10.

Carolina got the ball to start the second half, but Chris McClellan and Evan Williams stopped Hubbard a yard short on fourth-and-two from midfield. On Green Bay's ensuing drive, Love found Jacobs to extend the lead to 27-10.

Green Bay led 27-13 and had the ball on Carolina's 28 in the opening minute of the fourth quarter when Love threw a pass to Golden that Zakee Wheatley intercepted in the end zone.

That turnover sparked Carolina's comeback attempt, but the Panthers ultimately couldn't break through against Green Bay's defense.

"I said at the beginning of the year, and I still feel this way: I think the sky is the limit for this defense," Packers linebacker Isaiah McDuffie said.

The Packers - while 5-3 - still sit bottom of the NFC North, the NFL's strongest division, while the Panthers remain atop the NFC South even with a negative record on the season.

Sports.title: 'I'm built differently' - Hamilton defiant over extending F1 career into 2030s
Sports.content:
Lewis Hamilton insisted he "is built differently" as he continued to rule out extending his Formula 1 career into the 2030s.

Following the announcement earlier in October that Africa will return to the F1 calendar at some point in the 2030s with a race in Rwanda, Hamilton had said he hoped he would be able to compete in the first grand prix on the continent since 1993.

Given Hamilton turns 42 in January and will be 45 at the start of the 2030 F1 season, at which point it is far from certain the circuit in Rwanda will be ready, it was initially unclear how seriously his comments should be taken.

But quizzed on the topic on Thursday ahead of this weekend's Mexico City Grand Prix, the seven-time world champion said: "I mean, firstly, you've never had anyone like me here in the 70 years [of the sport's history], so I feel that I'm built differently.

"Of course, there are challenges up ahead that I can't foresee that come with age. But along this way, along this journey, there have been so many preconceived ideas about the fact that your reaction time drops off.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Craig Slater reports that Formula 1 will return to Africa for the first time since 1993, with a brand-new Rwandan circuit set to host a Grand Prix from the early 2030s

"Did you see my reaction in the last race? My reaction is faster than some of the youngest people here. There are lots of tools that you can utilise to continue to keep yourself, your mind sharp.

"I guess as long as you're willing to sacrifice everything, which I am right now, I can't say in four years whether I want to continue to do what I'm doing. But I love what I'm doing still now. I'm still all in, and I will be for the foreseeable future."

Hamilton's current contract with Ferrari is understood to run until the end of the 2027 season, with the Brit holding an option to extend for a further year should he wish to do so.

After a blockbuster move from Mercedes to Ferrari for the 2025 season, Hamilton's performances during his first year in red raised doubts, at times from the driver himself himself, over whether his skills were declining, but he has bounced back with a much-improved 2026 campaign, which included a memorable victory in Barcelona.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player With Kimi Antonelli set to win the title this weekend in Mexico City, we look back at Hamilton’s dramatic 2017 title triumph, when he recovered to finish P9 after an opening-lap clash involving Max Verstappen and Sebastian Vettel

Hamilton continued: "Whether or not I can compete at 44 with a 20-year-old, who knows? But at 41, I can compete with a 20-year-old. So, time will tell whether I'm here in the 2030s, we'll see.

"But I never want to overstay my welcome in the sense of still not having the performance. I don't want to be driving around with that really dropped off.

"My reaction has dropped off, my driving has dropped off, and my pace has dropped off, which everyone assumed last year. But I've proved everyone wrong with that, and I'll continue to try to do so."

Hamilton's focus on Constructors', not Drivers' Championship

While Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli is set to seal the Drivers' Championship this weekend with four races to spare, Hamilton is part of an extremely tight four-way battle for second place in the standings.

Antonelli's team-mate George Russell is in second, a point ahead of Hamilton, with Red Bull's Max Verstappen five points further back and the other Ferrari of Charles Leclerc three more points adrift.

Hamilton insists his focus is on ensuring Ferrari seal second in the Constructors' Championship, in which they hold a 119-point over Red Bull and McLaren, with Mercedes 133 points clear out front.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Ferrari's Hamilton claimed his first win in red at the Barcelona-Catalunya Grand Prix

"I'm not going to say it [second in the Drivers' Championship] doesn't mean anything, but it's not something I focus on," Hamilton said. "Winning the championship is the only thing any of us really care about.

"Maybe some people do care about the other positions, but for me, my sole focus is on making sure that we secure second in the Constructors' Championship because the team deserve it.

"It's a huge boost from last year and it really is something we can build on for next year.

"In terms of finishing second, third, fourth, you want to finish first."

'The car should be good here'

Hamilton is hopeful Ferrari can deliver a strong weekend in Mexico, where many believe the turbo element of their engine, which is smaller than their rivals', could be an advantage at high altitude.

Asked about Ferrari's chances, Hamilton said: "Someone just said that it should be good for our car, and I really have no idea.

"I mean, everyone's going to be maximum downforce here. It would be an unusual experience for us all, because it's like 25 or 30 per cent less downforce than we had the last time we drove here.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Speaking on F1 Show podcast, Ant Davidson explains why Ferrari could be dominant this weekend at the Mexico City Grand Prix

"So, whether we can get the tyres switched on... the car should be good here.

"And being that we have high altitude, hopefully straight-line speed won't be as affected as it is in some of the other places where at sea level the drag is significant.

"So, I'm hoping that we are able to continue on from the strong performance we had last year and bring it into this weekend."

Sports.content:
Chris Dobey clinched his third ranking title of the season as he beat Tommy Morris 8-4 at Players Championship 32 on Thursday.

Sports.title: Russell: 2026 F1 season won't break me
Sports.content:
George Russell insists this year's Formula 1 season "won't break me" as Kimi Antonelli is set to become world champion this weekend in Mexico.

A top nine finish for Antonelli, or Russell or Lewis Hamilton failing to win Sunday's Mexico City Grand Prix, would secure the title for the Italian, who would be the youngest champion in F1 history at 20 years old.

Russell came into 2026 as favourite after dominating Antonelli last year but has won just three races to his team-mate's nine, regularly being outperformed throughout the season.

"I've probably learned more about myself this year than I would have liked to in all honesty. The highs and lows you go through in sport are immense. That's because we all care so much for what we're doing," said Russell.

"I remind myself I'm 28 years old. I see Lewis still competing extremely well at 41 and Fernando at 44. Lewis won the majority of his titles in his 30s.

"This year is absolutely not going to define my career as a whole. It's not going to break me. If anything, it's going to make me stronger."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Take a look at our picks of the pivotal moments that defined the F1 season, as Kimi Antonelli looks to secure the 2026 World Drivers' Championship in Mexico

Russell pointed to an unusual trend where he's generally bounced back strongly from poor weekends or misfortune, including an underwhelming race in Madrid where Antonelli won, before a dominant performance on his way to pole and victory at the next race in Baku.

"I've been pretty proud of my resilience and how I've bounced back from very tough moments," he explained.

"Actually through my lowest points of this season, I've generally bounced back really, really strong then I had another bad race, after the good one, so maybe it's something I need to analyse as well because I always perform best after my worst races, which is maybe just a coincidence, maybe there's something in it.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player George Russell crashes out shortly taking the lead at the Singapore Grand Prix Sprint

"I've been racing more years of my life than I haven't. I've had more successful years than relative failures, and I don't think any athlete, no matter how great, has every single year of their career performing at their highest level.

"Unfortunately, this year for me has come at maybe the time when I needed it most. But it's by no means the end of my journey. I've still got a good 12 to 15 years left in me."

Russell: Antonelli has been at a higher level than me

Antonelli's title-winning campaign is a big surprise after his challenging rookie season in 2025 as he has completely turned the tables in the Mercedes head-to-head battle.

Russell finished eighth last time out in Austin while Antonelli won and the British driver says "it's important to find some consistency" and admits his team-mate has been getting more out of the car.

"On a personal level, Kimi is obviously a great guy with lots of energy. We've had no reason this year not to continue a good relationship," he said.

"I think a lot of these rivalries start because of on-track incidents or actions. The truth is he's been at a higher level than me this year, so we've not really been in that situation too often.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Toto Wolff hits back at accusations that Mercedes favour Kimi Antonelli over George Russell

"We've had one or two races, and when it comes to the race itself, we sort of keep ourselves to ourselves and work with our individual engineers to try and get the most out of it."

Antonelli missed Thursday's media day at the Mexico City Grand Prix due to a viral illness but is expected to be fit enough to drive in Friday's practice sessions.

He told Sky Sports F1 in Austin: "The perfect way would be to finish off in style and enjoy the rest of the season.

"I'm very well aware it's very close but the mindset hasn't changed. I want to finish the season on a high in order to have high hopes in 2027.

"First we focus and worry about finishing this [season] well and we will see."

Sports.title: Everton see off Newcastle to reach Carabao Cup quarter-finals
Sports.content:
Everton are through to the quarter-finals of the Carabao Cup after seeing off Newcastle 3-1.

James Garner, Hayden Hackney and Thierno Barry were all on the scoresheet at the Hill Dickinson Stadium on Thursday night. Dan Burn netted a late consolation for Newcastle.

The Toffees will head to Fleetwood Town in the last eight in December, after the League Two side's epic win over Arsenal earlier in the week.

It provides Everton with a real opportunity of reaching a first cup semi-final since 2016.

Grealish dropped due to disciplanary breach Everton announced before the game that Jack Grealish had been dropped due to a disciplinary breach. It was reporter that the Man City loanee had missed a training session earlier in the week.

The hosts found the lead from nothing on 34 minutes. Tyrique George's pressure saw Amar Dedic lose the ball on the sidelines. Hackney then flicked the ball into Garner, who finessed a shot into the bottom corner.

On the stroke of half-time it was 2-0. Hackney turned scorer this time as he guided home from Barry's cross, to claim his first goal for the club.

And then it was Barry's time on 69 minutes, finishing up a clinical counter-attack with some fine movement and a cool finish after picking up Kieran Dewsbury-Hall's pass.

Burn headed in late on for Newcastle, but it was too little, too late.

The key moments from the Hill Dickinson Stadium

12: CHANCE! Gonzalez picks out the smart run of Barnes down the left. The winger ghosts in behind Rohl to head towards goal but he draws a save from Pickford instead.

34: GOAL! Garner applies some finesse on his finish to put Everton ahead. It comes from nothing. Dedic loses it near the corner flag, under pressure from George. Hackney finds Garner with a neat pass and the Everton midfielder curls home.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player James Garner scores the opening goal in Everton's League Cup clash against Newcastle

45: GOAL! HACKNEY GUIDES HOME HIS FIRST EVERTON GOAL! It all starts from a Newcastle opportunity. Barnes' effort takes a nick, and Pickford gathers before starting an Everton counter. Dewsbury-Hall leads the charge forward before being taken out. Advantage is played and Barry keeps going, taking the ball wide before digging out a cross for Hackney to see home.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Hayden Hackney scores his first Everton goal to put Toffees 2-0 up in their League Cup clash with Newcastle

69: GOAL! NEWCASTLE ARE SLICED OPEN BY EVERTON. Garner carries the ball up the field and feeds Dewsbury-Hall. He continues the charge down the left, pulling back a cross into the area. Barry has all the time in the world in the Newcastle box to compose himself and fire into the top corner.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Thierno Barry scores Everton's third goal ahead slick counter attack

89: GOAL! Burn heads in to give his side a consolation. Willock swings a ball into the area and Burn, high up the field, beats O'Brien to the ball. Burn is then booked, along with Joelinton and Tarkowski for some pushing and shoving after the goal.

Jaissle calls for maturity as he laments 'story of the season' in cup defeat

Newcastle head coach Matthias Jaissle called on his side to show greater maturity after their defeat to Everton, describing the result as a reflection of the "story of the season so far".

"We lack in the clinical approach to solve the situations; just think about the first one," Jaissle said.

Newcastle United

Everton Monday 2nd November 6:30pm Kick off 8:00pm

"This is again a no-risk zone where we clear the ball and nothing happens, and a couple of seconds later you can see the goal out of nothing.

"These are the things we need to learn quickly. We had many occasions, many opportunities to score, big chances as well, but in their box we need to be more clinical to get a different result."

Jaissle insisted Newcastle's overall performance was not as poor as the scoreline suggested, but acknowledged their individual mistakes had proved costly.

"We need to avoid these mistakes, be more mature, be more clinical in these situations," he added.

"This is a learning process, but you don't get the time. We need to learn fast, especially with these young lads. Being a young team is not an excuse any more."

Moyes praises Everton's values as players put Grealish absence to one side

David Moyes praised Everton's squad values and professionalism after they put the Jack Grealish situation to one side to reach the Carabao Cup quarter-finals.

Grealish was left out after reportedly missing a training session, with Moyes describing his absence as a club decision.

Asked whether he was pleased with his players' professionalism, Moyes said: "The one thing about Everton and what they've got is they've got really good values behind it.

"All the players stand up to the values, accept the values Everton put out there, what we want from them on the pitch and off the pitch, and from that point of view, the players done a brilliant job tonight.

"It's a smallish squad we've got, and we're limited in some areas. But we're doing our best to try and keep challenging."

Sports.title: Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekend
Sports.content:
1

Michael Carrick and Bruno Fernandes held clear-the-air talks this week. Fernandes was an unused substitute against Bournemouth after criticising Carrick’s tactics during the Champions League defeat by Como but it seems the situation has been resolved – for now. Dropping Fernandes did not do United any good against Bournemouth, who ran riot at Old Trafford, and the captain is expected to return to the starting lineup for the trip to Chelsea. If that happens, he owes Carrick a performance. Fernandes has been poor this season and it is time he did his talking on the pitch. Jacob Steinberg

Chelsea v Manchester United, Saturday 12.30pm (all times GMT)

2 Maresca wary of another City slip

Since Manchester City were found guilty of serially breaching Premier League financial rules, Enzo Maresca’s team have won four games (including Wednesday’s Carabao Cup shootout victory over Brighton) and lost two. Saturday’s 2-1 reverse at Aston Villa was their first Premier League defeat and should another follow in their rematch with the Seagulls, the manager may start to fear the guilty verdict and possible sanction (demotion to the Championship, for example) may become a distraction to his players. There is a precedent for City initially responding well to adversity, before it then affected results. After Rodri sustained a serious knee injury against Arsenal in September 2024, Pep Guardiola’s team went undefeated in seven matches, winning six. But then the wheels clattered off, with one victory and 10 defeats in the next 13. Jamie Jackson

Manchester City v Brighton, Saturday 3pm

View image in fullscreen Manchester City and Brighton meet again on Saturday after an entertaining Carabao Cup contest in midweek. Photograph: Gary Oakley/Every Second Media/Shutterstock

3 Hamer keen for Coventry chance

The last time north-east opposition visited the CBS Arena, Frank Lampard’s side had no trouble finding the net, but their four goals against Newcastle on 12 October make up two-thirds of their league total for the season. Perhaps the most creative player at the club has spent most of this campaign watching from the bench. Gustavo Hamer, who created 12 goals for his Sheffield United teammates in the Championship last season, has asked to play for the under-21s to get his minutes up. “Myself and the staff have been really, really impressed by his approach, his training, his ethic,” Lampard said before Hamer came on as an 86th-minute substitute in last weekend’s defeat by Fulham. Will he get more than four minutes off the bench against the only team beneath Coventry in the table? Billy Munday

Coventry v Sunderland, Saturday 3pm

4 Evanilson’s value clear for Bournemouth

Beating Milan and then Manchester United made for a halcyon week in Bournemouth’s history. Winning at Old Trafford and defeating Aston Villa in the Carabao Cup on Wednesday all followed Marco Rose’s first Premier League win, against Sunderland on 18 October, which came as a great relief. The project is back on course. Eli Junior Kroupi, a late substitute last Sunday, has returned to the squad. In the Frenchman’s absence Evanilson has been on his best run of form since joining the club. He has four goals from five matches, and a tight-angled finish to make it 3-0 at United belied his reputation as a player who could score more. The Brazilian is a capable line leader, with Kroupi able to work the space his partner’s tireless running creates. When Sturm Graz were defeated in the Europa League, Evanilson served as support striker for the raw Álvaro Rodríguez. There is little starry about a club-record signing whose work ethic has been important to Rose’s early weeks in charge. John Brewin

Bournemouth v Leeds, Saturday 3pm

5 Forest still searching for finishing touch

Brentford’s early-season charge has slowed. No wins from their last three, and a disappointing draw at Hull last week – although only Liverpool have beaten Keith Andrews’ team this season in the Premier League. A 1-1 draw at Ipswich last Friday heightened frustrations at Nottingham Forest, Liam Delap’s scoring touch continuing to desert him, an unmarked Murillo missing a free header the best of a host of unconverted chances. The better opportunities tended to arrive from the flanks, with Daniel Muñoz overlapping from wing-back as the supplier for Neco Williams’ goal. After a decent start to the season for Morgan Gibbs-White in terms of chance creation, he was crowded out by Ipswich’s packed midfield. Oliver Glasner’s formation, founded on a defensive trio, seeks to bring the best from playmakers and ball-players. It brought results from Eberechi Eze and Adam Wharton at Crystal Palace but Gibbs-White and Forest are yet to prosper. Better finishing would certainly help a team stuck in the bottom three. JB

Brentford v Nottingham Forest, Saturday 3pm

6 Promoted rivals are sitting comfortably

Two promoted teams and two positive managers meet at MKM Stadium on Saturday. “There will be ups and downs, this is normal,” said Hull’s Sergej Jakirovic last week. “We showed already that we can compete.” Ipswich’s Gary O’Neil is similarly enthusiastic: “They’re an incredible group,” he said of his players this week. “We’re not carrying anybody in that, there’s no one getting dragged along by this group.” Both teams kick off in mid-table, though with the awareness of the importance of defeating an opponent with similar ambitions. While other Championship graduates have been too readily accepting of their fate, both have grasped the nettle and shown off their survival instincts. Manchester City’s potential punishment could create an opportunity, leaving just two relegation spots to avoid. Hull’s initial hot streak has cooled, though last week’s draw with Brentford was useful. Against Forest, Ipswich made up for their lack of fluidity by showing the staying power to claim a point. JB

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Hull v Ipswich, Saturday 3pm

7 Tottenham’s Tel keen to ‘work, work, work’

Despite landing in the Premier League in January last year, Mathys Tel’s goal against Chelsea felt like an arrival of sorts. The 21-year-old was highly rated as a youngster at Bayern Munich but has found the net just seven times in 50 league games since joining Spurs, initially on loan. Against Chelsea he picked the ball up in his own half and drove forwards 40 yards before finding the bottom corner from the edge of the box. Spurs fans will want more from Tel who, unlike many of his teammates, is rarely injured. “I think I can still do better,” he said after the 2-0 win at Chelsea that made it two on the spin for Spurs. “I can always do better. I need to work, work, work, work.” Crystal Palace come off the back of victory over Fulham in the Carabao Cup – the head coach, Pierre Sage, has been backed by the board after a tricky spell in the league. BM

Tottenham v Crystal Palace, Saturday 5.30pm

View image in fullscreen Mathys Tel enjoyed a breakthrough moment for Spurs with his solo goal at Stamford Bridge. Photograph: Shaun Brooks/CameraSport/Getty Images

8 Jackson offers striking blueprint for García

Álvaro Arbeloa is at last getting somewhere with Fulham. After going without a win in his first six league matches, the Spaniard has collected six points against Hull and Coventry. Goals remain in short supply, though, and the form of the £40m striker Gonzalo García – seven games without scoring – is concerning. Arbeloa’s past relationship with García at Real Madrid is not proving as beneficial as Unai Emery’s knowledge of Nicolas Jackson’s game. That pair worked together at Villarreal, where Emery gave Jackson his La Liga debut. “Unai taught me everything about football,” Jackson said on signing from Chelsea in the summer. With four goals in five Premier League games, including a double against Manchester City last Saturday, Jackson is one of the form strikers in the country. “He was shooting a lot of balls over the crossbar,” Emery said. “Now he’s getting better.” BM

Aston Villa v Fulham, Saturday 8pm

9 Iraola’s Liverpool side look four-midable

“Let’s try to finish this four-in-a-row in the best way,” said Andoni Iraola on Wednesday as thoughts turned from the Carabao Cup penalty shootout win over Chelsea to Arsenal’s impending visit to Anfield. Three consecutive home wins in different competitions, and in quick succession, have helped build momentum at Liverpool, although seven wins from the last eight (including Chelsea) shows the process had already begun. Iraola has handled his first intensive run of Champions League, Premier League and Carabao Cup fixtures expertly, rotating in every game while continuing to produce results. Noticeably, there has been no drop-off in Liverpool’s physical intensity either. The manner of Arsenal’s title triumph last season – and the general shift towards more aggressive, urgent football in the Premier League – were factors in Liverpool’s decision to change head coaches in the summer, and the results are paying off quickly. Iraola will be facing questions about a title challenge should four-in-a-row finish as he hopes on Sunday. Andy Hunter

Liverpool v Arsenal, Sunday 4.30pm

View image in fullscreen Andoni Iraola’s Liverpool side have won their last five games in all competitions, including Wednesday’s penalty shootout win over Chelsea. Photograph: Ryan Browne/Shutterstock

10 Pickford out to frustrate Newcastle again

David Moyes described it as “out of this world”, Alan Shearer talked about a world-class intervention, and Jordan Pickford agreed it ranked as “up there with my very best.” Rewind to March and Everton are beating Newcastle 3-2 on Tyneside when, in the 94th minute, Sandro Tonali unleashes a vicious and technically perfect volley. To the astonishment of everyone inside St James’ Park, Everton’s goalkeeper throws out his right hand and tips the ball over the crossbar. Pickford’s teammate Jarrad Branthwaite said it was “the best save I’ve ever seen” and Moyes can only hope his England goalkeeper proves in similarly defiant mood at a time when his international place is under a little pressure from the Leeds goalkeeper, James Trafford. Not that Pickford will lack inspiration; the lifelong Sunderland fan always enjoys frustrating Newcastle, as he did again in Thursday’s Carabao Cup victory. Matthias Jaissle’s team, and their midfield, are still adapting to life after Tonali and face a testing rematch at St James’ Park on Monday. Louise Taylor

Sports.title: Everton ease past Newcastle to set up Fleetwood trip after Grealish is dropped
Sports.content:
The biggest night in Everton’s season started with a big call from David Moyes and demanded a big performance from his players. With the exception of Jack Grealish, they did not let him down. A quarter-final at Fleetwood Town is their prize after a clinical, committed display shattered Newcastle’s hopes of lifting the Carabao Cup for a second time in three seasons.

Newcastle dominated spells of the fourth round tie and the stats – registering 28 shots to Everton’s 11, although only nine visiting attempts were on target – but individual defensive errors and an ineffective attack proved a ruinous combination. Matthias Jaissle denied his team are a soft touch, despite persuasive evidence to the contrary, yet called Newcastle “naive” and the defeat, in front of almost 8,000 of their fans, “shocking”. Andy Burnham was among the many Evertonians in attendance grateful for Newcastle’s generosity.

James Garner, with his first goal of the season, Hayden Hackney, with his first goal for the club, and Thierno Barry were on target to take Everton into the last eight of a competition they have never won. Jordan Pickford was in commanding form against his old adversaries while Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall ran the show from midfield. But it was the absent Grealish who dominated the buildup after Everton announced he had been dropped for disciplinary reasons.

Grealish is understood to have missed training on Monday without permission. Despite the importance of the fixture and the limited options at his disposal, and the playmaker’s subsequent return to training, Moyes demonstrated that no player is bigger than the club by banishing the 31-year-old from the game. The Everton manager later claimed it was “a club decision” but it was taken by him and the chief executive, Angus Kinnear. Ultimately, and no doubt to Grealish’s great relief, he was not missed.

Newcastle dominated the opening 20 minutes to the extent that a two-goal interval lead for Everton would have seemed inconceivable. Pickford saved an early header from Harvey Barnes, who then turned provider to set up Jacob Ramsey for a shot that was blocked superbly by Vitalii Mykolenko. Fabian Schär also tested Pickford from distance, leaving the England international raging at the lack of protection in front of him. He could not fault his defenders’ willingness to put their bodies on the line, however.

View image in fullscreen Hayden Hackney scores Everton’s second goal against Newcastle. Photograph: Aidan Hunter/Action Plus/Shutterstock

Everton gradually turned the contest around. Putting an end to ineffective long balls up to Barry, when he was marked by Dan Burn, helped their cause, although it was a long clearance from Pickford that led to the breakthrough. Amar Dedic looked to retrieve the goalkeeper’s punt but was harried out of possession by Tyrique George. The ball broke to Hackney, who squared inside for Garner to find the far corner of Lukas Hornicek’s goal. “The first goal, it’s no risk, clear it,” said a dismayed Jaissle. “But we concede out of nothing. The first, second and third goals were the same with individual mistakes. We need to be more efficient and learn fast.”

Pickford came in for his customary Sunderland stick from the Newcastle support. He responded in the best way possible; with a hand in a second goal that deflated the sizeable away section. The Everton keeper reacted sharply to launch a quick throw towards Dewsbury-Hall in the centre circle. Dewsbury-Hall spun away from Burn before embarking on a determined run that was halted by a trip from behind by Ramsey. The referee, Farai Hallam, played an excellent advantage as the ball broke to Barry. Newcastle appeared to pause, waiting for the free-kick, and were punished when Barry clipped over a cross for Hackney to volley home from close range.

A triple half-time substitution from Jaissle was an unmistakable sign of discontent with Newcastle’s ineffective display at both ends of the pitch.

There was more menace from the visitors in the second half with the substitute Yoane Wissa having an early chance from Joe Willock’s chip and Dedic’s shot looping over off Hackney’s heel. But with Pickford standing firm and saving smartly from Lewis Hall, Anthony Elanga and Ramsey, and Wissa almost hitting the corner flag with one decent chance, Newcastle’s failure to make their pressure count continued.

The visitors were punished when Everton made the game safe in devastating style. Garner, a growing influence, intercepted a pass from Dedic and released Dewsbury-Hall behind a static Newcastle defence. The midfielder took Burn out of the equation with a perfect pass across to Barry, who had time to control and place a fine finish beyond Hornicek.

Burn finally broke Everton’s resistance with a late header from an Elanga cross. A melee involving the goalscorer, Pickford, James Tarkowski and Joelinton broke out as they fought over the ball – all four were booked – but there would be no miraculous escape for Newcastle. It is Everton who march on to face the Cod Army.

Sports.title: PSG claim late point after Shaw penalty to hit Manchester City’s WCL top-four hopes
Sports.content:
You cannot miss half a dozen big chances at Women’s Champions League level and expect to get away with it. That is the harsh lesson Manchester City learnt on Thursday against Paris Saint-Germain, who extended the English champions’ wait for their first win in Europe this season by striking late to secure a point at a disappointed Joie Stadium.

City’s third draw from three Champions League games so far this season really ought to have been a victory. Instead, their hopes of a top-four spot and with it automatic qualification for the quarter-finals are looking increasingly slim.

They thought they had won the game through Khadija “Bunny” Shaw’s 85th-minute penalty, but conceding sparked PSG into life and they snatched a point with a scrappy equaliser three minutes later as their substitute Tara Elimbi Gilbert found the net from close range.

How, therefore, should we look upon City’s season? Are they the team that is unbeaten in all competitions? Or the team without a win in Europe? Both ring true, and although they are still likely to progress to the knockout stages, they will have been hugely frustrated with their profligacy.

“There are a lot of things in this game we are pleased with. The result is not what we wanted, of course. Maybe we should kill the game earlier,” the City manager, Andrée Jeglertz, reflected. “Annoying is not the right word but it’s a little bit a feeling of ‘argh’. We deserved more, I think, but that’s how it is in the Champions League. When you dominate games and you don’t score, the opponent will take their chances and that’s what they did.”

View image in fullscreen Khadija Shaw converts her penalty to give Manchester City the lead. Photograph: Mike Egerton/PA

Draws away to Bayern Munich and at home against Real Madrid in their first two games were certainly not poor results, against strong opposition and with theoretically kinder fixtures to come, so there was no need to panic, but City’s 11th-placed position in the table, only one above the final qualification spot, before kick-off will nonetheless have looked a little concerning to some of their supporters. They ended the night 10th.

Jeglertz was positive about their chances: “We got drawn against six teams and we have played the three toughest of them, I think, so now we have three games that we have the opportunity, again, to get the points we need to qualify for the next round. So that’s our goal and nothing has changed.”

Nonetheless, this latest draw was a blow. PSG sought to frustrate City in the first half, and succeeded after riding out an early storm. Shaw’s header dropped wide at the far post from Aoba Fujino’s third-minute cross, as the home side made a bright start but were unable to score while on top. Shaw fizzed a low strike narrowly wide 11 minutes later after terrific play from Lauren Hemp. City controlled possession but did not test the PSG goalkeeper, Oliwia Peda, until the second half.

Quick Guide Roundup: Barcelona stay perfect, Juventus win again, Paris FC and Häcken draw Show Barcelona laid down another marker in their defence of the Women’s Champions League with an 8-0 win thrashing of the Danish champions, HB Køge. A Caroline Graham Hansen penalty and a goal from Ewa Pajor, who finished second in the Ballon d'Or behind her recently departed teammate Alexia Putellas, had the holders in command by half-time in Denmark. Esmee Brugts, Patri Guijarro, Clara Serrajordi, Kika Nazareth and Clàudia Pina, who grabbed a brace, all scored in the second half to complete the rout. Barcelona, who won the women's club award at the Ballon d'Or to go with Pere Romeu's coach of the year prize, remain top of the league phase with three wins from three by an aggregate score of 19-2, while despite the heavy defeat Køge remain in the playoff places. Juventus struck twice late on to get the better of Austria Vienna 4-1. Goals by Matilde Pavan and Alba Redondo put Juve seemingly in control before Lotta Cordes reduced the deficit with 12 minutes left, but Kysha Sylla and Júlia Bartel struck in the final nine minutes. This second straight away win puts Juventus fifth, a point off the last automatic quarter-final qualification spot, while Austria Vienna sit 15th and two points off the playoffs. Paris FC and Häcken shared the spoils in the French capital after Anna Anvegard scored in the fourth minute of stoppage time to cancel out Evelyne Viens’ early opener and grab the Swedish champions their first point in Europe this season. They and Paris FC both remain outside the playoff spots. Photograph: Sebastian Elias Uth/Ritzau Scanpix Denmark Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

This tricky game came in a testing week for City, sandwiched between last Sunday’s Manchester derby – where they dropped points for the first time this season after conceding a late equaliser – and this Sunday’s mouthwatering game away to in-form London City Lionesses and their Ballon d’Or winner, Alexia Putellas, who sit just one place and three points behind them in the WSL. Nobody in sky blue could afford to think about that game yet, though – PSG were no pushovers.

Straight after the restart, Fujino went close as she latched onto Kerstin Casparij’s clever ball and shot over from a tight angle. Fujino, a livewire throughout the night, also saw a shot blocked by Thiniba Samoura, as the hosts began to ask tougher questions. Soon they were creating chance after chance.

Shaw’s powerful low shot was turned behind by Peda. From the resulting corner, curled in expertly by Alex Greenwood, Shaw had a free header but was unable to connect. Mary Fowler then scuffed wide as frustrations began to mount. Shaw headed wide again moments later.

Surely the WSL’s top goalscorer was not going to fire a blank? Indeed not. She finally broke the deadlock after winning a spot-kick, brought down by Griedge Mbock Bathy, and then fired her penalty low to the keeper’s right. But that triggered PSG to attack with vigour for the first time in the match and they were soon level, bursting the City bubble.

Sports.title: Inter and Milan unveil plans for new shared stadium to replace San Siro
Sports.content:
Internazionale and Milan have unveiled plans for their new Generali Stadium, which will replace the shared San Siro venue from the 2031-32 season.

The stadium, sponsored by Generali – Italy’s largest insurance company – will have a capacity of 71,500 seats and is expected to cost the two clubs €1.2 billion (£1bn). The plans were revealed at a gala event at Milan’s Castello Sforzesco on Thursday – but some fans in attendance voiced their opposition to San Siro being demolished.

Shortly before the briefing began, a group of Inter fans walked into the courtyard of the castle and unfurled a banner reading “you will never extinguish the lights at San Siro,” and chanting “hands off San Siro.” Work on the new stadium is set to begin in 2028, on the site of the existing 75,000-capacity venue.

The Generali Stadium will be shaped “low in the body, and rises up at either end” behind the goals, architect Norman Foster said. David Manica, a stadium specialist who collaborated with Foster on the project, added that the steep-sided design aims to bring fans as close to the pitch as possible.

“The most important thing that we realised when we designed this project is that San Siro is a feeling,” Manica said. “It’s more than a building, it’s a feeling … we brought all the seats as close as possible to the field. They could not be any closer, it’ll actually feel as though you’re sitting on the grass.”

View image in fullscreen An artist’s impression of a concourse inside the planned 71,500-capacity arena. Photograph: Foster + Partners

The stadium will also be capable of hosting NFL international games, rugby matches and concerts. Milan and Inter paid €197 million (£165m) to acquire the current San Siro stadium and its adjacent parking arenas. The current ground will be largely demolished once construction work nears completion.

Also known as the Giuseppe Meazza Stadium, San Siro opened in 1926 and is the largest sports stadium in Italy. It is considered to be one of European football’s most iconic venues, but requires extensive modernisation despite undergoing a number of renovations during its lifespan.

The Generali Stadium could be used as a venue for Euro 2032, which is being jointly hosted by Italy and Turkey. Foster and Manica previously worked together on the new Wembley Stadium, while the architect’s Foster + Partners firm also designed the plans for Manchester United’s proposed new 100,000-capacity home.

Sports.title: Uefa close to selecting candidate to run against Infantino in Fifa election
Sports.content:
Uefa and its allies are close to identifying a candidate to run against Gianni Infantino in the Fifa election and could select the challenger as early as next week.

The clock is ticking on efforts to oppose Infantino in March, with candidates required to confirm they are standing by 18 November, but there is growing confidence those attempts are nearing a successful resolution. Discussions with potential nominees have gained momentum despite recent setbacks that included a U-turn by the Asian Football Confederation president, Sheikh Salman bin Ibrahim al-Khalifa, who surprisingly endorsed Infantino’s push for a fourth term.

Should an opponent’s identity be confirmed, it will be presented to Uefa’s executive committee and in an online meeting of the confederation’s FA heads. There remains an appetite to leave any announcement until as close to the deadline as possible, largely to head off the possibility of a “dirty tricks” campaign by Fifa against the proposed candidate, but some sources believe the relevant meetings may be called in the next seven days.

Although Arsène Wenger has been among the high-profile names mooted, and is highly favoured as a potential unity candidate in some European football circles, the former Arsenal manager is not believed to have seriously entered the reckoning. Wenger, Fifa’s chief of global football development, could be found at the Fifa Under-15 World Cup in Azerbaijan this week extolling the virtues of his employer’s new tournament.

Anyone confirming their desire to stand will have to tackle severe doubts about the prospects of defeating Infantino, who has embarked on an international effort to recover his position in recent weeks after being heavily damaged by the Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) scandal. They would need to add a substantial number of votes from Asia, Concacaf and Africa to the European bloc, which itself may not be taken for granted in a secret ballot, to reach the 106 required.

There has been growing cynicism in some corners about the prospects of unseating Infantino in an election, one argument being that a more effective strategy would be a mass boycott or abstention from the vote in Rabat. A view exists that this would isolate Infantino, who has never hidden the fact that his organisation is dependent on Europe for vast amounts of its revenue. Now he finds it in a form of administrative paralysis. The 2029 men’s Club World Cup, currently without a host, is among the events stuck in a deep freeze with little progress being made on its shape or location.

View image in fullscreen Aleksander Ceferin is a strong critic of Gianni Infantino’s actions. Photograph: Mark Pain/Alamy

But there remains a determination to face down Infantino in March, with some close to the process pointing out that events may have turned further against the Fifa president by then. Infantino faces the spectre of Uefa’s application to four courts in the US for the release of documents pertaining to the failed FFE scheme, with a view to lodging a criminal complaint in Switzerland alleging financial mismanagement. Fifa has accused Uefa of “harassment” and “misinformation” and denied wrongdoing by Infantino.

A preliminary ruling is expected in the coming weeks, although the prospect of Fifa appealing against any decision that goes against it means the process may be extended. Should Uefa make significant progress with the case, any election or candidature process may come to feel inconsequential.

Fifa has until Monday, a deadline set by Uefa, to respond to 42 questions regarding its governance and decision making. Those include issues surrounding FFE, the Fifa peace prize and the suspension of Folarin Balogun’s ban at the World Cup. The Guardian understands Uefa is yet to receive any response. Infantino said last week that Fifa would “answer all the questions posed, to the extent that the process allows and to the best of our ability”.

The US midterms, which will be held on Tuesday, may provide further hope for Infantino’s opponents. In July Jamie Raskin, the top Democrat on the House judiciary committee, launched an investigation into links between Infantino, Fifa and the Trump administration. He asked Infantino to provide relevant documents and sit for a transcribed interview, although that is yet to take place. Should the Democrats flip the House, currently controlled by the Republicans, his quest may receive fresh impetus.

Regardless, the period before 18 November feels critical for Uefa and its president, Aleksander Ceferin. The Slovene has driven a hardline approach against Fifa’s leadership, which he restated in his “Emperor’s New Clothes” polemic against Infantino at the general assembly of European Football Clubs in Copenhagen last month. Fielding a viable candidate would go a long way towards underlining its credibility.

A repeat of Uefa’s climbdown on the eve of the Under-20 Women’s World Cup, when it withdrew its threat to boycott the competition, would prove damaging. The extensive autumn charm offensive launched by Infantino has included visits to Latvia, Czechia and Azerbaijan.

Sports.title: Scottish Premiership makes first UK move to remove Saturday 3pm broadcast blackout
Sports.content:
The Scottish Premiership has made the first move in what is expected to be a coordinated attempt from the UK’s domestic leagues to remove the Saturday afternoon broadcast blackout by inviting bids to televise all of its matches in the next rights cycle from 2029.

A tender document issued by the Scottish Professional Football League (SPFL) last week is understood to have given broadcasters an option to bid for live rights to all matches, including games kicking off at 3pm on Saturdays, the domestic broadcast of which is currently prohibited under Article 48 of Uefa’s statutes.

The Guardian revealed last year that the Premier League and English Football League were eager for the blackout to be lifted because they have concluded that selling more matches to broadcasters is the best way to raise revenues, a view that also appears to have taken hold in Scotland.

The SPFL’s invitation to tender, first reported by Sports Business, is understood to give bidders the flexibility to bid on the basis of the blocked hours governed by Article 48 not being in place.

A source with knowledge of the tender said it appeared increasingly unlikely that the four British Football Associations would apply blocked hours in their territories after 2029.

UK broadcasters are prevented from showing live football between 2.45pm and 5.15pm on Saturdays when 50% of games in the top two divisions take place during that period, a provision that means 3pm kick-offs can be broadcast on FA Cup weekends and on weekend bank holidays over Christmas.

The UK is the last country in Europe to invoke Article 48, which allows associations to stipulate a period during which matches cannot be televised live in their territory.

While the English, Scottish, Welsh and Northern Irish FAs are responsible for applying Article 48, they will be guided by the wishes of the clubs.

UK broadcasters can currently show up to 270 Premier League matches, 1,059 EFL games and 82 from the Scottish Premiership, amounting to 35% of fixtures across the season.
