The Premier League chief executive, Richard Masters, said in August the subject of lifting Article 48 was a live discussion. “We’ve got to take that decision at some point in the future about whether things are going to change,” he told TalkSport. “It’s not a decision for now. It’s a decision we’ve got to make before the next set of domestic processes that the EFL and the Premier League are going to do. I’d say in about 18 months’ time we’ll come back to that decision about whether Article 48 should remain or not.”

Sports.title: Carrick keeps Fernandes as captain and says he needs no assurances on United future
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick has said he will not strip Bruno Fernandes of the Manchester United captaincy after dropping him for the defeat by Bournemouth and that he is not surprised to have kept his job as the head coach.

Carrick and Fernandes held talks this week after the Portuguese criticised the tactics in the loss to Como, resulting in the midfielder being an unused substitute on Sunday. Harry Maguire took the armband but will not retain it for Saturday’s game at Chelsea, with Carrick saying “there is no decision to be made” and praising Fernandes.

“He’s an important player for this group,” he said. “He has been and he will be. Between us, we’ve got to make a difference and we’ve got to push things in a good direction. He’s fully committed to this football club, he’s fully committed to making things better. It doesn’t change for me. He’s the one that’s kind of led the team so well for many a game and many a year, and he’ll continue to do that.”

Carrick’s future remains unclear but he has been given a chance to turn around United’s form. The hierarchy held talks over whether to stick with Carrick at the start of the week after eight games without a win, including a wait of more than two months for a Premier League victory. There is keen interest in Eddie Howe or Julian Nagelsmann as potential replacements.

“I don’t need any assurances from anyone,” Carrick said. “I totally get the position, I understand the job, I understand the responsibilities, I understand what comes with that.”

Asked whether he was surprised still to be in charge, Carrick said: “No, I am here to do my job. I am here to do the best for the team, and I am desperate to make us better and improve things, so I’m not surprised, no.”

The United supporters cheered Carrick off after the Bournemouth game, turning their anger on the players, who were booed at Old Trafford. “I care about what the supporters think,” Carrick said. “I care about what it feels like in the stadium, and them travelling for games, to come and see us and support us.

“I care about what we give them, and what we offer them, and what they see. I genuinely don’t take any notice of anything else. I know this job, I know what it brings, I know what we need to do really to be better. I don’t need anyone else to tell me anything else.”

United will be without the striker Benjamin Sesko until the new year because of a shin injury but Carrick was boosted by Kobbie Mainoo’s return to training this week.

Sports.title: Max Dowman to miss three games after Arsenal’s red card appeal rejected
Sports.content:
Arsenal’s appeal against Max Dowman’s red card in their Carabao Cup defeat at Fleetwood and the three-match suspension imposed has been rejected by an independent commission.

The 16-year-old Dowman was sent off for a kick out at Harrison Neal following a bruising tackle in the 85th minute of the game, which Fleetwood won on penalties after a 1-1 draw.

Arsenal subsequently lodged an appeal, but the Football Association confirmed on Thursday an independent commission had dismissed claims of both wrongful dismissal and excessive punishment for Dowman.

As a result, Dowman will be suspended for Sunday’s Premier League trip to Liverpool as well as their home game with Hull and trip to Newcastle either side of the international break.

The FA said the written reasons for the commission’s decision to dismiss the claims would be published in due course.

The Arsenal manager, Mikel Arteta, said after Tuesday’s match he had not spoken to Dowman about his dismissal, but added: “When we prepared the context of the match, we were very clear on the things to respect, the things that emotionally we have to dominate, it was very clear.”

After Fleetwood’s keeper, Jay Lynch, saved Bruno Guimarães’ penalty, 19-year-old defender Conor Haughey stepped up to fire the hosts into the quarter-finals with one of the biggest upsets in the competition’s history. Fleetwood will host another Premier League side, Everton, in the last eight.

Arsenal fell behind to Aaron Loupalo-Bi’s 21st-minute strike in a disjointed first-half performance after Arteta made nine changes.

The captain, Martin Ødegaard, came on at half-time and Viktor Gyökeres quickly levelled, but Dowman was dismissed before Lynch starred in the shootout to secure a memorable victory.

Sports.title: Inside Jack Grealish's struggles: Why Everton had concerns LAST season, how acolytes are taking advantage, issues with his attitude to football - and what he should do next, writes IAN HERBERT
Sports.content:
Inside Jack Grealish's struggles: Why Everton had concerns LAST season, how acolytes are taking advantage, issues with his attitude to football - and what he should do next, writes IAN HERBERT

At the Pride of Britain awards a week back, we witnessed the brilliant and magnetic side of Jack Grealish, sprinkling stardust as he presented an award to a child of imaginable courage who counts the Everton player as his hero. 'Footballers are classed as heroes – but these are the real heroes,' Grealish said that night. You could have heard a pin drop.

It was no different when he arrived back at Everton in September, to the delight of the kids awaiting him and his white Lamborghini in the country lane outside the club's Finch Farm training base. 'It feels so good. I think I'm at my best at everything in life when I feel loved,' Grealish said, articulating a very real sense that he was coming home.

He is popular around the club because it can be said without fear of exaggeration that he has a heart of gold.

Only on Thursday, an Everton-supporting father-of-three with a cancer diagnosis that gives him weeks to live disclosed that Grealish had put £10,000 his way. But within hours of that simple act of altruism coming to light, evidence of the other Grealish emerged, as Everton announced he had been excluded from the squad to face Newcastle in the Carabao Cup for failing to turn up for training last week.

It was by no means the first time. Everton sources say there had been similar causes for concern last season. Grealish reported sick ahead of last weekend's game at Arsenal, shortly after the Pride of Britain awards, and has breached Everton's disciplinary code through an unauthorised absence. The stated reason for his absence at Arsenal was illness.

Jack Grealish remains popular at Everton and has a heart of gold, shown by a £10,000 gift to a fan suffering from cancer, but he has since been dropped over a breach of discipline

There were similar causes for concern last season, with his return this summer going against David Moyes' better judgement

Everton's owners, looking for Grealish's glitz and glamour to gloss over their desperately poor and unambitious summer in the transfer window, were keen to bring him back. It was against Moyes' own better judgement that he accepted his return as part of the deal that brought Iliman Ndiaye's unwelcome departure to Manchester City.

Moyes needed discipline in a thin squad where every player's contribution would count this season. It was an opportunity for the few star players to inspire and shine a light for the younger ones. And therein lies the tragedy of missed opportunity where Grealish is concerned.

He, the quintessential British maverick playmaker in the mould of George Best and Alan Hudson, could be a Goodison hero of these days, yet seems incapable of showing he is bothered, ridding himself of the acolytes and hangers on who are dragging him down, and appreciating what an opportunity football offers him.

Though he likes a drink, it's not so much booze as his attitude, and a struggle to turn down a good night out, which is contributing.

There is no doubt that he still has the skills to be a cherished player. That much was clear in the early stages of last season when he was providing more assists than any other Everton player until a broken foot requiring surgery brought a premature end to his season.

This season he has, as yet, no assists. He has perhaps been frustrated at the number of chances he has created not being converted, though not every winger has Erling Haaland as his support act.

Grealish's patchy attitude to a football life is affecting his game, as he is not taking his man on in the way he used to and does not emit such light on the wing

Look hard enough, though, and you'll see signs that his patchy attitude to a football life is affecting his game. He is not taking his man on in the way he used to and does not emit such light on the wing. Pep Guardiola, at Manchester City, was the first to see this and rapidly made it clear he wanted him gone.

It's not too late for the 31-year-old to become the totemic presence that so many fervently want him to be on Merseyside. Moyes, who sees the wasted potential, has given him abundant support and patience since City left him out in the cold, hoping that he can make him see the opportunity, here.

Thursday night's excellent Carabao Cup win over Newcastle United opens up the potential for an exciting Cup run, with Fleetwood Town awaiting in the quarter-finals. Everton have not won a trophy for 31 years.

The hope must be that the significantly public nature of Grealish's omission – very much a case of Moyes refusing to tolerate another breach – will shock him into action.

It was even the wish of Prime Minister Andy Burnham, present at Thursday night's match, that Grealish would be re-signed to Everton and the PM declared after meeting him at the Pride of Britain awards that the player was an example of the way people 'buy into Everton.'

The collective wish for him to thrive at the club could not be clearer. Only he can make that happen.

Sports.title: 'I'm living my dream and loving every minute': West Brom star HARRY WHITWELL on his first-team breakthrough, James Morrison's words of advice, learning Norwegian and the Baggies' promotion hopes
Sports.content:
'I'm living my dream and loving every minute': West Brom star HARRY WHITWELL on his first-team breakthrough, James Morrison's words of advice, learning Norwegian and the Baggies' promotion hopes

As Harry Whitwell wheeled away after scoring against Burnley back in August, the home fans in the Hawthorns erupted in unison.

This was more than West Brom supporters celebrating a crucial goal against a potential promotion rival, though. Nine years after joining the Baggies' academy, the 20-year-old Whitwell, the latest academy gem from the club's underrated production line, had delivered a moment that showed he belonged.

‘I didn't really know what to do,’ Whitwell admits to Daily Mail Sport. ‘Growing up in the academy, you're always picturing scoring your first goal in the garden and thinking about what you’d do.

‘That went out the window. I was just taken aback for a little bit, but given I've been at the club for half of my life, it made it extra special.’

Whitwell joined West Brom aged 11 and has enjoyed a breakthrough few months after impressing in pre-season and earning the trust of boss James Morrison.

His goal against Burnley was his first in the league for the club, following an EFL Cup strike against Rotherham a few weeks earlier.

Although usually a central player, he has largely operated on the right of Morrison’s fluid 4-4-2 set-up, making 12 appearances in all competitions as West Brom sit fifth in the Championship. A new contract last month was recognition of his progress.

West Brom youngster Harry Whitwell has enjoyed a breakthrough few months at the club

With Whitwell and Co impressing, the Baggies have moved up to fifth in the Championship

‘It’s what I’ve always wanted, and I’ve loved every minute of it,’ Whitwell says. ‘It took a bit of time from my first game in the FA Cup to break through properly, but to be given a chance at the club you've grown up at is a dream come true.’

Patience has been key. Whitwell made his first-team debut against non-League Aldershot in the FA Cup in January 2024, before his Championship bow came in May 2025. A superb loan spell at Forest Green Rovers followed, but opportunities were limited after he was recalled in January.

He featured just twice in the league during a chaotic campaign in which West Brom narrowly avoided relegation. Morrison answered an SOS call in late February to take charge for a third spell as interim boss, guiding the Baggies to safety with 18 points from 12 games.

Whitwell had no guarantees when he reported for pre-season and was prepared to head out on loan again, but his immediate priority was to impress the coaching staff and see where it led.

Although he barely featured after his recall, he views that period as an invaluable learning experience.

Morrison’s impact over that time saw his role become permanent, and the momentum was carried into a summer rebuild that brought ten new arrivals.

The recruitment focused heavily on young talent at the behest of chairman Shilen Patel, technical director Dominic Price and head of football operations Ian Pearce, with Jimmy-Jay Morgan, Rabby Nzingoula and Toby Collyer among the additions. Norwegian midfielder Felix Horn Myhre, 27, was the only outfield signing older than 23.

Meanwhile, experienced high-earning stars including Karlan Grant, Alex Mowatt, Jed Wallace and Josh Maja departed as the Baggies trimmed their wage bill.

Whitwell is loving working under boss James Morrison (pictured), who has played a big role in his development

He is one of a number of talented youngsters in the Baggies squad, alongside the likes of Jimmy-Jay Morgan (right)

‘It's really exciting,’ Whitwell says. ‘We could be doing better, but to be in the play-off spots is really good. The squad is quite young, but it’s made up of players who are trying to prove themselves and are full of energy.

‘We're maybe just missing that final bit in front of goal to show that we're a team who can really be among it this season at the top.’

Morrison, an Albion legend who made 341 appearances for the club between 2007 and 2019, has played a significant role in Whitwell’s development. He previously coached the midfielder in the academy and handed him his Championship debut against Luton in May 2025.

‘We have a really good relationship,’ Whitwell says. ‘He's provided me with a lot of chances in the first team. With the career he's had, and as a fellow midfielder, I just want to learn as much as I can from him. He's always given little pieces of information which have been helpful and made me see the game a bit differently.

‘Maybe that’s why it’s been a bit more comfortable for me making that jump to the first team too, because I’ve worked with him before and know how he works and what he demands.’

West Brom remain a work in progress, with defeats against rivals Wolves and Birmingham exposing their deficiencies, while they’ve conceded first in their past six games. But there are encouraging signs of quality and resilience, evidenced by comeback wins over Blackburn and Wrexham in recent weeks.

Whitwell is enjoying the atmosphere around the squad and has struck up particularly close friendships with striker Barney Stewart and young goalkeeper Joe Wallis.

Whitwell pictured making his Albion debut in an FA Cup tie against Aldershot in January 2024

The midfielder (right) has made 12 appearances this season and recently signed a new deal

He sits alongside Albion’s Norwegian duo Aune Heggebo and Felix Horn Myhre on the team bus, and even started learning Norwegian on language app Duolingo as a result. That proved to be a struggle, however, with his lessons lasting only a week. Whitwell can at least safely order a coffee and say thank you next time he visits Oslo.

His progress is testament to West Brom’s academy, an often-underappreciated production line that has developed a host of talented stars over the years.

Morgan Rogers left for Man City aged 17 in a £5million move, while the sales of Tom Fellows, Alex Palmer and Dara O’Shea in recent times helped ease the club’s financial pressures under the troubled ownership of Chinese businessman Guochuan Lai, who sold up to Patel in 2024.

Under its manager Richard Stevens, who has just passed seven years at the club, the academy has continued to emphasise that hard work is key to player development. Whitwell, speaking to Daily Mail Sport as part of the EFL’s 'Raised in the EFL' initiative, which celebrates the work of youth systems, is the latest graduate to make the step up.

‘There's a lot of really good people and coaches who are very experienced and good at developing players,’ he says. 'We're hard-working and down to earth, too. The academy doesn't get the money that maybe the big clubs get, but all of our teams are focused on hard work, resilience and technical quality.’

Whitwell looked up to the likes of Fellows, Caleb Taylor and Sam Field during his own academy days and now, having established himself in the first team, he is a key part of a West Brom side that face a significant week before the international break.

A trip to West Ham is followed by back-to-back home games against Southampton and Millwall, and with eighth place now enough to qualify for the play-offs, the Baggies have an opportunity to underline their promotion credentials.

Whitwell sits next to Albion's Norwegian duo Aune Heggebo (right) and Felix Horn Myhre on the team coach and tried to learn their language on Duolingo

The 20-year-old is determined to continue developing and not take anything for granted

For Whitwell, the challenges keep coming but his determination won't waver after committing his future to the club until at least 2029.

‘To get that show of faith and be able to commit the next few years here was a really good feeling but this is just the start,’ he says.

‘I’m not taking anything for granted and just trying to make as many appearances as possible. Hopefully I can get more goals and assists because that's what you get judged on as an attacking player.

‘If we can get a bit of positive momentum leading into the international break, that will put us in a good position. Our home games are massive for us, so we’ve got to make the Hawthorns a fortress.’

Sports.title: Jack Grealish DROPPED for failing to turn up for training: Everton fine star for 'breach of club discipline' as midfielder misses Carabao Cup win over Newcastle
Sports.content:
Jack Grealish has been disciplined by Everton after missing a training session without permission.

The Toffees winger, 31, was left out of David Moyes's squad to play Newcastle in the Carabao Cup and will also be fined.

Grealish was said to be 'ill' when he missed Saturday's trip to Arsenal, which Everton lost 2-0.

But now the Manchester City loanee has been reprimanded for failing to show for Monday's work-out and was not part of the matchday squad on Thursday night.

Unusually, the club gave the reason in a statement on social media which accompanied the team news: 'Jarrad Branthwaite remains sidelined for a second successive game due to concussion protocols, while Jack Grealish is unavailable for selection due to a breach of Club discipline.'

The midfielder, who has had a stop-start season so far having failed to register a goal or assist in eight matches, left manager Moyes with little choice but to assert his authority.

Jack Grealish was left out of Everton's squad for their game against Newcastle after missing a training session without permission

Grealish (pictured with partner Sasha Attwood) was punished after missing training prior to the game on Thursday - Instagram: sashaa__attwood

Moyes, a disciplinarian, would only say after the 3-1 win against Newcastle: 'You probably know I’m not going to give any details, it is a club decision and I support that decision. It is something I don’t want to speak too much about.

'The one thing about Everton is that we have got really good values behind it. All the players stand up to the values and accept the values, on the pitch and off the pitch. From that point of view, I think the players did a brilliant job.

'It’s a small squad we have got, we are limited in some areas but we are doing our best to keep challenging. You can see what it meant to the supporters, this is a big moment for them, the players need to keep at it and we are not accepting any excuses. There’s a humility about us tonight.'

Grealish returned to Merseyside on loan in the summer from Manchester City after being frozen out of their squad last season.

British football's first £100m signing when he moved to City from Aston Villa in 2021, Grealish played 22 games for Everton last term, including 20 in the Premier League, scoring two goals and picking up two assists.

He has been regularly included on the left of attack, but Tyler Dibling and Tyrique George were used out wide against Newcastle.

The breach of club rules comes after Grealish was praised by fans after donating £10,000 to the fundraising campaign of an Everton supporter suffering aggressive kidney cancer.

DJ Anton Powers – an Evertonian – is believed to have shared the efforts launched by the family of Leon, 35, on Wednesday night, with Grealish quickly responding to the call-out with a generous donation.

'What an absolute gent Jack Grealish is,' Powers wrote. 'I put up an Insta story up late last night about a heartbreaking situation for a big Everton fan.

'And Jack goes on to donate to his fund. What a top guy (blue heart, hands raised emojis).'

Fans flooded the comments of Powers' missive with their own praise for the former England star, with many recalling that he has made similar impressive gestures in the past.

'Believe he makes a lot of charity donations like this, gent of the game,' one user commented. 'More players should follow (hands raised emoji).'

'In fairness Grealish has shown over the years that he's class,' another wrote. 'Fair play (applause emoji).'

Sports.title: Man United consider shock Dominic Calvert-Lewin move as club launch search for new striker after Benjamin Sesko injury blow left them with NO fit centre-forward
Sports.content:
Manchester United are exploring the possibility of a move for Leeds striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin as the club looks to strengthen in attack in January. Daily Mail Sport understands a move is viewed as difficult given the fierce rivalry between the two clubs. Calvert-Lewin has revitalised his career at Leeds after joining on a free transfer in the summer of 2025, following an injury-plagued end to his time at Everton. The 29-year-old has scored 20 goals in 49 appearances for Leeds, including five in ten games at the start of this season. Calvert-Lewin scored against Man United when the two sides played out a 1-1 draw earlier this month. The forward’s form earned him an England recall during the last international window, ending a five-year absence from the national team set-up. Man United are exploring a possible move for Leeds United forward Dominic Calvert-Lewin Calvert-Lewin netted against the Red Devils in a 1-1 draw between the sides earlier this month Man United are currently without a recognised striker with Benjamin Sesko on the sidelines Calvert-Lewin, who has started 38 times in his 43 Premier League appearances for Leeds, is currently contracted until 2028. Man United are currently operating without a recognised striker with Benjamin Sesko having been ruled out until at least January with a shin injury. The 23-year-old was struggling with the issue at the beginning of the season and saw his game time carefully managed as the club attempted to nurse him back to full fitness but those efforts now appear to have been in vain. Sesko has not featured for the club since their defeat by Brighton in the Carabao Cup on September 16, when he was substituted in the 66th minute. He missed all of pre-season with the complaint, which also plagued him last season and resurfaced against Liverpool in May, causing him to miss the final three Premier League games. The Slovenian, who pulled out of international duty last month, now looks set to be sidelined until the new year, dealing a major blow to United during a difficult run of form and leaving Michael Carrick without a recognised striker. WHEN LEEDS STARS JOIN MAN UNITED Eric Cantona - November 1992 Cantona's move to Man United was credited as one of Sir Alex Ferguson's most successful moves, with the Frenchman helping to transform his side into title winners. The maverick star had seen his relationship break down with Leeds boss Howard Wilkinson leading to speculation over a departure. Leeds chairman Bill Fotherby called his Man United counterpart Martin Edwards to enquire about signing Denis Irwin. After the suggestion was rebuffed by Edwards, Ferguson then asked about Cantona’s availability with a £1.2m deal then being struck. While initially seen as a risky move, Cantona helped inspire Man United to a first title in 26 years. The Frenchman was part of four title winning sides at Old Trafford and won two FA Cups. Rio Ferdinand - July 2002 Ferdinand became the most expensive British footballer in history when he completed a £30m move in 2002 after two seasons at Leeds. Ferdinand has claimed he sat in the office of Leeds chairman Peter Ridsdale for six hours to force through the transfer. The deal came amid growing concerns over Leeds financial situation, which was referenced by Sir Alex Ferguson when the transfer was completed. ‘A transfer like this has to be difficult. Leeds are a big club and our fiercest rivals, and he had four years left on his contract,’ Ferguson said. ‘We were hopeful because of Leeds' financial position. I think Peter Ridsdale has admitted that. Most importantly, Rio wanted to come here and this contributed to the deal.’ Ferdinand would go on to win six Premier League titles, the Champions League and two League Cups during his time with the Red Devils. Alan Smith - May 2004 Life-long Leeds fan Smith moved to Old Trafford in a deal worth £7million, with Danny Pugh going the opposite way. Smith opted to make the move following Leeds relegation to the Championship, which had left him in tears on the final day of the season. Smith's move angered Leeds fans having previously declared he would never play for Man United. The move, however, had helped Leeds amid the club's financial turmoil with Smith also waving a fee that was owed to him. Sir Alex Ferguson hailed Smith, stating 'I have never been more impressed with a young player, his desire to play for Manchester United is fantastic'. Smith career at Man United was heavily impacted by a broken leg and dislocated ankle he suffered in an FA Cup tie against Liverpool. He ultimately played 93 times for Man United, scoring 12 times, before moving to Newcastle. Karl Darlow - July 2026 Darlow is the most recent player to move between the two clubs, with the goalkeeper rejected a new deal at Leeds in favour of a move to Old Trafford. He had been Leeds first choice goalkeeper for much of last season but is now back-up to Senne Lammens at United. Darlow made his debut in Man United's Carabao Cup defeat by Brighton. When his summer move was confirmed, Leeds issued a 309-word statement but declined to name where Darlow had moved, instead stating he 'wished to explore a different challenge'. Right winger Bryan Mbeumo has been filling in at No9, starting their last five games there in all competitions, with Michael Carrick having lost faith in Dutchman Joshua Zirkzee. The decades-old rivalry between the clubs was highlighted in the summer when goalkeeper Karl Darlow became the first player to join Man United from Leeds since Alan Smith in 2004. Leeds refused to mention Man United in a statement confirming Darlow's departure at the end of his contract, with the club writing that he had 'wished to explore a different challenge'. Eric Cantona and Rio Ferdinand are among the most famous examples of star names to swap Leeds for the Red Devils. Daniel James moved from Man United to Leeds in a £25million transfer back in 2021, while Cameron Borthwick-Jackson was part of a rare loan deal between the sides in 2017 when Leeds were in the Championship.

Sports.title: AC Milan and Inter reveal first pictures of new stadium as San Siro replacement unveiled after £543million naming rights deal
Sports.content:
AC Milan and Inter reveal first pictures of new stadium as San Siro replacement unveiled after £543million naming rights deal

Italian giants AC Milan and Inter have detailed first images of their proposed new stadium ahead of demolishing the San Siro.

The two sides have long looked to move on from their iconic home, with plans to destroy it initially put on hold until things got back on track recently.

The teams shared a preview video of the new ground, with the aim of it opening in the 2031-32 season. It is set to be called the Generali Stadium, with naming rights sold to the insurance brand until 2052 for £543million.

Construction won't begin until 2028, and the stadium is set to hold 71,500 fans. It is to feature an X-frame structure and double-curved roof, with the frame to emphasise two curves, with one dedicated to Inter fans and the other to Milan supporters.

The stadium will be two-tiered, and will also be built with the idea of hosting concerts, with more public spaces, green areas and leisure and retail areas to be included.

Milan and Inter had initially planned on starting building in 2027, with plans to demolish the San Siro put into place as far back as 2019.

A new symbol for Milano.

A new home for future generations of fans.

Generali Stadium 🏟️@GENERALI pic.twitter.com/c7D0827E7T — AC Milan (@acmilan) October 29, 2026

Inter and AC Milan have revealed images of their proposed new stadium ahead of the demolition of the San Siro

The stadium will l also host concerts, though won't be ready until the 2031-32 season

Two different outside views were shared - one with blue for Inter's games, and one red for AC Milan's games

Construction won't begin until 2028, and the stadium is set to hold 71,500 fans in total

Images shared of the proposed stadium show the ground in all its expected glory in the heart of Milan.

One design showed a hypothetical game between Inter and AC Milan, with giant tifos of both sides shown in the ground.

A mock up of a concert is also presented, with bright lights on show and thousands of fans in the stadium.

The clubs had already announced agreements last year with architectural firms Foster + Partners and Manica to design a new stadium.

Foster + Partners and Manica's projects include Wembley Stadium in London, Chase Center in San Francisco, and Lusail Stadium in Qatar.

Norman Foster and David Manica presented the plans at Thursday's briefing.

'It is always a challenge to design a building that replaces a beloved project,' Manica said. 'And the way I'm thinking about this project and the spirit that we began with from the beginning was: same soul, different building.

'The most important thing that we realized when we designed this project is that the San Siro is a feeling, more than a building, it's a feeling. And everything that we needed to do here was to drive that feeling and carry it into the building.'

There was initially no objection to the plans, but negotiations dragged on and concerns began to rise over the cultural impact of demolishing the ground, which was built more than 100 years ago.

In 2023, it was ruled that the San Siro could not be demolished because it has 'cultural interest'. In 2025, however, the clubs bought the site to build a new ground, which made the decision to demolish the ground possible.

In its initial form the stadium was completed in 1926 but the middle tier, along with the iconic spiral towers, was added in 1955.

The San Siro was supposed to host the Champions League final this season, but was stripped of the right by UEFA after authorities in the Italian city could not offer guarantees that refurbishment work at the stadium and the surrounding area would not affect the match.

The aim is to host matches at Euro 2032, which Italy will co-host with Turkey.

Sports.title: Jack Grealish has let his team-mates down AGAIN: This latest self-inflicted episode shows he lacks the hard graft and humility so desired by David Moyes - and his team is better off without him, writes LEWIS STEELE
Sports.content:
Jack Grealish has let his team-mates down AGAIN: This latest self-inflicted episode shows he lacks the hard graft and humility so desired by David Moyes - and his team is better off without him, writes LEWIS STEELE

Hard graft, humility and fighting for team-mates: three qualities not shown by a certain Jack Grealish this week.

They are also a trio of traits demanded by the Premier League's most experienced boss, David Moyes, who banished the once £100million man Grealish to the naughty step for missing training without permission.

News of his latest act of ill-discipline dominated every conversation on the Merseyside waterfront before this full-blooded contest with Newcastle but Grealish was not missed a jot as his youthful and energetic replacements put on a show.

Goals from James Garner, Hayden Hackney and Thierno Barry were enough to send Moyes and Co to the Carabao Cup quarter-final and within sight of their first trophy since 1995, something the 63-year-old boss and these loyal fans crave above anything.

Moyes made the decision to drop and fine Grealish alongside chief executive Angus Kinnear. It is unknown if he will return for Monday's league game, also against Newcastle. The boss would not comment on the situation but said he supported the club decision to drop him.

'The one thing about Everton is that we have got really good values behind it,' he said. 'All the players stand up to the values and accept the values, on the pitch and off the pitch.

Hayden Hackney and James Garner were on target as Everton reached the Carabao Cup quarter-finals with a 3-1 victory over Newcastle

David Moyes' side advanced without Jack Grealish, who was absent from the squad due to a breach of club discipline

Garner broke the deadlock with an effort into the bottom corner after Newcastle gave the ball away

'From that point of view, I think the players did a brilliant job. It's a small squad we have got, we are limited in some areas but we are doing our best to keep challenging. You can see what it meant to the supporters, this is a big moment for them. There's humility about us tonight.'

Giant-slayers Fleetwood Town are up next. Given the way they toppled champions Arsenal on Tuesday, that will be no easy feat, but a trip to Highbury is all that stands between the Toffees and a first domestic cup semi-final since 2015-16.

Newcastle, meanwhile, look a pale imitation of the great team that beat Liverpool to win this competition in 2025 and the jury remains out on Matthias Jaissle. He lambasted his side's lack of maturity and said: 'It is shocking and it is frustrating as well.

'You need to be more mature and more clinical in these situations. Just clear it. It is a learning process but we don't have the time, we need to learn fast, especially with these young lads which is not an excuse any more.'

Fans around the country have tended to see the Carabao Cup as a chance to save some money in recent years and Everton supporters have grumbled at Moyes and former boss Sean Dyche for having a similar attitude with line-ups.

But a full house of 51,894 here – including 8,000 of the travelling Toon army – indicated that both teams were taking this seriously. Both mid-table with inconsistent form, this was a real chance for success.

Even the Prime Minister, Andy Burnham, knew that and was in attendance alongside his wife Marie-France. There was an obvious joke to be made around this week's budget, which has given a helping hand to those in need this winter.

Given the Grealish-shaped hole in Moyes's team and the obvious lack of numbers in multiple positions, the Everton top brass might have fancied getting in Burnham's ear to get the chancellor's phone number and ask for a leg-up too.

Hackney volleyed in his first goal for the club following his summer move from Middlesbrough

Thierno Barry added Everton's third in the second half to set-up a tie against Fleetwood Town

Matthias Jaissle's side will seek revenge when the sides meet again in the league on Monday

Prime Minister Andy Burnham was among those celebrating as Everton bid to end their trophy drought

Moyes has had to muddle through the season with a dearth of outfielders following a botched transfer window, but he has made the best of a tricky situation – one that was not helped by Grealish's actions.

Any frustration at those off-the-field issues was parked on the night, though, as Everton found themselves two ahead at half-time. It was a scoreline to leave Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle cursing after a string of missed chances.

MATCH FACTS AND PLAYER RATINGS EVERTON (4-2-3-1): Pickford 7; Rohl 6, Tarkowski 7, O'Brien 7, Mykolenko 7 (Maitland-Niles 86); Hackney 8, Garner 7; Dibling 7 (Johnson 77), Dewsbury-Hall 8 (Norgaard 86), George 8 (Alcaraz 77); Barry 7. Subs not used: Travers, King, Keane, Armstrong, Graham. Scorers: Garner 34, Hackney 45, Barry 69. Booked: Hackney, Dewsbury-Hall, Mykolenko, Pickford, Tarkowski. Manager: David Moyes 8. NEWCASTLE (4-2-3-1): Hornicek 5; Dedic 5, Schar 5, Burn 6, Hall 6; Gonzalez 5 (Steur 81), Ramsey 5 (Joelinton 46); Murphy 5 (Toure 67, 6), Willock 5, Barnes 7 (Elanga 46, 6); Osula 5 (Wissa 46, 6). Subs not used: Pope, Botman, Bamba, Thiaw. Scorers: Burn 88. Booked: Schar, Burn, Joelinton. Manager: Matthias Jaissle 5. Referee: Farai Hallam 7. Attendance: 51,894.

As it was, Everton weathered the storm thanks to Jordan Pickford and several last-ditch blocks.

Despite Newcastle's territorial advantages, the Toffees settled and were first to strike on 34 minutes. It came through Grealish's direct replacement for a starting berth, Tyrique George, winning possession and, via Hackney, feeding Garner to pass into the far corner.

Hackney soon turned from provider to goal-scorer, although referee Farai Hallam might claim an assist. Good officiating saw him play an advantage when Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall was hauled down when charging goalwards.

Barry picked up a loose ball and fed Hackney who volleyed home, making it look easy when he could have easily fired over the bar. Seconds earlier, Harvey Barnes had been denied by Pickford but Newcastle were undone by a motoring counter-attack.

Moyes would be delighted with the two goals but arguably more buoyed by the defensive rearguard that followed. Jaissle responded by throwing on three half-time changes in Yoane Wissa, Joelinton and Anthony Elanga.

None of them worked as Everton played with their hearts on their sleeves in a warrior-like defensive display that had this new stadium rocking like rarely before. James Tarkowski put his body on the line and Sunderland lad Pickford made several inspired stops.

Barry put the icing on the cake on 69 minutes when Garner robbed Amar Dedic of possession and Dewsbury-Hall teed up the No9 to finish with composure and help his team one giant step closer to ending that trophy drought.

No Grealish? No problem. The Manchester City loanee, who showed his admirable side earlier in the day when he gave £10,000 to help an ill fan, has let his team-mates down with this latest episode.

But with a collection of young talents thriving, mixed with some soldier-like experienced heads and a boss with an appetite for silverware, Everton do not need Grealish right now.

This night was one to forget for him and Jaissle's work-in-progress Newcastle, who are a shadow of the halcyon days of Eddie Howe's cup-winning side, despite pulling one back late on through captain Dan Burn's header.

Everton fans including Mr Burnham, meanwhile, will have March 21 and a potential final at Wembley circled in their diaries.

Sports.title: Cristiano Ronaldo hits HAT-TRICK in Al-Nassr's victory - and Portugal star, 41, could have had FIVE after having two ruled out as he closes in on 1,000-goal milestone
Sports.content:
Cristiano Ronaldo hits HAT-TRICK in Al-Nassr's victory - and Portugal star, 41, could have had FIVE after having two ruled out as he closes in on 1,000-goal milestone

Cristiano Ronaldo has edged closer to the 1,000-goal mark after scoring a hat-trick in Al Nassr's 5-3 win over Al Kholood.

The 41-year-old Portugal star scored all three within 15 second-half minutes, finding the back of the net in the 66th, 72nd and 81st minutes to seal all three points at Alawwal Park on Thursday.

Ronaldo's treble has taken him to 985 career goals as he edges nail-bitingly close to the ultimate milestone that he has been chasing for many years, since breaking the record for top goalscorer in football history in 2021.

Addressing the target with his former team-mate Rio Ferdinand in 2024, Ronaldo said: 'I want to reach 1,000 goals. If I don't have any injuries, this for me is the most important (thing), I want that.

'For me, the best mark that I can have in football is to reach, first, 900 goals. After, my challenge is to be at 1,000 goals.'

Despite surpassing Josef Bican five years ago as the all-time top goalscorer for club and country, that number is contested due to a lack of data from some historical records.

Ronaldo's treble has taken him to 985 career goals as he edges nail-bitingly close to the ultimate milestone that he has been chasing for many years

Last week, Ronaldo became football's first multi-billionaire after the veteran forward raked in £225million this year, according to Forbes (source: cristiano/Instagram)

Brazil legend Pele, for example, is recognised by Guinness World Records as having scored 1,279 career goals in 1,363 games, though many of those matches were exhibitions. FIFA lists Pele's total at 767 career goals.

Lionel Messi, meanwhile, has continued to remain hot on Ronaldo's heels, and is the next player directly behind him with 936.

Ronaldo won consecutive Saudi Pro League Golden Boots in 2023-24 and 2024-25. He finished third in last season's scoring race with 28 goals.

Of his 985 official goals, a whopping 450 came during his nine-year spell at Real, while he netted 145 for Manchester United, 146 for his country Portugal, 101 for Juventus, 138 for current club Al-Nassr and five at Sporting Lisbon.

Last week, Ronaldo became football's first multi-billionaire after the veteran forward raked in £225million this year, according to Forbes.

Ronaldo reportedly passed the $2billion mark in career earnings earlier this year, just six years after he was the first footballer to surpass $1billion.

Ronaldo's status comes as he again topped Forbes' football rich list, aided by a lucrative salary at Saudi Arabian side Al-Nassr which is estimated at £488,000-per-day.

Forbes has determined that Ronaldo has also earned £42million off the pitch over the course of the year, which has come via endorsements and his business ventures.

Ronaldo reportedly passed the $2billion mark in career earnings earlier this year (source: cristiano/Instagram)

Ronaldo's off the pitch earnings alone would surpass the total earnings of all but four of his peers.

Confirmation of Ronaldo's continued position at the top of the rich list comes just days after he was fined a measly £215 by Portugal for walking out of their national team during the recent international window.

Ronaldo is joined in the top two by his longtime rival Messi, with the pair occupying the highest two positions for the 12th time in the last 13 years.

Inter Miami star Messi is estimated to have earned £109million over the past year and is expected to soon join Ronaldo in passing the $2billion career earnings milestone.

Sports.title: Chelsea's rivals eyeing unused Estevao - plus the reason Xabi Alonso is snubbing Brazilian, why other clubs believe Blues will win race for £90m Alex Scott and the Como wonderkid on radar: CHELSEA CONFIDENTIAL
Sports.content:
Chelsea's rivals eyeing unused Estevao - plus the reason Xabi Alonso is snubbing Brazilian, why other clubs believe Blues will win race for £90m Alex Scott and the Como wonderkid on radar: CHELSEA CONFIDENTIAL

Multiple Premier League and European rivals of Chelsea are watching the club's handling of Estevao Willian with intrigue after the Brazilian wonderkid again went unused under Xabi Alonso.

Despite Cole Palmer’s suspension and Joao Pedro’s injury, Estevao was overlooked during Wednesday’s Carabao Cup exit to Liverpool. The 19-year-old stayed sat on the bench at Anfield while four others were introduced during the 1-1 draw preceding the penalty shootout.

In Chelsea’s eight Premier League fixtures, he has been brought on as a late substitute six times and unused twice.

Estevao is tied down to a contract lasting into the 2030s with Chelsea, who consider him among their ‘untouchables’ and have looked at trying to arrange a new deal. But external sources have confided that his situation is piquing interest within Premier League and European circles.

It is understood Estevao's limited role under Alonso is not the result of a fall-out, and purely down to tactical and technical decisions. Chelsea’s manager has hinted that the physicality of the Premier League is a contributing factor while promising greater chances as the season progresses.

Alonso does not see Estevao as suited to a wing-back role, which involves a great deal of tracking back, but as a winger who can come inside, as Palmer does in the 3-4-2-1 system.

Estevao was an unused substitute during Chelsea's Carabao Cup exit to Liverpool and his lack of minutes is piquing the interest of rivals clubs in the Premier League and across Europe

In Chelsea’s eight Premier League fixtures, the Brazilian has been brought on as a late substitute six times and unused twice

Chelsea fans hope they will soon see more of Estevao in action – the away end at Anfield were singing his name on Wednesday while he went unused. But Palmer will be back available when Manchester United visit Stamford Bridge in the Premier League this Saturday lunchtime after serving his one-game ban.

Carlo Ancelotti has named him in his Brazil squad for their November friendlies against Japan and Singapore. Estevao has started as many matches for his country in their one international break as he has for Chelsea in all competitions this season.

Ancelotti said during the last break that he would overlook his lack of minutes with Chelsea because he considers it his duty to aid his development. The Sao Paulo native has six goals in 14 Brazil caps.

Como star on radar

Chelsea are continuing to keep tabs on Jacobo Ramon, the 21-year-old defender of Como who is impressing under Cesc Fabregas, though they are joined by others across England and Europe.

Arsenal and Manchester United have also been linked with Ramon. His situation is likewise complicated by Real Madrid retaining a 50 per cent sell-on clause in any deal for the Spain Under 21s centre back, as well as an unspecified buy-back clause.

Ramon played under Alonso way back in 2018-19, when the now-Chelsea manager began his coaching career within Madrid’s youth system.

Chelsea’s interest predates Alonso’s arrival and goes back to last January, when they had Ramon on a shortlist along with Jeremy Jacquet – then of Rennes, now of Liverpool – and Marcos Senesi – then of Bournemouth, now of Tottenham.

Chelsea focused on trying to sign Jacquet, but he chose Liverpool, signing a pre-agreement to join them in the summer for £60million. He came on as a substitute in Wednesday’s Carabao Cup clash, replacing Virgil van Dijk.

Chelsea are continuing to keep tabs on 21-year-old Como defender Jacobo Ramon (left), but face competition from various rivals

Chelsea leading race for £90m Scott

Sources at rival clubs believe Chelsea will end up winning the race to Bournemouth’s Alex Scott, with it possible that an agreement could be reached before the January window.

The word is a fee of around £90m would be expected to be enough, despite Bournemouth saying they want £100m-plus.

In a way, the improving results of Marco Rose’s side are helping expedite Scott's exit, as they insist any winter sale would be blocked if their Premier League position were precarious. Scott is injured and Bournemouth have won five consecutive games in all competitions without him.

While Liverpool have looked at Scott, they are not said to have shown as much interest as Chelsea, and there are some suspicions that Bournemouth would like a bidding war for a 23-year-old midfielder who has indicated his interest in moving on.

Monaco’s Lamine Camara, who Chelsea came close to signing for half the price of Scott at £47m in the summer, also has his fans at Liverpool.

Chelsea's rivals believe the Blues will win the race to sign Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott

A bad omen for Blues?

Five years ago this week…

October 24, 2021: Manchester United lose 5-0 at home to Liverpool.

October 25-26: Ole Gunnar Solskjaer appears on the brink of losing his job.

October 27: Solskjaer surprisingly avoids the sack.

October 30: United head to London and win 3-0 away at Tottenham.

Chelsea are aiming to avoid history repeating itself when Michael Carrick's side visit Stamford Bridge this Saturday after a week in which United were beaten by Bournemouth but the boss avoided the axe.

Chelsea are expecting United captain Bruno Fernandes to return to their starting line-up after his clear-the-air talks with Carrick.

Lavia hits the full 90

Romeo Lavia completed his first full 90 minutes in a competitive match for Chelsea against Liverpool, which can only be good for his confidence levels.

Alonso identified that as an issue in pre-season, when he allowed the 22-year-old midfielder to complete the match in a friendly win over AC Milan. Chelsea’s manager told those of us on the tour that he wanted to give Lavia that moment because he believed he had a ‘mental block’ about it after his injury history.

Romeo Lavia completed his first full 90 minutes in a competitive match for Chelsea against Liverpool on Wednesday night

Post-career protection

This week, a group of Chelsea first-teamers and promising academy players got together in a meeting room at Cobham for a talk from a specialist brought in to discuss career-ending insurance.

While a dry topic, it is an important consideration for footballers in this unpredictable game.

Speaking of injuries, Chelsea have had an unfortunate run of muscle issues of late, with Maxence Lacroix struggling to walk off the pitch at Anfield after picking up a hamstring problem.

Fancy a job at Chelsea?

Chelsea are searching for a physical performance coach to join their first-team support staff. Within the job listing, they say they want someone who can ‘lead on GK specific physical development’.

Sports.title: Mystery surrounds Jack Grealish after David Moyes gives blunt response to Everton axing
Sports.content:
Mystery surrounds Jack Grealish after David Moyes gives blunt response to Everton axing

Jack Grealish was not in Everton's squad for their 3-1 win over Newcastle in the Carabao Cup on Thursday night due to "a breach of club discipline"

View 3 Images David Moyes was without Jack Grealish on Thursday night (Image: Getty Images)

David Moyes refused to explain why Jack Grealish was dropped from Everton's squad for their match against Newcastle on Thursday night.

‌



‌



Grealish was conspicuous by his absence for their Carabao Cup tie, with the club stating he was "unavailable for selection due to a breach of club discipline.”

‌



The 31-year-old was not part of the squad which was beaten 2-0 away at Arsenal on Saturday due to illness. It is understood that the on-loan Manchester City winger then missed a training session in between the Premier League match and the Carabao Cup fourth-round tie.

‌



But there remains some mystery around the situation after Moyes opted to stay tight-lipped following the 3-1 win on Thursday night. “I’m not going to give any details and it’s a club decision and I support the decision," the Everton boss said. “I don’t want to go into details.”

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



Asked if he felt let down by Grealish, who he has championed since his arrival on loan from City last season, Moyes said: “It is something I don’t want to speak too much about.”

The Everton manager was then asked whether Grealish would be involved in the trip to St James' Park to play Newcastle in the league on Monday night. "I wouldn't give any team news away," he replied.

‌



Goals from James Garner, Hayden Hackney and Thierno Barry had Everton cruising into the next round of the cup before Dan Burn scored a late consolation for the Magpies. Moyes' words on the performance appeared to hint at the Grealish situation.

View 3 Images Jack Grealish is understood to have missed a training session (Image: Getty Images)

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

“The one thing about Everton is that they have got real good values, all the players stand behind it and accept the values, on the pitch and off the pitch," he said. "I think the players did a good job tonight, it is a small squad but we are doing our best to keep challenging."

‌



Grealish, who is in the final year of his £300,000-a-week City contract, is in his second successive loan spell with Everton. He has made eight appearances in all competitions this season without registering a goal or an assist.

Last season he contributed two goals and six assists in 22 games for the Toffees and Moyes recently outlined his expectation for the winger.

‌



View 3 Images Jack Grealish is in his second loan spell with Everton (Image: Getty Images)

“I think Jack knows what I expect now," he said. "We had lots of conversations last year. He knows when he comes here there is an opportunity for him to play and to show what he can do.

‌



“But I also want him to be a senior professional and a role model. We’ve got Tyrique and Tyler and if ever you are looking at somebody for how to play as a wide player, Jack Grealish would certainly be one of them. I think both of them could learn an awful lot from Jack and I want him to become that senior citizen amongst them, somebody who teaches them.

“I think we’ve got a mature Jack Grealish now as well in terms of understanding the game and what is required, being a team player – not that he is an individual but he plays with an individual style.”

Sports.title: Liverpool news: £80m man urged to snub Chelsea and move to Anfield as Reds told 'sky is limit'
Sports.content:
Liverpool news: £80m man urged to snub Chelsea and move to Anfield as Reds told 'sky is limit'

Liverpool, who continued their run of strong form with a penalty shootout victory over Chelsea in the Carabao Cup on Wednesday night, are in the ascendancy both on and off the pitch

View 3 Images Andoni Iraola is all smiles at the moment (Image: Getty Images)

Things are looking up for Liverpool after they knocked Chelsea out of the Carabao Cup to book their place in the quarter-finals. A tense 6-5 victory on penalties at Anfield moved the Reds a step closer to Wembley and extended their winning run.

‌



‌



The shootout followed a hard-fought 1-1 draw, with Morgan Rogers putting Chelsea ahead from the penalty spot five minutes before half-time. Cody Gakpo responded just three minutes later, also converting from 12 yards to bring Liverpool level.

‌



The result means Andoni Iraola's side have now won five consecutive matches since their 3-0 defeat by Manchester City earlier this month. Virgil van Dijk was quick to highlight the renewed optimism around the club after the game, insisting the "feel good factor" had returned.

‌



Liverpool will now look to build on their momentum as they target a place in the Premier League title race and consider potential opportunities in the transfer market. With confidence growing at Anfield, here are the latest Liverpool headlines.

Carabao Cup quarter-final draw in full as Liverpool and Man City discover opponents READ MORE :

Liverpool open talks over January transfer as clear leader in Alex Scott race emerges READ MORE :

Make sure you don't miss the best Liverpool coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

£80m man told to snub Chelsea for Liverpool

Alex Scott has been urged to reject Chelsea in favour of a move to Liverpool. The Bournemouth midfielder, 23, was the subject of intense interest from several big Premier League clubs over the summer. But the Cherries opted not to sell, despite several bids from Chelsea.

‌



The Blues are expected to reignite their interest in the England international in January, with a potential £80million deal on the cards. But former Liverpool and Chelsea defender Glen Johnson thinks Scott would be better off at Anfield.

"As of today, I'd have to say Liverpool [over Chelsea]," Johnson said when asked which of the two teams Scott should join.

‌



View 3 Images Alex Scott is linked with both Liverpool and Chelsea (Image: Mark Leech/Offside/Offside via Getty Images)

"That's not necessarily due to him getting more game-time or anything like that, but I'm saying it more from the perspective of Liverpool as a club being a lot more stable and they’re going in a better direction.

‌



"I'd choose Liverpool purely for stability, but I'm not sure which club he'd get more game-time at to be honest. You can certainly understand why both clubs are interested in him though."

‌



Liverpool starlet told 'sky is the limit'

Rio Ngumoha has lavished praise on his Liverpool team-mate Trey Nyoni, claiming the "sky is the limit" for the 19-year-old.

Nyoni started in midfield on Wednesday night and produced a man of the match performance against a high-quality Chelsea engine room that featured Moises Caicedo, Romeo Lavia and former Liverpool captain Jordan Henderson. After the game, Ngumoha insisted that was just a taste of Nyoni's talent and demonstrated just how high the youngster's ceiling is.

‌



View 3 Images Trey Nyoni was named man of the match against Chelsea (Image: Getty Images)

"Trey is top," Ngumoha said. "You guys haven't even seen him at his very best yet. He definitely has another level to go and he's only 19."

‌



He added: "The sky is the limit for Trey. I'm really happy he's getting the minutes to show himself, but also everyone else, how good he is.”

Iraola was similarly impressed. "I think he has done very well. Really well," said the Liverpool boss. "It's good for the young players especially to have these experiences in cup competitions, where if you lose, you're out.

‌



"We were losing and then drew level. They weren't involved in the penalty shootout, but they experienced those feelings. They played under pressure against a very good team. And Trey finished physically in a good place, so well done to him."

Sports.title: Man Utd news: Michael Carrick told 'start getting results' as agreement reached on 3 replacements
Sports.content:
Man Utd news: Michael Carrick told 'start getting results' as agreement reached on 3 replacements

Michael Carrick remains at the helm of Manchester United for now as his strife-torn side prepare to face Chelsea in the Premier League

View 3 Images Michael Carrick is hanging on by a thread at Manchester United (Image: Getty)

Michael Carrick has been granted a stay of execution as Manchester United manager. But Saturday afternoon's clash with Chelsea could help decide just how long he remains in the post.

‌



United have played 12 matches in all competitions so far this season. They have won just two. Carrick was given the reins after a stellar end to the previous campaign, but after a relatively quiet summer, his squad are winless in eight.

In the Premier League, they've only tasted victory once - a 5-2 win against newly-promoted Ipswich Town - and currently sit 16th. Sunday's 3-0 defeat to Bournemouth seemed like it would be the coup de grâce for Carrick's reign. However, the club opted not to sack him.

After crisis talks involving CEO Omar Berrada and sporting director Jason Wilcox, the decision was made to give Carrick some time, with viable replacements scarce and a dressing room disagreement resolved. However, he remains under immense pressure and an impending visit to Stamford Bridge feels like a must-win.

Man Utd told Michael Carrick answers 'no' to two key questions in brutal reality check READ MORE :

Carlos Tevez claims he joined Man City to get REVENGE after Sir Alex Ferguson's broken promise READ MORE :

United hero Roy Keane certainly believes that's the case. He's told "lucky boy" Carrick exactly what he must do after surviving the axe. Mirror Football brings you the latest from Old Trafford.

Roy Keane's message to Michael Carrick

Keane pulled no punches when discussing Carrick's current situation and warned the manager that he must go to Chelsea on Saturday and get a result.

View 3 Images Keane has warned Carrick (Image: Getty)

Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Speaking alongside Gary Neville on the Stick to Football podcast, he said: "When he got the job last year and Carrick went in there, we said from day one we didn't think he was probably good enough long term.

"It's alright managing a few games, all of a sudden, then you've got to manage the football club, preseason, expectations, recruitment. They were getting results last year and people were saying you've got to give him the job because of results. All of a sudden, they're not getting the results. 'Oh, it's the board, it's [Jason] Wilcox. It's somebody else.'

"Michael Carrick, his coaching staff, Jonny [Evans], [Jonathan] Woodgate, [Steve] Holland - they're lucky boys to be still involved at Manchester United. They have to grow a pair and start getting results on Saturday. Get a result at Chelsea."

Three replacements

Elsewhere, two of Keane's former Old Trafford team-mates, Paul Scholes and Nicky Butt, have voted on three managers they agree would be fit to take over should Carrick be let go. And one of them was the Irishman.

View 3 Images Scholes and Butt agreed on three names (Image: Getty)

The United legends, appearing on the X page of their podcast, The Good, The Bad & The Football, were both given 11 names. They only agreed on three.

Antonio Conte was the first put to them and whilst Scholes approved, Butt did not. Next up was Gareth Southgate and they were split: Butt gave him the nod, but Scholes didn't buy into the ex-England coach.

Unai Emery was the third and both agreed he'd be a stellar fit. Out of the other eight, only Keane and Kieran McKenna had the two in agreement. On Keane, Butt said: "It would be fun" before Scholes admitted with a grin: "I don't see why not."

The pair were split on Fabian Hurzeler and Mauricio Pochettino, whilst both turned their noses up at Eddie Howe, Daniel Farke, Cesc Fabregas and Julian Nagelsmann for the time being.

Sports.title: Glazer family angry at Sir Jim Ratcliffe for breaking Man Utd 'promises'
Sports.content:
Glazer family angry at Sir Jim Ratcliffe for breaking Man Utd 'promises'

Sir Jim Ratcliffe faces growing Glazer frustration over his Manchester United management, as the minority shareholder's INEOS tenure comes under scrutiny after the club's worst Premier League start in almost 40 years

View Image The Glazer family have grown unhappy with way Man United have been run

The Glazer family are said to be increasingly dissatisfied with Sir Jim Ratcliffe's stewardship of Manchester United following his acquisition of a minority stake in the club during 2024. Ratcliffe bought a 25% shareholding in United as part of an agreement valued at roughly £1.2billion, with his INEOS organisation assuming oversight of footballing matters.

‌



‌



Nevertheless, the Glazers maintain authority over any prospective sale of the club. Under the arrangement, Ratcliffe also committed to a further £245million in investment, taking his overall financial outlay to approximately £1.5billion.

‌



The supplementary capital was earmarked to fund future infrastructure enhancements at Old Trafford, though on-field performances have demonstrated scant evidence of meaningful progress. The Glazer family, who continue to observe developments at Old Trafford from a distance, are now believed to be profoundly dismayed by the manner in which the club has been managed under Ratcliffe's direction.

‌



Man Utd eye January striker transfer after Benjamin Sesko update but shock rival move unlikely READ MORE :

Lisandro Martinez given Man Utd escape route after Jason Wilcox outburst READ MORE :

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

A source with social ties to the family informed the Mail that 'it's a travesty and not what they expected or were promised,' before noting that 'they have never run the club this way. '

Meanwhile, ESPN reported this week that the Glazers believe Ratcliffe 'couldn't have masterminded a worse situation', and described his 'downgrading in all departments' at Old Trafford as 'the opposite of what he said his strategy is.'

‌



United's difficulties have persisted on the pitch, with the Reds presently enduring an eight-match winless streak across all competitions. They have secured only one Premier League triumph this season, representing their poorest campaign opening in nearly 40 years.

The club stand merely two points above the foot of the table ahead of Saturday's encounter with Chelsea, intensifying the scrutiny on those overseeing football operations. United's continued troubles have additionally sparked questions regarding the club's worth.

‌



The Glazers had previously attached a $6billion (£4.5billion) valuation to United while considering a possible sale four years ago, though that sum now seems increasingly challenging to defend.

‌



Nonetheless, the American family retain authority over any prospective sale. According to the provisions of their 2024 arrangement with Ratcliffe, the Glazers possess the capability to compel him to dispose of his stake, which has subsequently risen to 28 per cent, should they consent to selling the club to another party.

Ratcliffe would possess no authority to prevent such a transaction unless he matched the bid and acquired the entire club himself, a scenario deemed extremely improbable.

‌



While reports have surfaced regarding the Glazers' discontent, they are prevented from repurchasing Ratcliffe's stake directly. Nevertheless, from next February onwards, the INEOS chief will no longer be able to stop the family from selling United at a valuation beneath the $33 (£25) per share he initially paid.

Meanwhile, INEOS have already started scaling back their involvement in football elsewhere. Swiss side Lausanne- Sport have become the latest club to be placed on the market, while the group has also reduced its asking price for French side Nice.

Sports.title: Tottenham star Dejan Kulusevski made heartbreaking admission to his mum amid injury hell
Sports.content:
Tottenham star Dejan Kulusevski made heartbreaking admission to his mum amid injury hell

Tottenham winger Dejan Kulusevski missed the entirety of last season with a devastating injury, and he has now opened up on just how serious the problem was

View 2 Images Dejan Kulusevski is now back in action for Spurs (Image: Getty Images)

Tottenham star Dejan Kulusevski has admitted his injury was so bad that it made him consider retirement. The former Juventus man was injured on the final day of the 2024-25 campaign after a collision with Marc Guehi.

‌



‌



Kulusevski consequently missed the entirety of last season as he attempted to recover. He has only just returned to contention for Spurs, having recently made brief cameos against both Coventry and Chelsea.

‌



Discussing his layoff with Spurs official website, Kulusevski has admitted that he discussed potentially hanging up his boots in a conversation with his mum.

‌



He said: “I told my mother, I sat with her and I told her, ’Listen, I don’t think this is going to work out’. I had to prepare her, ’I don’t think I can play anymore’.”

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



On the day he picked up the injury, Kulusevski added: “I remember the game, it felt a great warm-up, and then I remember the hit after 10 minutes.

“It was pain but it didn’t hurt that much, it has been much worse. I could feel that the knee was moving a little bit too much. I broke my cartilage, and the cartilage flew out and went to another part of the knee, and they can’t fix cartilage so In the scan they could see that a part of my cartilage was gone.”

‌



One of the games that Kulusevski was forced to miss was the 2025 Europa League final where Spurs beat Premier League rivals Manchester United to end their lengthy trophy drought.

View 2 Images Dejan Kulusevski was injured on the final day of the 2024-25 season (Image: Getty Images)

‌



And while Kulusevski was delighted to see the side finally claim a trophy, the actual moment itself was bittersweet. He said: “That was one of the hardest days in my life, I think.

“It was so beautiful to see all the people happy, but it was very difficult for me, going there with crutches, can’t walk. I couldn’t even take my medal because it was too slippery to go on that thing [the podium].

‌



“Things like this was not nice but I accepted it and I came back to Barcelona and I had to stay there because I couldn’t travel with the flight back so seeing the team celebrating on the bus, that was probably the most difficult part of all this journey, because you feel so alone in this time.”

Kulusevski could build his fitness even further this weekend as Spurs aim to make it three wins in a row against Leeds.

Sports.title: Jack Grealish AXED from Everton squad after 'breaching club discipline'
Sports.content:
Jack Grealish AXED from Everton squad after 'breaching club discipline'

Everton take on Premier League rivals Newcastle in the Carabao Cup on Thursday evening, but Jack Grealish will not be playing a part in the game after breaching club rules

View 2 Images Jack Grealish rejoined Everton in the summer (Image: Getty Images)

Jack Grealish was cut from Everton’s Carabao Cup squad to take on Newcastle after ‘a breach of club discipline’. The Toffees took on their Premier League rivals in the fourth round of the competition at Hill Dickinson Stadium on Thursday, winning 3-1.

‌



‌



The game was seemingly a perfect opportunity for Manchester City loanee Grealish to build up his fitness, having missed large swaths of last season with an injury. But he was surprisingly absent from the team sheet, with Everton confirming that he was not missing through injury.

‌



A social media post from the club before the game on Thursday read: “Jarrad Branthwaite remains sidelined for a second successive game due to concussion protocols, while Jack Grealish is unavailable for selection due to a breach of Club discipline.”

‌



Everton are yet to confirm details of the breach, although the Liverpool Echo say that Grealish failed to report for a training season after missing Saturday's 2-0 loss away to Arsenal through illness. His axe comes just weeks after boss David Moyes underlined his expectations of the 31-year-old.

Make sure you don't miss the best Arsenal coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



He said: “I think Jack knows what I expect now. We had lots of conversations last year. He knows when he comes here there is an opportunity for him to play and to show what he can do.

“But I also want him to be a senior professional and a role model. We’ve got Tyrique and Tyler and if ever you are looking at somebody for how to play as a wide player, Jack Grealish would certainly be one of them. I think both of them could learn an awful lot from Jack and I want him to become that senior citizen amongst them, somebody who teaches them.

‌



“I think we’ve got a mature Jack Grealish now as well in terms of understanding the game and what is required, being a team player – not that he is an individual but he plays with an individual style.”

Moyes added: “If there is one person who would be able to carry that [pressure] it would be Jack, just because of the way he is. He will find it easy to carry expectation and he’ll be happy to do so. That’s his character.

‌



View 2 Images Jack Grealish won't play against Newcastle (Image: Getty Images)

“I do think that is the case [that there is more expectation in the second season] because everybody wants Jack to get back to where he was. His first three months for us last season were hugely important in getting us wins, so now it is about getting him right to perform at that level again.

‌



“He’s had six-and-a-half months out. He’s had no pre-season games, he came on for 15 minutes in the Community Shield, so he’s had no real football and I think Jack is someone who thrives on the football. He gets himself fit through the games more so than the training. We need to be careful and see how he goes but he’s looking good.”

Grealish spent a productive spell on loan with Everton last season before injury curtailed his time with the club. He returned to Merseyside this summer and has made six appearances but has yet to contribute to a goal.

Sports.title: Man Utd target Premier League star for January transfer after suffering huge injury blow
Sports.content:
Man Utd target Premier League star for January transfer after suffering huge injury blow

Manchester United are set to be without Benjamin Sesko until at least January due to injury, leaving the Red Devils short up front, and a striker is on their shortlist

View 2 Images Dominic Calvert-Lewin recently scored against Manchester United (Image: Stu Forster/Getty Images)

Manchester United are weighing up a surprise move for Dominic Calvert-Lewin in the January transfer window. Calvert-Lewin, 29, is enjoying his second season at Leeds and scored one of his five goals this season against the Red Devils in this month's 1-1 draw at Elland Road.

‌



‌



The England international bagged 15 in his first campaign after leaving Everton on a free transfer and has proven his fitness with Daniel Farke's side. Leeds are already keen to offer him a new contract, with his current deal due to expire in 2028, but United are now circling.

‌



According to The Athletic, Calvert-Lewin is under consideration at Old Trafford as they target a striker. It follows this week's news that Benjamin Sesko, who led the line for the Red Devils last term, will be out until at least January because of a shin injury.

‌



Sesko is one of only four United players to have scored a Premier League goal this season, despite his minimal game time. "Unfortunately, Ben looks like he's going to be out for a period of time," Carrick confirmed on Thursday.

Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

"We're still not clear on exactly how long but it's going to be a longer period of time. "It was the process and, as I said to you before, we had to go through the process, a bit of a healing process for the injury, to see how it would react, in what direction to go with that.

"So, even now, we're still working through it but, yeah, it's unfortunate. Obviously, first and foremost, for Ben, for the kind of period that he's had and tried to get through it. Going through this again, and for us to not have him available, is obviously a blow, but we'll try to get him back as quick as we can."

‌



Should Manchester United sign Dominic Calvert-Lewin? Have your say in the comments section.

View 2 Images Benjamin Sesko is nursing a shin injury (Image: James Gill - Danehouse/Getty Images)

‌



As things stand, however, a move for Calvert-Lewin is thought to be unlikely, especially in the winter window. Leeds and the Red Devils share a bitter rivalry and deals between the two clubs are rare.

Karl Darlow notably made the switch to Old Trafford this summer but that was on a free transfer. Leeds last sold a player to the Red Devils in 2004, receiving £7million for Alan Smith.

Previously, Eric Cantona and Rio Ferdinand made the same move. Dan James is the most recent player to go the other way, with Leeds paying £25m plus add-ons in 2021.
