National development follows a similar principle. Ambition must be supported by clear priorities, functioning institutions and sustained implementation. President Tinubu’s reform programme seeks to address structural conditions that have constrained Nigeria’s economic potential, while investments in roads, education, healthcare, agriculture and other productive sectors provide practical pathways towards achieving the administration’s development objectives.

These efforts are deeply interconnected. Infrastructure fuels commerce, education empowers the workforce, healthcare drives productivity, and investment unlocks enterprise. Together, they create a powerful compounding effect—building a resilient economy capable of sustaining higher living standards and truly inclusive growth.

The Kaduna presidential campaign flag-off marks a pivotal milestone in Nigeria’s democratic journey. Beyond the political energy of a single Saturday, the true significance of this gathering lies in its vision for the future. It bridges the bold reforms already underway, the strategic investments being delivered, and the boundless opportunities being unlocked for all Nigerians.

Development demands patience, but patience requires proof. Citizens will only endure today’s hardships if they can clearly see tomorrow’s opportunities. This makes policy continuity vital. True progress relies on the unwavering, long-term execution of major reforms and infrastructure projects.

In the future, the Renewed Hope Agenda will be assessed by the extent to which its reforms and investments improve livelihoods, strengthen institutions and expand opportunities for Nigerians. The administration’s responsibility is to continue converting economic stability into productive growth and ensuring that the benefits reach communities across the federation.

As President Tinubu leads the ongoing work of national development, with the unalloyed support of Vice President Shettima, Nigeria’s ultimate ambition remains clear.

The administration envisions a nation where true economic progress is reflected in the vast opportunities open to the people, the enduring strength of institutions, and the shared confidence of citizens looking forward to a brighter tomorrow.

-Nkwocha, Media Assistant to the Vice President, writes from Abuja.

World.title: Ugwu: Could Nsukka Hold Key to Enugu’s 2027 Guber Poll?
World.content:
Can grassroots mobilisation, regional dynamics and Peter Ugwu’s humanitarian appeal in the vote-rich Nsukka zone upset the calculations and turn Governor Peter Mbah of Enugu State’s re-election bid into a fiercely contested battle? Jonathan Eze writes.

As political permutations ahead of the 2027 governorship election in Enugu State begin to take shape, the emergence of Chief Uche Nnaji and Chief Ugwu Chijioke Peter on the platform of the opposition Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) presents a contest that could be more complicated than prevailing political calculations suggest.

Challenging Governor Peter Mbah, whose administration has made significant investments in infrastructure over the last three and a half years, might appear daunting. Roads, public infrastructure and other development projects have given the incumbent a formidable record. Yet, the visibility of projects does not automatically translate into an unassailable electoral advantage.

Elections are ultimately contests over public perception, political alliances, regional interests and grassroots mobilisation. By this measure, the Nnaji-Ugwu ticket cannot be dismissed as a mere footnote in Enugu’s emerging political equation.

The choice of Ugwu as deputy governorship candidate introduces a potentially consequential dimension to the contest, particularly in Enugu North Senatorial District, popularly known as Nsukka zone, which remains central to the state’s electoral arithmetic.

The coming election may therefore become a test of whether an incumbent’s development record can withstand a challenger offering a different political narrative and a candidate whose appeal is rooted in humanitarian service and grassroots relationships.

The challenge beyond infrastructure

Infrastructure will undoubtedly feature prominently in arguments surrounding Mbah’s re-election bid. His administration’s projects provide tangible talking points and an opportunity to present himself as a leader committed to physical development.

However, voters also evaluate their economic circumstances, employment opportunities, access to essential services, security and the extent to which government policies improve their daily lives. This distinction creates an opening for the opposition.

The Nnaji-Ugwu ticket can build its campaign around the proposition that development must extend beyond impressive structures to the people who inhabit them. Ugwu’s political philosophy, as expressed in his acceptance statement, places human welfare, economic opportunity, dignity and collective responsibility at the centre of governance.

His declaration that Enugu should be measured not merely by its structures but by the quality of lives improved offers the opposition a framework for engaging voters who want infrastructure to translate into broader economic and social benefits.

The effectiveness of this argument will depend on its credibility and the candidates’ ability to connect policy promises to everyday experiences. Nevertheless, the opposition does not have to deny the incumbent’s achievements. It needs to convince voters that more remains to be done and that it possesses the competence and organisational capacity to deliver.

Why the deputy governorship choice matters

In Enugu politics, the deputy governorship candidate can carry considerable political significance when the individual brings regional credibility, personal relationships and an established network of supporters to the contest.

Ugwu Chijioke Peter appears to offer the PDP that opportunity. A humanitarian and philanthropist, he could help the party broaden its appeal beyond conventional political alignments by presenting himself as a figure associated with community engagement, compassion and service.

In an environment where voters expect leaders to understand their material circumstances, these attributes could provide a foundation for political mobilisation.

His appeal in Nsukka zone could prove particularly significant. Any serious contender for the governorship must recognise the importance of building a credible coalition across the area’s communities.

By selecting a deputy with grassroots connections in the zone, Nnaji has an opportunity to strengthen the PDP’s engagement with voters whose preferences could influence the election’s outcome. However, the advantage will depend on how effectively Ugwu converts personal relationships into organised support.

Ugwu’s background as a strategist also adds an interesting dimension to the ticket. Political strategy involves understanding local interests, identifying influential community networks, building consensus and ensuring that campaign messages resonate with different categories of voters.

If he translates his grassroots standing into a disciplined mobilisation structure, he could become an important asset to the PDP. His public presentation, centred on humanitarian service, may also appeal to voters seeking leadership that prioritises community welfare.

His acceptance statement provides further clues about the political identity he hopes to establish. By declaring that the office may carry individual names but that the work belongs to everyone, Ugwu presents himself as a team player rather than a deputy consumed by personal ambition. That message could resonate with voters seeking cooperation and collective responsibility in government.

Nnaji factor and opposition’s prospects

The other half of the equation is Chief Uche Nnaji, whose political standing, organisational capacity and ability to unite disparate interests within the opposition will be central to the ticket’s prospects.

A strong deputy cannot independently compensate for weaknesses in a governorship candidate’s organisation, message or credibility. The Nnaji-Ugwu partnership must therefore operate as a coordinated political project, with both candidates complementing each other’s strengths and building a campaign beyond their immediate constituencies.

For Nnaji, Ugwu’s emergence offers an opportunity to deepen the party’s presence in Nsukka zone while building a broader coalition across Enugu’s three senatorial districts. For Ugwu, the nomination provides a platform to transform his humanitarian and grassroots engagements into a statewide political responsibility.

The challenge will be to convince voters that the partnership can offer practical solutions to unemployment, security, education, healthcare, agriculture, small businesses and the cost of living.

The ticket must also demonstrate that its promise of collective responsibility can translate into effective governance. Ugwu’s emphasis on collective effort in achieving security and development is politically significant, but the campaign must explain the policies and institutional arrangements through which that vision would be realised.

Opposition politics is rarely won by criticism alone. It requires a persuasive alternative.

Why Mbah should not take the contest for granted

Governor Mbah enters the emerging contest with the advantage of incumbency and an infrastructure-based record that his supporters can showcase. That advantage is real, and it would be unwise for the opposition to underestimate it.

However, incumbency is not immunity from electoral competition. Visible projects can strengthen a governor’s standing, but their political returns depend partly on how voters experience the broader economy and whether they believe government achievements have translated into meaningful improvements in their lives.

The PDP could benefit if it turns the election into a debate about inclusion, economic opportunity, grassroots representation and the distribution of the benefits of governance.

Ugwu’s humanitarian profile could help personalise that argument. His appeal to ordinary citizens, supported by verifiable community engagements and an effective campaign structure, may provide an avenue to reach voters who are not persuaded by infrastructure statistics alone.

There is, however, an important distinction between political potential and demonstrated electoral strength. Grassroots goodwill must be tested through organisation, credible alliances, turnout operations and a compelling policy agenda.

The PDP must also avoid internal divisions and personality clashes among opposition figures who agree on the need to defeat an incumbent but disagree on the leadership and strategies required to achieve that objective.

If Nnaji and Ugwu maintain cohesion, articulate a consistent message and mobilise effectively, their ticket could become more competitive than initial assessments suggests.

An election with room for surprises

The February, 2027 governorship election in Enugu State should not be reduced to a contest between an incumbent with visible infrastructure projects and an opposition struggling to catch up. It is also a contest over political organisation, regional interests, the credibility of alternative leadership and voters’ expectations of government.

Mbah has achievements to defend and the advantages that accompany incumbency. But Nnaji and Ugwu have an opportunity to make the election a more demanding political test by emphasising human development, economic inclusion and grassroots participation.

Ugwu, in particular, could prove more consequential than the conventional perception of a deputy governorship candidate might suggest. His humanitarian disposition, philanthropic engagements, strategic orientation and grassroots connections in Nsukka zone provide the foundation for a potentially valuable political role. Whether these strengths translate into votes will depend on execution, credibility and the ability to build alliances across the state.

The Nnaji-Ugwu ticket is therefore not a political pushover. It has the potential to challenge assumptions about the incumbent’s electoral strength and compel the ruling camp to take the opposition seriously.

Ultimately, Enugu’s voters will decide whether the administration’s infrastructural record outweighs the opposition’s promise of a more people-centred approach to development. If the PDP consolidates its grassroots networks, capitalises on Ugwu’s regional appeal and presents a credible alternative, the contest could be more fiercely fought than some observers anticipate.

Enugu may yet deliver surprises in 2027. For a governor whose achievements are central to his political argument, the emergence of a credible challenger could make the road to re-election considerably more demanding.

World.title: Obama Versus Trump and November 2026 Elections
World.content:
Chido Nwangwu writes that in a couple of days in November, 2026, the battle of the political leadership and grassroots battalion will begin to show the results of the American contentious politics.

U.S. former President, Barack Obama, campaigning on October 24, 2026 at one of his political rallies for this midterm November elections, depicted incumbent President Donald Trump as an agent of “chaos and cruelty and corruption.” He said that Trump’s policies – especially Trump’s war on Iran – caused the inflation in the country.

Obama pointedly argued that “this administration’s actions are directly responsible for rising costs…. The current president chose to make a series of bad decisions. Most importantly, he decided to start an unnecessary war that nobody asked for, nobody voted for…. Now, two years ago, there were a lot of people who weren’t crazy about the guy’s character, but they were frustrated about post-Covid inflation,”

Obama did not spare Trump where he mocked Trump’s very prominent gold accents and other construction work the nativist, controversial politician has added to the White House.

In a major put down of Trump, Obama noted: “He’s got the White House looking like Saddam Hussein opened a Cheesecake Factory.”

He asked “Does anybody really think this guy in the White House right now is spending all that time thinking about these issues? I mean, I don’t know if you’ve noticed, but he seems very focused on home renovations. He should be on HGTV.”

The former President came to support Amy Acton, the Democratic party’s governorship candidate, former Sen. Sherrod Brown in Ohio; and in Michigan he campagned with Abdul El-Sayed (for Senate) and Jocelyn Benson for Governor.

Trump has been calling El-Sayed “Mohammad.”

Obama believes that the November, 2026 midterm election offers an opportunity for a “course correction.”

He predicted that “After two years of chaos and cruelty and corruption and incompetence, the likes of which we have not seen in modern times, you get the chance to say, ‘Enough’s enough. We are going to change right here in Ohio.” Only a few hours ago, Obama visited Atlanta, the iconic city of American civil rights, where he campaigned for Senator Jon Ossoff and Keisha Lance Bottoms, the Democratic Party candidate for governor of Georgia.

Obama recalled about Trump: “Two years ago, there were a lot of people who weren’t crazy about the guy’s character, but they were frustrated about post-Covid inflation…. They were seeing prices go up, and they heard him make a bunch of promises to get costs under control. This administration’s actions are directly responsible for rising costs. The current president (Trump) chose to make a series of bad decisions. Most importantly, he decided to start an unnecessary war that nobody asked for, nobody voted for.”

Next week, in a couple of days this November, the battle of the political leadership and grassroots battalion will begin to show the results of the American contentious politics.

-Nwangwu, Founder & Publisher of the first African-owned, U.S-based newspaper on the internet, USAfricaonline.com, established USAfrica multimedia networks in 1993 in Houston. Follow @Chidö247

World.title: Ego, Alleged Graft Set Awka Anglican Communion on Fire
World.content:
David-Chyddy Eleke reports that the very foundation of Christianity is being threatened in the Anglican Church, as the Primate, Henry Ndukuba; Archbishop of the Province of the Niger and Bishop of Awka Diocese, Alexander Ibezim; the Diocesan Board and other members are embroiled in war.

Things are deteriorating very fast in the Province of the Niger, Church of Nigeria, Anglican Communion, Awka Diocese. With the fast turn of events, Christianity no longer looks like a religion of tolerance and obedience, and the very people giving her the tag are its leaders. The Province of the Niger is one of the 14 Provinces of the Church of Nigeria (Anglican Communion). It was created in 2002. It is made up of nine dioceses, all within Anambra State. They include Awka, Aguata, Amichi, Ihiala, Mbamili, Niger West, Nnewi, Ogbaru Dioceses, and the mother diocese and oldest diocese in Nigeria, Diocese On the Niger (Onitsha).

The specific tag of the Diocese On The Niger as being the oldest in Nigeria gives a glimpse of its importance to the religious body in Nigeria. The province is headed by Archbishop Alexander Chibuzo Ibezim, who also doubles as the Bishop of Awka Diocese. He was ordained Bishop of Awka Diocese in 2010 in circumstances some church members had claimed were rigged to favour him, and nine years after, in 2019, we was elected the Archbishop of the Province of the Niger, to oversee the nine dioceses.

Genesis of Crisis

Early in his administration, both as Bishop and Archbishop, Ibezim had encountered challenges with some people expressing unhappiness about his administration of the church, but there was nothing really concrete to hold onto. But Ibezim’s real problems appeared in 2025 when a member of the church, Prince Echezona Bonti Onuigbo wrote a petition submitted to the Enugu Zonal Directorate of the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) through his lawyer, Chief G. Tagbo (SAN) of Ike Ike Associates.

The petition alleged that Archbishop Ibezim authorized / facilitated the sale of church-owned lands belonging to Diocese of Awka valued at over N2billion without the mandatory approval of the Board of Trustees, who are the legal custodians of church assets. The petition also complained of what was described as voracious wealth acquisition and shortchanging of allies, and alleged that proceeds were converted / some transferred to personal account. Also, Multiple plots at Ifite, Awka, Amansea, Ngozika Estate, were put up for sale at tens of millions to over N100m each. This prompted the EFCC to open investigation into the matter.

The Archbishop denied all these copiously. There were rumours at some point that Ibezim started evading arrest by EFCC, and then another that he was later arrested, but the clergy man dismissed all these, insisting he was only invited and because he had nothing to hide, he honoured the invitation, answered some questions and was later released. Not taking things lightly, especially as his character was at stake, he also approached the court to clear his name. Though he had also earlier obtained an injunction, on Sept 9, 2025, from Anambra State High Court, restraining EFCC and Bonti Onuigbo from arresting/detaining him. It was renewed by consent on Oct 14, 2025.

Comes the Suspension

As things got worse, Primate of the Church of Nigeria (Anglican Communion), Most Rev. Henry C. Ndukuba, got into the picture and directed Ibezim to proceed on six months’ leave with immediate effect amid investigations. Ndukuba, in a letter dated Tuesday, October 13, 2026, also announced the appointment of the Bishop of the Diocese of Aguata, the Rt. Rev. Samuel Ezeofor, as Supervising Bishop of the Diocese of Awka and Coordinating Bishop of the Province of the Niger during Ibezim’s absence.

The letter, addressed to Ibezim, stated that the decision followed recent developments in the Diocese of Awka, where the archbishop had been at the centre of various allegations and events which, according to the Primate, had raised concerns about the integrity and reputation of the Church of Nigeria.

He explained that the administrative measure was intended to allow a fair and thorough investigation into the allegations, while creating room for the restoration of peace and reconciliation in the Diocese of Awka. He specifically clarified that the leave did not constitute a disciplinary sanction, but was an administrative step to facilitate an impartial inquiry into the state of affairs in the diocese.

Ibezim Fights Back

Not willing to give up his position, and in what looked like attempt to clear his name, Archbishop Ibezim headed to court and challenged his suspension. To some others, this moved racked of a major insubordination to constituted authority, which is one of the cardinal message of Christianity.

In Suit No A/371/2026 – The Most Rev. Alexander Ibezim vs The Most Rev. Henry Ndukuba & Most Rev. Blessing Enyindah, filed same day he was suspended, Oct 13, 2026 at High Court of Anambra State, Awka Judicial Division through his lead counsel, B.E.I Nwofor( SAN) Ibezim asked the court to clear him of the allegations, insisting that no due process under church constitution was followed. He contended that no formal charge was ever preferred against him, no presentment served, and no ecclesiastical trial held. Therefore any letter of suspension / compulsory leave / removal / retirement / dismissal is unconstitutional, ultra vires, null and void.

Ibezim argued in the suit that section 29(1) chapter V relied upon by the Primate to suspend him only gives general supervisory powers but does not empower the Primate to compel a sitting Archbishop/Bishop to proceed on six months compulsory leave and appoint another Bishop to take over.

He relied on section 4, Canon X, which entitles a Bishop to remain in office until mandatory retirement age of 70 years, and asked the court to affirm that.

Church Board Sides Ibezim

While the back and forth continued, the Diocesan Board of the Church which represents the lay people of the diocese has taken side with its bishop, absolving him of all allegations. In an emergency board meeting presided over by B.E.I Nwofor who is the Lord Chancellor of the Diocese and also doubles as the lead counsel for Ibezim in a communique issued after the meeting reechoed the lack of powers by the Primate to sack Ibezim.

In the communique made available to newsmen after the emergency meeting, which was signed by Lord Chancellor, Diocese of Awka Anglican Communion, Sir B.E.I Nwofor, Synod Secretary, Ven. K.E.N Chukwukamma, and Lay Synod Secretary, Mr Eugene Chukwudi Okonkwo, the board said: “The Board rejects the appointment of His Lordship, Rt. Revd Samuel C. Ezeofor as supervising Bishop of Awka Diocese and Coordinating Bishop of Province of the Niger. His Grace, The Most Revd Henry C. Ndukuba, Archbishop Metropolitan and Primate of All Nigeria, His Lordship Rt. Revd Samuel C. Ezeofor and many members of the Church of Nigeria are fully aware of the pendency in court of these cases and are duty bound in law to refrain from doing anything whatsoever to interfere with the subject matters of the suits until the determination of the cases by the court.”

The War Begins

Not even the reference to the church’s laws that the Primate had no powers to suspend the Bishop could stop Bishop Samuel Ezeofor from immediately assuming his position as Supervising Bishop of Awka Diocese. To him, Ibezim had proceeded on leave as instructed, and he had taken charge.

The first casualty of Ezeofor’s assumption of office was the Diocesan Chancellor, Sir B.E.I Nwofor, who was removed from office on Saturday. In a letter, dated Saturday, October 17, 2026, and written on the letterhead of the Diocese of Awka, Ezeofor accused Nwofor of allegedly using his position to undermine the authority of the Primate of the Church of Nigeria and defying lawful directives issued by the church leadership.

In the letter addressed to Nwofor from Emmanuel Chambers, Port Harcourt, Rivers State, Ezeofor declared him unfit to continue as Chancellor of the Diocese of Awka. The letter, signed by Ezeofor in his capacity as Supervising Bishop, accused the senior lawyer of engaging in activities intended to undermine the authority of the Primate and bring the Church of Nigeria into disrepute. It stated that the alleged conduct was incompatible with his continued service as Chancellor of a diocese under the Church of Nigeria, and necessitated his removal.

Unrelenting Ibezim Sits Tight

As the drama continued, Archbishop Ibezim is not relenting. He has stuck to his position, insisting he is only being fought by dark forces. The clergy man who surprisingly showed up at the Cathedral Church of St Faith, Awka during last Sunday service said he was in church to pray for the church and against the battles against him. His appearance at the service was against the directive of the Primate, who suspended him from all church activities. A defiant Ibezim while speaking with the congregation said: “Please, at this time of trial, at this moment, let us recognize that we are not fighting against flesh and blood. It is a spiritual warfare. It is the battle against principalities. Battle, not of flesh and blood, but against principalities. Principalities are spiritual agents, powers, rulers of the darkness of this world, spiritual weaknesses in high places. So our battle is not the battle of flesh and blood. Bible is enjoining us that we should not fight physically. This is not a time to fight with gun or fight with cutlass; but it is a fight that is spiritual.”

Though Ibezim is fighting his war with prayers, he is not leaving out guns. This is evident in the number of security men that accompanied the revered clergyman to church on that Sunday. He may have noticed of plans to disgrace him out of office and did not want to be caught napping. For example, Bishop Ibezim’s security on Sunday would leave one thinking where God’s powers to protect his people was, especially as the Bishop always preaches to the lay faithful of God’s powers to protect. His security consisted of conventional and unconventional operatives drawn from the Nigeria Police Force and the state vigilante services, known as Agunechemba.

The Bishop may not be alone in the fight as his younger brother who is the Deputy Governor of Anambra State, Dr Onyekachi Ibezim, was also in church with security men attached to his office. It was not exactly known if his presence was to give support to his brother or a regular church attendance, but his presence with his security and full paraphernalia of office gave stronger protection to the cathedral which is known to be the enclave of Bishop Ibezim.

Where the People Stand

Though the church currently stands very polarized, a larger chunk of members of the church spoken to by this reporter have dismissed Bishop Ibezims claim of innocence, while some insist that the best way to clear his name was to step aside for six months and allow an impartial investigation into the matter.

A member of the church, Mr Tony Okafor in his admonition to the Bishop said: “This is deeply concerning to many who believe that the Church should remain a beacon of peace, humility, discipline, and reconciliation. At this critical juncture, I respectfully urge you (Ibezim) to allow the sleeping dog to lie. As a father in the faith and a senior priest in God’s vineyard, you have a responsibility not only to defend your position but also to preserve the unity, dignity, and progress of the Church. No personal disagreement, however serious, should be permitted to overshadow the spiritual mission of the institution we all cherish.

“Your Grace, leadership also entails teaching younger clergy how to respect constituted authority, obey lawful directives, and pursue disagreements through established ecclesiastical channels. The Church cannot effectively preach obedience, humility, and submission if its leaders appear unwilling to model these virtues when tested by difficult circumstances. Equally important, an investigation is not a declaration of guilt. It is a process for establishing facts, examining allegations, and arriving at an informed conclusion. The presumption of innocence must be respected, but so must legitimate investigative processes. Allowing an impartial investigation to proceed should not be interpreted as an admission of wrongdoing; rather, it can demonstrate confidence in the truth and commitment to institutional accountability. You have an opportunity to demonstrate such statesmanship by stepping back from confrontation, allowing due process to prevail, and creating room for genuine reconciliation.”

World.title: Farm attack: Family provides update on Donovan Marx’s condition
World.content:
The family of North West cattle farmer Donovan Marx have provided an update on his recovery following a brutal farm attack. Image: Facebook

WARNING: This article contains graphic descriptions of violence and injuries that some readers may find disturbing. Reader discretion is advised.

The family of North West cattle farmer Donovan Marx have provided an update on his recovery following a brutal farm attack in which his ears were cut off, he was shot in the back and stabbed in the thigh.

Marx, 50, was attacked on his farm between Potchefstroom and Ventersdorp on Wednesday, 28 October.



In an update shared by DA MP Ian Cameron, the family confirmed that Marx had undergone surgery and was stable in the Critical Care unit at Mediclinic Potchefstroom.

His pain has improved, but his injuries remain serious.

The family also appealed for privacy while Marx continues receiving treatment and police investigate the attack.

Family corrects false claims about injuries

Cameron said he wanted to correct misinformation circulating about the attack, particularly claims that Marx had been castrated or that an attempt had been made to castrate him.

The family confirmed that these claims were completely false.

According to the latest information provided to Cameron, one of Marx’s kidneys was injured during the attack but was saved during surgery. His ears were cut off and he was stabbed in the thigh.



Cameron warned against sharing unverified information, saying false claims mislead the public and disregard the family’s privacy.

What happened during the farm attack?

The attackers reportedly struck shortly after Marx’s wife, Louise, left for work in Ventersdorp shortly before 08:00.

The assailants allegedly tied up a farmworker before turning on Marx.

The worker later managed to free himself and raise the alarm. He escaped without injuries.

Marx was shot in the back and stabbed in the leg, while his ears were cut off during the assault.

Paramedics rushed him to Mediclinic Potchefstroom, where he underwent surgery.

His attackers fled in his red Isuzu bakkie.

An alert was issued at approximately 11:40, warning motorists to look out for the stolen vehicle and not to confront the suspects, who were believed to be armed.

Community rallies around the Marx family

Following news of the attack, members of the Ventersdorp and Potchefstroom communities rallied around the family.

A prayer gathering was held outside Mediclinic Potchefstroom on Wednesday evening as residents came together to pray for Marx’s recovery.

In their latest statement, Louise and the family expressed gratitude to both communities, emergency and medical personnel, the South African Police Service (SAPS) and everyone who had offered prayers and support.

Their message was that their greatest wish was for Marx to receive the rest, treatment and opportunity he needs to recover.

Family asks public to respect privacy and investigation

The family has asked members of the public to respect restrictions on hospital visits and avoid unnecessary calls or requests for medical details.

They also urged anyone with relevant information about the attack to provide it directly to SAPS or the family’s authorised legal representatives.

The family cautioned against circulating speculation or sharing information that could interfere with potential evidence.

Freedom Front Plus leader Corné Mulder previously condemned the attack and called for stronger measures to protect farming communities.

South African UFC fighter Dricus du Plessis also reacted to the horrific attack, by reposting a message calling for action.

On his Instagram Stories, Du Plessis reposted several videos and posts about the news.

North West police spokesperson Captain Majang Skalkie had earlier confirmed that police were investigating the incident, with further details expected once the relevant information had been gathered.

As at the time of publishing, no arrests have been confirmed.

World.title: Eastern Cape gets major R416 million cancer treatment boost
World.content:
A R416m oncology centre in Mthatha is bringing radiotherapy and other specialised cancer treatments closer to patients in the Eastern Cape. Image: canva

Cancer patients in the Eastern Cape will have improved access to specialised treatment following the opening of a R416 million oncology centre at Nelson Mandela Academic Hospital in Mthatha.

The new facility brings chemotherapy, radiotherapy, brachytherapy and specialised inpatient care closer to patients who previously had to travel long distances to access some forms of cancer treatment.

The centre will particularly benefit patients from the OR Tambo, Alfred Nzo, Chris Hani and Joe Gqabi districts.



Patients previously had to travel for radiotherapy in the Eastern Cape

Before the new centre opened, patients requiring radiotherapy at Nelson Mandela Academic Hospital had to be referred to oncology centres in KuGompo City and Gqeberha.

This meant some patients had to travel significant distances and spend extended periods away from their families while undergoing treatment.

The new facility is expected to reduce the need for this travel by bringing a wider range of specialised oncology services to Mthatha.



68 beds for inpatient treatment

The state-of-the-art centre is equipped with two linear accelerator (LINAC) machines, which are used to deliver radiotherapy treatment.

It also has 68 dedicated inpatient beds, comprising:

Beds Number Female oncology patients 30 Male oncology patients 30 Paediatric and neonatal oncology 8

The facility also includes an outpatient department with consultation rooms, counselling facilities and resuscitation capacity.



A dedicated oncology pharmacy has been included, with areas for chemotherapy mixing and dispensing.

The centre includes dedicated areas for chemotherapy treatment, as well as isolation rooms and procedure and treatment rooms.

There are also nursing stations, patient holding areas and recovery facilities designed to support patients throughout their treatment.



A suspended link bridge connects the new oncology centre to the existing hospital.

This provides access to supporting services including radiology, laboratories, theatres and the Central Sterile Services Department.

The provincial government said the building has been designed with future expansion in mind.



The structure can accommodate two additional floors, allowing the facility to expand as demand for specialised cancer treatment grows.

World.title: Former Springbok coach Nick Mallett turns 70
World.content:
Former Springbok and national team coach Nick Mallett celebrates his 70th birthday today, Friday, 30 October. Image: Famous Faces

Former Springbok and national team coach Nick Mallett celebrates his 70th birthday today, Friday, 30 October, marking a milestone for one of South African rugby’s most recognisable figures.

Mallett enjoyed a playing career with Western Province – and the Springboks – before making his mark as a coach, leading South Africa through one of the most successful periods in their history.

READ | Here’s which schools the latest six uncapped Springboks attended



Studied at UCT

Born Nicholas Vivian Hayward Mallett in Haileybury in Hertfordshire in England, on 30 October 1956, he attended St Andrew’s School in Grahamstown before beginning his rugby career.

He was called up to the Western Province Currie Cup team while studying at the University of Cape Town in the late 1970s.

In 1979, he moved to Oxford University, where he earned rugby and cricket Blues. He also made headlines in a friendly cricket match against Somerset when he reportedly hit England great Ian Botham for three sixes in one over.



After returning to South Africa, Mallett continued playing for Western Province.

Two Springbok Test appearances

Nick Mallett was part of the Western Province team that won three consecutive Currie Cup titles between 1982 and 1985.

His performances earned him a call-up to the Springboks, and he made his Test debut against South America at Loftus Versfeld in Pretoria on 20 October 1984.



Playing at eighthman, Mallett scored a try in South Africa’s 32-15 victory.

He earned his second and final Springbok cap a week later, on 27 October 1984, when the teams met at Newlands in Cape Town. The Springboks won that encounter 22-13.

Mallett finished his international playing career with two Test appearances and one try.



He is Springbok No 541.

From club rugby in France to the Springboks

Nick Mallett’s coaching career began in France, where he spent five seasons playing for and coaching St Claude in the Jura Mountains.

He later moved to Boulogne-Billancourt in Paris before returning to South Africa in 1994.



His first coaching role back home was with False Bay Rugby Club. He subsequently took charge of the Boland Cavaliers, guiding the team to a narrow defeat in the Currie Cup quarter-finals.

After two seasons with Boland, Mallett joined the Springbok coaching staff as an assistant in 1996.

He took over as head coach the following year, succeeding after a difficult period for South African rugby that included a series defeat to the British and Irish Lions and a disappointing Tri-Nations campaign.



Record-breaking Springbok era

Nick Mallett quickly transformed the Springboks’ fortunes.

Under his leadership, South Africa equalled the world record of 17 consecutive Test victories and won the Tri-Nations title.

However, his tenure ended on a disappointing note at the 1999 Rugby World Cup.



The campaign was also overshadowed by Mallett’s decision to leave out captain Gary Teichmann, following a reported falling-out between the pair.

In 2000, Mallett publicly criticised the South African Rugby Union over ticket prices, accusing the organisation of greed.

He subsequently resigned while facing a hearing over charges of bringing the game into disrepute.



In total, Mallett coached the Springboks in 38 Tests, winning 27 and losing 11 for a win-percentage of 71.1%.

Success in France and Italy

Nick Mallett returned to France, taking charge of Stade Français in 2000.

The club went on to win consecutive French Top 14 titles in 2003 and 2004 under his leadership.



He returned to Western Province in 2004, this time as director of rugby.

In 2007, Mallett was appointed head coach of Italy’s national team.

He took charge of his first Six Nations campaign in 2008. Although Italy managed only one victory, Mallett was credited with helping develop a team seeking to become more competitive at international level.



His career across South Africa, France and Italy established him as one of the most experienced coaches in the international game.

Nick Mallett shares a birthday with a number of fellow Springboks, including Paul Roos (deceased), Phil Mostert (deceased), Alan Menter (80) and Wian du Preez (44).

World.title: The Olympics could be coming to Durban
World.content:
Durban has just taken a huge step towards hosting the Olympics. Image: canva

Durban has been selected as the preferred host city for South Africa’s ambitious bid to bring the Olympic and Paralympic Games to Africa for the first time.

The coastal city will spearhead the country’s bid for either the 2036 or 2040 Games, with Moses Mabhida Stadium expected to play a central role if South Africa’s plans are successful.

The announcement was made by the South African Sports Confederation and Olympic Committee (SASCOC) on Thursday, 29 October, following Cabinet approval of the country’s Olympic bid.



However, the proposed Games would not be confined to just Durban.

Durban could host up to 70% of the OLYMPIC GAMES

SASCOC acting president Lwandile Simelane said around 60% to 70% of the Olympic programme could potentially be staged in Durban.

The city would also host the proposed Olympic Village, with the opening and closing ceremonies held in Durban.

“Durban as the host city will then be the home of the Olympic Village, as well as the opening and closing ceremonies,” Simelane said.

The plan is to use existing infrastructure wherever possible, while limiting the travel required by athletes and spectators.

Moses Mabhida Stadium, which was built for the 2010 FIFA World Cup, would be at the heart of the proposed Games.



Cape Town and Johannesburg could also host events

Although Durban has been selected as the preferred host city, South Africa’s Olympic bid would be a national effort.

Cape Town and Johannesburg had also put themselves forward as potential host cities, and could host events that cannot be accommodated in Durban.

Certain sports would naturally require different venues or locations.

Surfing and sailing, for example, would require suitable coastal facilities, while other Olympic disciplines could make use of infrastructure already available in Johannesburg or Cape Town.

SASCOC says the aim would nevertheless be to keep the Games compact rather than creating a situation where athletes and spectators have to travel extensively around the country.

“We need to ensure that we do not create a fragmented Games and that it is compact, and that athletes are not expected to be all over the show, as well as spectators, to experience the Games,” Simelane said.

South Africa faces major competition

South Africa is now one of seven countries interested in hosting the 2036 Olympics. According to SASCOC chief executive Nozipho Jafta, the other interested countries are:

Country 2036 interest South Africa Yes Germany Yes Hungary Yes India Yes Qatar Yes South Korea Yes Turkey Yes

All seven countries have been invited to present their cases to the International Olympic Committee (IOC) at the end of November.

The presentations will give each prospective host an opportunity to outline its plans and explain why it should progress to the next stage of the process.

Interest is also emerging for the 2040 Games, with Germany, Poland, Egypt and the United Kingdom among countries that have indicated potential interest.

While Durban’s selection represents a major step for South Africa, it does not mean the city has been awarded the Games.

There is still a lengthy bidding and evaluation process ahead before the IOC makes a final decision.

SASCOC has already acknowledged that major questions need to be addressed, including the cost of hosting the Games, the availability of existing sporting facilities and the country’s public transport infrastructure.

The bid has an exploratory value of around R500 billion, although that figure should not be interpreted as a confirmed final cost of hosting the Games.

SASCOC is expected to present South Africa’s case to the IOC’s Future Host Commission in November, with further feasibility work and evaluation to follow.

The final host decision is expected in 2029.

World.title: SA to keep buying chickens from Brazil despite disease outbreak
World.content:
South Africa will not impose a blanket ban on poultry imports from Brazil despite an outbreak of Newcastle disease. Image: Wikimedia Commons

South Africa will not impose a blanket ban on poultry imports from Brazil despite an outbreak of Newcastle disease in the Brazilian state of Santa Catarina.

The Department of Agriculture says imports will continue under strict veterinary certification requirements designed to protect the country’s animal and public health.

serious consequences

Newcastle disease is a highly contagious viral infection that primarily affects wild birds and domestic poultry.



Outbreaks can have serious consequences for poultry producers and the wider agricultural industry.

However, South Africa says its existing import protocols with Brazil are designed to prevent infected poultry products from entering the country.

#DoAUpdate | SOUTH AFRICA’S RESPONSE TO NEWCASTLE DISEASE OUTBREAK IN BRAZIL



Brazil notified South Africa on 20 October 2026 of an outbreak of Newcastle disease in the state of Santa Catarina.



Following an assessment of the notification, South Africa will not impose a… pic.twitter.com/TbYneHIK8g — National Department of Agriculture (@DOAgov_ZA) October 28, 2026

Strict controls on Brazilian poultry imports

The department’s Chief Director for Animal Production and Health, Dr Botlhe Modisane, says Brazil is prohibited from exporting chicken or poultry from facilities affected by Newcastle disease.

He explained that the restrictions also extend to areas surrounding infected facilities.

“The import protocol of poultry between South Africa and Brazil is such that Brazil is prohibited from exporting chicken or poultry from facilities that are infected with Newcastle disease,” Modisane said.



“They also have to ensure that around a certain radius, over 10 kilometres, there haven’t been any reports of Newcastle disease in those facilities.”

According to Modisane, these requirements are intended to exclude the possibility of Newcastle disease being imported into South Africa through poultry trade.

No blanket import ban

The department’s position means poultry imports from Brazil can continue, provided exporters comply with the required veterinary certification and disease-control measures.

Rather than suspending all imports from the country, South Africa is relying on restrictions that prevent poultry from affected facilities and surrounding areas from being exported.

The approach allows trade to continue while maintaining safeguards against the introduction of the disease.

The department has emphasised that the existing protocols are designed to protect South Africa’s poultry industry and animal health.

World.title: RIP | ‘Star Trek’, ‘X-Men’ star Patrick Stewart dies aged 86
World.content:
Patrick Stewart, the British Shakespearean actor who became a Hollywood megastar through roles in the "Star Trek" and "X-Men" franchises, has died. Image: PATRICK BAZ / AFP

Patrick Stewart, the British Shakespearean actor who became a Hollywood megastar through roles in the “Star Trek” and “X-Men” franchises, has died at his home in Los Angeles. He was 86.

His death on Wednesday came after a “brief and poignant journey” with Alzheimer’s disease and Lewy body dementia, according to an official statement on his social media accounts.

“His sonorous voice and singular talent will forever be synonymous with indelible performances in every genre,” the statement said.



Topped pop culture history books

The actor, who hailed from the northern English region of Yorkshire, trod the boards in Britain with the Royal Shakespeare Company and the National Theatre in London, and worked on British television.

But he rocketed into the pop culture history books in his mid-40s when he was cast as Captain Jean-Luc Picard in “Star Trek: The Next Generation,” and then again as Professor Charles Xavier in multiple “X-Men” and related Marvel films.

A proud Yorkshireman, Stewart “wore his heart on his sleeve, which made him a man to rely on, to admire and in my case, love,” Ian McKellan said of his “X-Men” co-star and dear friend.

McKellan, 87, recounted meeting Stewart in London and hearing about his “Star Trek” offer, warning him he may get lost in Hollywood and to think of his stage career.

“Well, he took the risk and thank goodness for us all that he did.”

Aboard the Enterprise

Patrick Stewart was 47 when he debuted as Picard in “Star Trek: The Next Generation,” the first live-action television spinoff of the trailblazing late-1960s sci-fi series.



He effectively filled the boots of William Shatner’s Captain Kirk – to resounding success, both in the TV series and in several films.

Picard became known for a few catchphrases including “Make it so” and “Engage!”

But his move to America in 1987 was initially greeted with disdain by the Los Angeles Times, who wrote him off as an “unknown British Shakespearean actor.”

Stewart later dubbed suggestions he was “slumming it” by moving into US television offensive.

He once called his Shakespearean bona fides “nothing but a preparation for sitting in the captain’s chair of the Enterprise.”

‘Colossus of both stage and screen’

Patrick Stewart found further acclaim in the “X-Men” series, debuting in 2000 as Professor Charles Xavier, the founder and mentor of the mutant superhero team.

“For more than 25 years, he brought a gravitas and profundity to the role, earning fans across the globe,” Marvel Studios said on Thursday.

Longtime co-star Hugh Jackman, who played Wolverine, remembered Stewart as both “one of the greats of stage and screen” and “a tremendous friend and man.”

Stewart is to make his final on-screen film appearance as Professor Xavier in “Avengers: Doomsday,” set for release in December.

“What a heartbreaking week it has been,” posted Shatner.

Stewart’s death marked the second in days from the “Star Trek” universe, following that of Walter Koenig, who played Chekov in the original series.

Shatner said Stewart – who most recently played Picard in 2023 – brought “intelligence, grace and a deep sense of humanity to everything he did.”

Stewart earned four Emmy nominations but never won. He did nab a spoken word Grammy, for his narration of “Prokofiev: Peter And The Wolf.”

And even as he found success in Hollywood, Stewart’s love of theater, and the bard in particular, never left him.

Between filming, he would return to the stage, winning two Olivier awards.

Shakespeare, Stewart said, “feels like a friend, someone who just went out of the room to get another bottle of wine.”

The Royal Shakespeare Company called him “a colossus of both stage and screen and one of the finest classical Shakespearean actors of his generation.”

Troubled start

Patrick Stewart was born on July 13, 1940 in the small West Yorkshire town of Mirfield, the third of three brothers in a working-class family.

His father, back from World War II and perhaps suffering from PTSD, would often beat Stewart’s mother – which prompted Stewart to later work with the charity Refuge, which specializes in domestic abuse.

The actor left school at 15, and studied at Bristol Old Vic Drama School beginning in 1957, making his professional acting debut two years later.

Prematurely balding, Stewart missed out on many of the young romantic leads but quickly slotted into theater life, joining the RSC in 1966 and staying there until 1982.

Any misgivings Stewart had about taking the Picard role in the “Star Trek” universe were mollified by the thought it would be a one-season failure.

He was wrong.

“It changed my life,” he said.

Knighted in 2010, Patrick Stewart married three times: to Sheila Falconer, with whom he had two children; briefly to “Star Trek” producer Wendy Neuss; and most recently to American singer Sunny Ozell, 38 years his junior.

By Garrin Lambley © Agence France-Presse

World.title: Andrea Johnson, Feroz Khan arrested
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Former Independent Directorate Against Corruption (IDAC) head Andrea Johnson and former Crime Intelligence boss Feroz Khan have been arrested.

eNCA understands the pair face charges relating to defeating the ends of justice. Their arrest warrants were authorised on Thursday.

Khan was dismissed from the police service, while Johnson resigned as IDAC head in July following damaging testimony at the Madlanga Commission of Inquiry.

According to police, Khan’s dismissal followed his failure to appear before the designated senior officer overseeing his disciplinary process.

During proceedings at the Madlanga Commission, it emerged that Johnson and Khan shared a close personal relationship that extended beyond their professional roles.

They will be appearing in the Pretoria Magistrate's Court.

World.title: Western Cape police threaten taxi rank shutdown amid rising violence
World.content:
CAPE TOWN - Western Cape Police Commissioner Sizakhele Dyantyi has warned taxi operators that ranks could be shut down if violence continues, following a deadly month in which at least 12 people have been killed in taxi-related incidents.

Dyantyi issued the warning after an urgent meeting between police leadership and the City of Cape Town’s safety officials to develop a coordinated response to escalating violence ahead of next week’s local government elections.

The proposed interventions include increased police deployments, drones, licence plate recognition technology and the use of the city’s extensive CCTV network to identify and apprehend those responsible.

Dyantyi says authorities will take decisive action against those involved in the violence, including shutting down taxi ranks if necessary.

The City of Cape Town’s Safety and Security Commissioner, Johan Brand, says the municipality will support SAPS through increased deployments and stricter enforcement of transport legislation and traffic by-laws.

Meanwhile, the Independent Electoral Commission says it is working with law enforcement and the city to ensure voting stations, election officials and voters are protected.

Western Cape IEC chief electoral officer Michael Hendrickse says preparations are largely on track, although the commission is still awaiting ballot papers following a Constitutional Court decision that required them to be reprinted.

He remains confident that all materials will be in place ahead of the special votes scheduled for Monday.

World.title: India's animal megacentre vows reset after criticism
World.content:
JAMNAGAR - Behind guarded gates resembling an Indian maharajah's palace are hundreds of elephants and big cats, giraffes grazing in a mock savannah, and chimpanzees and orangutans swinging from ropes.

This is Vantara: billed as the world's biggest animal rescue centre, but also the target of persistent criticism over how it amassed an unprecedented collection, including critically endangered animals.

After years of scrutiny, including a Supreme Court-ordered probe in its favour, the Indian centre has pledged a reset, saying it has halted imports, hired global experts, and shifted towards helping wildlife in its natural habitat.

"Vantara has pivoted," CEO Vivaan Karani told AFP. "Wherever animals can be effectively supported in their own countries, we increasingly believe our resources should travel, rather than the animals."

The centre in Jamnagar, in India's western Gujarat state, is closed to the public.

AFP was granted rare access for a two-day tour, passing expansive glass-fronted enclosures housing some of the 200 lions, 200 cheetahs and 150 tigers.

Meaning "Star of the Forest", Vantara in August pledged to "respond to criticism through dialogue, transparency and evidence -- not litigation".

The centre is the vision of 31-year-old Anant Ambani, youngest son of one of Asia's richest men Mukesh Ambani, chairman of retail-to-refining giant Reliance Industries.

It spans 1,416 hectares across multiple sites -- around 2,000 football pitches -- alongside a Reliance oil refinery, the world's biggest.

Over 260 former working elephants wander through teak plantations, trumpeting as they bathe in lakes.

World.title: Crypto platform Binance confirms major hack, more than $2.5bn frozen
World.content:
BEIJING - Cryptocurrency platform Binance said it had fallen victim to a major hack and indicated that more than $2.5 billion in funds had been frozen in an effort to prevent a massive theft.

The company -- the world's largest crypto exchange by daily trading volumes -- posted a series of sometimes contradictory messages on X, insisting that "user funds are completely safe" but also saying it would "cover all losses."

The scope of the heist was not immediately known, but blockchain analytics company Chainalysis said its "current estimate on amount stolen is approx $5.912B at time of theft."

That would be almost four times the amount stolen in what has been the biggest-ever cyberattack of its kind to date: $1.5 billion taken in February 2025 from the Bybit platform -- an incident attributed to hackers affiliated with North Korea.

At about 0030 GMT Friday, Binance said all deposits and withdrawals had been "temporarily suspended while our team conducts security checks, freezes funds, and works with law enforcement."

"This figure may continue to increase as our teams work closely with law enforcement, issuers, blockchain intelligence firms and industry partners to trace and freeze additional assets," the company said.

Neither the company nor industry observers offered any explanation as to how the cyberattack might have occurred.

"It does look like a hack on Binance," said former Binance chief Changpeng Zhao, who no longer runs the group but remains a majority shareholder.

He estimated that the total losses could be "a bit higher" than $1 billion.

Paolo Ardoino, the CEO of Tether -- a company that issues a cryptocurrency known as USDT -- said his firm froze about $1.6 billion "related to a potential Binance exchange hack."

Circle boss Jeremy Allaire said his company had frozen more than $800 million in USDC.

USDT and USDC are both "stablecoins," or digital currencies whose value is linked to a traditional currency, the US dollar.

The US Department of Justice and the FBI did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

- Crypto prices tumble -

For several hours before Binance confirmed the attack, several industry observers said hackers had managed to reach the platform.

The prices of most major cryptocurrencies fell on the news, except for the stablecoins, which by definition can only fluctuate within tight margins.

At about 0025 GMT, bitcoin had lost nearly five percent, Ethereum fell nearly six percent, and BNB, native to Binance, tumbled nearly 10 percent.

The cyberattack on Binance comes as many observers express worries that the ever-expanding capabilities of artificial intelligence (AI) models could compromise cryptography and IT security protocols.

World.title: Charity crowdfunds millions to buy historic English estate
World.content:
LONDON - A leading UK conservation charity announced it had raised some £30 million ($40 million) via crowdfunding to buy a huge swathe of rolling moorlands and forests to transform into a sanctuary for biodiversity.

After an intense two-year campaign, the Wildlife Trusts has purchased the whole 3,800-hectares of the Rothbury Estate in northern Northumberland, England's largest land acquisition in three decades.

The purchase of the sprawling site, as large as central London, will be the opportunity "to create something very special for generations to come", said renowned environmentalist David Attenborough, who backed the campaign.

The trusts' director general Craig Bennett thanked the thousands of people who had donated to the campaign.

"Working alongside local communities, farmers and fellow land managers who know and care for this landscape so deeply, we can help this special place continue to thrive," he added in a statement.

Some £17 million towards the cost of the land was donated by 25,000 individuals.

The estate was sold by the Percy family -- the Dukes of Northumberland -- who had owned it for almost eight centuries, using the land until 2022 for grouse shooting.

The current duke's son, Max Percy, said it was too difficult to manage from his home in southern England, and after putting it up for sale in 2023 agreed to give the Wildlife Trusts two years to raise the funds.

The association also received £5 million from the National Lottery Heritage Fund, which finances projects to protect UK heritage, as well as a pledge of £1.94 million from the Department of Environment.

Bordered by several nature reserves and restoration project areas, the Wildlife Trusts and owners of those sites dream of one day creating a 65-kilometre-long biodiversity corridor stretching inland from the estate by the North Sea.

It would provide a much-needed sanctuary for wildlife, such as cuckoos, butterflies, pine martens and golden eagles as well as red squirrels, in the densely-populated, nature-ravaged UK.

The Wildlife Trusts also want to encourage the dozen farmers, mainly keeping sheep, to adopt more environmentally friendly practices, using fewer pesticides and chemical fertilisers.

The UK government is far from its objective to conserve and manage 30 percent of its land and seas for nature by 2030. According to the Wildlife Trusts, the acquisition of the Rothbury Estate could help it meet its goal.

World.title: Russell admits absence of rivalry because he cannot match Antonelli
World.content:
MEXICO CITY - George Russell admitted that his "great relationship" with teammate and title rival Kimi Antonelli had not suffered this year because he has been unable to match his on-track performances.

Antonelli (20) is poised to become Formula One's youngest champion and first Italian since 1953 by finishing ninth or better in Sunday's Mexico City Grand Prix, leaving pre-season title favourite Russell, 28, in a scrap for second place.

The pair have not clashed in races as many previous championship rivals have done, resulting in a breakdown in personal relations and the creation of bitter rivalries as infamously exemplified by four-time champion Alain Prost and three-time champion Ayrton Senna at McLaren in the late 1980s.

Russell said: "On a personal level, Kimi's obviously a great guy and has lots of energy... And we've had no reason this year not to continue to have a great relationship.

"I think a lot of these on-track rivalries start because of on-track incidents or actions and the truth is that he has been at a higher level than me this year.

"So, we've not been in that situation too often. We have had one or two races... But when it comes to the race itself, we sort of keep ourselves to ourselves and work with our individual engineers to try and get the most out of it."

Russell is 123 points adrift of Antonelli in the drivers' title race ahead of this weekend's race at the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez, one point ahead of former team-mate and seven-time champion Lewis Hamilton of Ferrari.

He is due to give up his seat in Friday's opening free practice to Mercedes team test driver Frederik Vesti, giving Antonelli an early advantage if the Italian recovers from a virus to take part.

Russell added that it would mean little to him to finish as runner-up to Antonelli in the title race.

"I think for every driver on the grid, there's only one position that matters and it's P1. To be best of the rest is not really something you dream of as a kid," he said.

"Of course, I want to finish as high as possible. I want to win as many races as possible.

"But what's more important to me is to finish the season on a positive momentum rather than necessarily that final order."

World.title: Suliman Carrim faces additional charge in vehicle smuggling case
World.content:
MUSINA - North West businessman Suliman Carrim is expected to face an additional charge when he appears in the Musina Magistrate’s Court on Friday.

He is expected to be charged with contravening the Immigration Act for allegedly employing a foreign national illegally. The charge will be added to his existing charges as he prepares to apply for bail in the attempted vehicle theft case.

Carrim faces charges of attempted theft, fraud and money laundering in connection with the alleged attempted smuggling of bank-financed vehicles across the border.

READ | Suliman Carrim granted R100k bail in Madlanga case

The case relates to an incident at the Beitbridge border post on 22 July 2026, when police intercepted two vehicles being transported from Mahikeng in the North West to Malawi.

Carrim and his two co-accused allegedly attempted to obtain bank authorisation documents to facilitate the vehicles’ movement across the border. However, the required authorisation was not granted.

The 49-year-old businessman was arrested by the Commission’s Recommendations Task Team (CRTT) on 15 October, shortly before he was due to board a flight to the United Arab Emirates.

On Thursday, he was granted R100,000 bail in a separate case linked to the Madlanga Commission of Inquiry.

World.title: Former pupils unite to preserve Pax College's 98-year legacy
World.content:
GA-MASHASHANE - Founded in 1928 by the Catholic Brothers of Charity, Pax College in Ga-Mashashane, about 30 kilometres outside Polokwane, has a proud legacy of providing educational opportunities to children from disadvantaged communities.

Its alumni include South African Reserve Bank Governor Lesetja Kganyago, Father Smangaliso Mkhatshwa and NPA spokesperson Kaizer Kganyago.

Now, former pupils are joining forces to restore the school’s former glory through the Make Pax Great fundraising initiative, aimed at improving its ageing infrastructure and providing much-needed resources.

Kganyago says the school lost many of its donors after apartheid and was subsequently absorbed by the Limpopo Department of Education.
