World.title: Iraqi pharmacy sets Guinness World Record with 79,069 hydration pledges
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Iraq has achieved a Guinness World Records title after Haya Pharmacy’s “Ghaith” hydration awareness campaign collected 79,069 pledges in one month, encouraging people across the country to adopt healthier water-drinking habits.

The initiative, which broke the record in Baghdad on October 5, 2026, got the highest pledges for a hydration awareness campaign in a single month.

The campaign, which was created in partnership with the Ebers marketing team, integrated community participation and public health awareness efforts to encourage regular water intake.

The campaign was strategically driven from Dubai, with teams from Ebers and Haya Pharmacy overseeing its execution on the ground in Iraq.

The success marks a significant milestone for Haya Pharmacy’s public health programs, demonstrating the effectiveness of national awareness campaigns in promoting better lives and community engagement.

World.title: Iraq signs agreement with Swiss pharma giant Roche
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Swiss pharmaceutical manufacturer Roche has inked a strategic partnership deal with Iraq’s Ministry of Health to strengthen healthcare services, with a focus on ophthalmology and hemophilia A.

In Baghdad, Swiss Ambassador Peter Nelson and officials from Roche and the Iraqi Health Ministry attended the signing of the agreement.

The partnership’s goal is to enhance patient care by strengthening diagnostic capacities, introducing sophisticated medical technology, and providing specialized training for Iraqi healthcare personnel.

Roche also reiterated its long-standing commitment to Iraq’s healthcare sector, emphasizing the necessity of working with government institutions to provide access to breakthrough therapies and medical knowledge.

The company thanked Iraqi Health Minister Dr. Abdul Hussein Al-Mousawi for his support of foreign pharmaceutical companies and recognition of the significance of intellectual property protection in promoting medical innovation.

The arrangement is part of an attempt to modernize Iraq’s healthcare system and provide access to specialized medical services.

World.title: Maserati expands Iraq presence with new automotive partner
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Italian luxury carmaker Maserati has appointed Tiraz Automotive and Service Group as its new official partner in Iraq, aiming to strengthen its presence and expand customer access to the brand.

The deal was inked on September 18 in Modena, Italy, during a meeting between Maserati personnel and a Tiraz team headed by Kambiz Fathibitaraf.

Maserati hopes that the relationship would allow it to grow its operations in Iraq and provide consumers with a more personalized ownership experience, including access to its Fuoriserie customization program.

Customers may personalize their automobiles with various colors, materials, and design features that suit their specific interests.

The appointment is part of Maserati’s strategy to expand its presence in the Iraqi luxury automobile market and increase its local customer base.

World.title: Iraq signs gas capture agreement with US firm Morgan Hughes
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – US-based Morgan Hughes Energy has signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) with Iraq’s General Company for Carbon Economics (GCCE) to develop projects aimed at capturing and utilizing associated gas currently flared at oil production sites across Iraq.

The agreement was signed in Baghdad by Morgan Hughes Energy Managing Director Gregory Bloom and GCCE, under the patronage of Iraq’s Minister of Environment, Sarwa Abdulwahid, and in the presence of US Chargé d’Affaires Steven Fagin.

The proposed partnership will focus on recovering low-pressure associated gas and using it to generate electricity for oil production facilities, reducing gas flaring and reliance on Iraq’s national electricity grid.

The initiative also aims to develop carbon credit projects using internationally recognized monitoring and verification standards, creating potential revenue opportunities through carbon markets while supporting Iraq’s emissions reduction targets.

Morgan Hughes Energy said it plans to bring American expertise and technology to the projects, supporting Iraq’s energy security and hydrocarbon development.

The company operates in the upstream and midstream oil and gas sectors, with interests across the Middle East, including offshore gas production, pipeline infrastructure, and gas storage facilities.

The MoU represents an initial step towards a broader strategic partnership between the two companies, with specific projects still subject to further development.

World.title: Iraq to issue licenses for digital banks in early 2028
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) confirmed on Wednesday that final approvals for the establishment of digital banks will be issued in early 2028.

The spokesperson for the CBI, Mahmoud Dagher, told the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA) that final permissions for digital banking licenses will be granted after the banking reform phase is complete, by the end of 2027 or the start of 2028.

Oliver Wyman is presently leading the banking reform process, and organizations that sought to establish digital banks and gained preliminary permissions are aware of the timescale for gaining final authorizations, according to Dagher.

In October 2025, the CBI has received approximately 80 applications to create digital banks in the country.

Licenses can only be awarded following a set of criteria based on market research, the nature of the business, and other countries’ experiences, where the number of digital banks is often limited to three or four.

Earlier in 2025, officials from the CBI and representatives from Oliver Wyman discussed a banking reform proposal offered by the Iraqi Private Banks League (IPBL) to modernize Iraq’s banking industry and align operations with worldwide practices.

The strategy aims to stabilize the banking sector to function more securely and effectively, as well as local legislation, while strengthening governance, compliance, and risk management.

The CBI noted that adopting the strategy will boost local and international trust in Iraq’s banking industry.

Iraq’s central bank reached an agreement earlier with Oliver Wyman to perform a thorough analysis of the conditions under which Iraqi banks are prohibited from conducting transactions in US dollars.

Oliver Wyman focuses on improving bank procedures to align with international standards, creating effective strategies to reintegrate Iraqi banks that have been barred from conducting US dollar transactions back into the banking sector, both domestically and internationally.

World.title: Iraq’s Development Road to provide million job opportunities
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The designs for the Development Road project have reached their final stages and will be fully completed before the end of 2026, according to the Iraqi Ministry of Transport.

The spokesperson for the Ministry of Transport, Ali al-Khalidi, said that the Development Road project is expected to generate approximately 100,000 job opportunities during its first phase.

Plans include the construction of modern stations, industrial zones, and residential areas along the route, developments that could potentially create over a million jobs as the project and its associated facilities expand, according to al-Khalidi.

The Iraqi official explained that 95 percent of the project’s railway designs have been completed, with 92 percent of the highway designs finished, the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA) reported.

Extending from the al-Faw Grand Port in the southern province of Basra to the Turkish border, with both the highway and railway being parallel lines, the first phase of the project is expected to be completed in 2033.

The Development Road’s primary objective is to transport goods from al-Faw Grans Port to Turkey—and onward to Europe—and vice versa.

Work is currently underway to finalize an agreement with Turkey to establish a fund that would finance the project’s implementation by Turkish companies through an oil-for-financing arrangement, according to INA.

The $17 billion project, which will connect the al-Faw Grand Port in southern Iraq to the Turkish border by constructing a railway and road network, is anticipated to transform Iraq into a transit center by cutting the time it takes to travel from Asia to Europe.

In addition to pipelines for energy transportation, the project’s railway will significantly assist in the transportation of commodities, with a first-phase capacity of 3.5 million tons and a second-phase capacity of 7.5 million tons.

By connecting the port city of Basra to Turkey via an overland route, the logistics project will compete with Egypt’s Suez Canal and establish Basra as a gateway to Europe.

World.title: Norway’s DNO considers exporting Iraqi Kurdistan oil via Syria
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Norwegian oil producer DNO is actively exploring routes through Syria to export its Iraqi Kurdistan crude oil to the Mediterranean.

According to Reuters, the initiative aims to bypass local market constraints and fetch significantly higher international benchmark prices.

DNO has been selling oil from its Tawke and Peshkabir fields to the local market at low prices. Although its domestic sales price increased somewhat to $45 per barrel in October 2026 compared to an average of $38.50 in the third quarter, it is still significantly below global benchmarks.

Due to the Syrian civil war, transport to the Mediterranean through Syria was previously impossible. However, regional logistics are shifting. Significant volumes of southern Iraqi fuel oil and crude are already being transported by tanker trucks directly through Syria for export.

Reflecting past delays in payments from the Kurdistan Regional Government (KRG), DNO requires international buyers to deposit US dollars into its offshore accounts before any oil is collected.

While trucks would be necessary for short-term movements, long-term solutions would encounter infrastructural obstacles.

Despite prior political support from the United States to study the route, rebuilding a key Iraq-Syria oil pipeline may cost around $15 billion and take years to become fully operational.

DNO is stepping up its drilling operations to increase the gross output from its important Kurdish licenses, which averaged 77,621 barrels of oil per day in the third quarter of 2026.

World.title: Iraq, Syria discuss exporting two million bpd of oil via Baniyas
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi and Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa discussed on Wednesday the development of economic and security cooperation, particularly the export of Iraqi oil through Baniyas with a capacity up to two million barrels per day.

The discussions took place during the first visit by an Iraqi prime minister to Syria since the fall of Bashar al-Assad’s regime in late 2024. The visit marks a step toward strengthening relations between the two countries, which share a border stretching over 600 kilometers.

The Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) said in a statement that the meeting addressed increasing trade exchange and developing the agricultural sector to achieve food and economic integration, in addition to discussing oil exports via Syria’s Baniyas port.

However, the statement did not mention when the route will start operating at the specified capacity.

Al-Zaidi highlighted initiatives to develop partnerships in the social and economic domains, boost security cooperation, and coordinate stances on regional and global concerns.

The Syrian Presidency said that the extended discussions in Damascus covered approaches to promote security, economic, and commercial cooperation, as well as regional and international developments.

Iraq started earlier exporting limited quantities of oil through the Syrian port of Baniyas—a move prompted by disruptions of maritime shipping in the Strait of Hormuz amid the conflict in the Middle East.

In July, the two countries signed a memorandum of understanding to revive the Haditha–Baniyas pipeline. A deal was signed with a consortium of three companies, including US-based Chevron, to carry out the project.

The pipeline was built in 1952, but it was abandoned in 2003 due to damage sustained during the invasion of Iraq by the United States. Its reactivation would provide an outlet for Iraqi oil exports via the Mediterranean Sea.

World.title: 'Will serve until my last breath': PM Modi declares in Gujarat - top quotes
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Friday said he would continue serving people until his last breath as he addressed a public event in Gujarat's Banaskantha, where he inaugurated and laid the foundation stone for development projects worth over Rs 14,000 crore.

The Prime Minister spoke about his 25 years in public office, the government's support for farmers amid global uncertainties and the use of technology in agriculture and animal husbandry. He also accused some people of spreading rumours about fertiliser and gas shortages to defame the government.

Here are the key quotes from PM Modi's address:

1. 'I will continue serving people until my last breath'

Referring to his 25 years in public office, PM Modi said, "On October 7, I completed 25 years in public office.

But it feels like just yesterday when I first took the oath of office in October 2001; you showered me with a lot of love."

"I will continue serving people until my last breath," he said.

2. 'Our government did not let fertiliser price rise burden farmers'

Addressing concerns over global uncertainties and tensions in the Gulf, Modi said his government had protected farmers from rising international fertiliser prices.





"Amid global uncertainties, there was a huge jump in the price of fertilisers, but our government, which is dedicated to the welfare of farmers, did not let the burden of this price rise fall on farmers. The government spent Rs 16 lakh crore on this..."

3. 'Some people feel happy when the country faces difficulty'

The Prime Minister accused some people of spreading rumours about shortages of fertilisers and gas amid tensions in the Gulf.

"Today, every youth, sister and daughter is working towards making India a developed nation. But some people do not like this. These are the people who want to see the country in difficulty. They feel happy when they see the country in difficulty. When the nation as one is facing uncertainties emerging due to tensions in the Gulf, they spread rumours about shortages of fertilisers and gas. They wanted to do this only to defame Modi.

I want to remind the farmers and all others that I had said that I would stand by you all. The tensions in the Gulf are still ongoing, but the govt did not let the burden of increased fertiliser prices across the world fall on our farmers..."

4. 'Our government has always prioritised farmers' welfare'

Modi said his government had focused on supporting farmers and empowering them through various initiatives. He said Rs 4.5 lakh crore had been transferred to small farmers under the PM-Kisan Samman Nidhi scheme.

5. 'Agriculture is our culture'

Speaking about the use of technology in agriculture, Modi said the government had connected farming and animal husbandry with technological advancements.

"Agriculture is our culture. We connected farming and animal husbandry with technology. More than 26 crore soil health cards have been availed by farmers today," he said.

6. 'Animal husbandry is an important part of our rural economy'

The Prime Minister also spoke about the contribution of women to the animal husbandry and dairy sectors.

"Animal husbandry is an important part of our rural economy. Our sisters have a very significant participation in it. In the past decade, we have emphasised the use of science and technology in the animal husbandry and dairy sectors as well," he said.

During his visit to the Bharat Bovine Breeding and Research Centre (BBBRC) cattle farm at Bhildi, a group of women chanted, "Modi will not leave" while posing for a photograph with the Prime Minister.

The 127-acre facility has been established as a Centre of Excellence to strengthen bovine breeding, genetic upgradation and advanced reproductive technologies. It is the country's first facility dedicated to the Kankrej cattle breed and is expected to accelerate breed improvement by 10-20 times.

World.title: INDIA bloc postpones 'public impeachment' of CEC Gyanesh Kumar due to rains
World.content:

World.title: Night polo goesmainstream in Jaipur
World.content:
A night polo match underway at the Rambagh Polo Club ground in Jaipur

An Evening At The Polo

In this bastion of the âsport of kingsâ, horse and rider are routinely taking to the field under floodlights, in the hope of drawing a wider audience, building tourism opportunities â and preserving a bit of the cityâs heritage, writes Mandakini Shaly

A Place In The City

Finding Players And Spectators

Later Dinners For The Horses

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Polo in Jaipur has become easier to catch. Matches at the Rambagh Polo Club ground now begin at 7.30pm, giving office-goers time to get there after work and families a chance to watch once the daytime heat has passed.Over the past couple of months, 10 newly installed floodlights have lit up the ground near the Vidhan Sabha and the high court. In a neighbourhood where lights over the Sawai Man Singh Stadium have long signalled IPL season, there is now another reason to stop for a match.The stands have young spectators watching their first game, taking selfies and discovering a sport whose familiar audience has largely been drawn from royal families, the cavalry and club circles. Broad-brimmed hats, pastel linen jackets and chiffon sarees are still in evidence. The club is hoping to give more people a reason to come.Night polo has been played in Hyderabad and Noida, in smaller arenas with sand surfaces. Jaipurâs matches are on a full-sized grass ground, under lights, as part of the official tournament schedule.For Major Anant Rajpurohit of 61 Cavalry, a veteran player, the advantage is straightforward: more people are free to watch.âThe good point is that people tend to get off from work, office, or day commitments, and the attendance is more,â he says.âEarlier, the matches and all the finals were done during the daytime, so the availability of gentlemen and ladies was very restricted and very confined. The development of any sport comes when the number of people watching it is more. Then, the number of people who intend to get into the sport or invest into the sport increases. So that way it is an added advantage,â he says.For Padmanabh Singh, 28, Indiaâs polo captain and scion of the erstwhile Jaipur royal family, encouraging people to watch is also part of keeping a city tradition alive.âI have always viewed polo as very intertwined with the culture of Jaipur,â he says. âJaipur is one of the main hubs of polo across the world and has given a lot to the sport. Some of the most iconic moments have happened here. So when I talk about conservation, restoration, and preservation of our culture and heritage, I mean polo too. Itâs part of our tourism.âRambagh Polo Club is marketing the sport more actively, with support from Rajasthanâs tourism leadership. Padmanabhâs mother, Diya Kumari, is deputy chief minister and tourism minister.Last month, a UAE delegation visited Jaipur to discuss cooperation in polo, horses and tourism. Among its interests was the Marwari, Rajasthanâs indigenous horse breed.âThe Marwari is our local breed here in Rajasthan, and the visiting delegation was incredibly keen to see them. We discussed avenues to encourage a vibrant cultural exchange between the UAE, Rajasthan Tourism, and Rambagh Polo Club. They are very eager to support polo further and bring global visibility to this magnificent breed that has served Rajasthan for centuries,â Padmanabh says.Elsewhere, access to a convenient ground is a concern. Delhi, Maharashtra and West Bengal have active polo circuits, supported by the Army, professional players and corporate patrons. In Delhi, however, Rajpurohit worries that a change of venue will cost the sport spectators and sponsors.âThe finals of all elite tournaments in Delhi used to be at Jaipur Polo Ground, which is in the heart of Delhi,â he says. âUnfortunately, we lost that ground a few months back. Now more matches will be conducted at the Army Polo and Riding Centre. It is a shame that we lost the ground in the heart of Delhi. The number of people who used to attend and sponsor the events were more. Now that number will reduce.âHe sees encouraging signs in the number of younger players taking up the sport.âThe number of horses that have been shipped in every year is increasing. The number of kids who intend to compete in the sport is increasing. Earlier we used to have around four odd teams in Junior National Championship. Now we have six-seven teams,â he adds.Polo remains expensive to take up, though schools are helping introduce children to it.âThere are many schools that are offering the equestrian part and the polo part, like Mayo and Delhi College, and they are coming up very well.âIn Jaipur, demand for lessons already exceeds what the Sawai Man Singh Polo School and Academy can offer.âWith that spirit in mind, a few years ago we started the Sawai Man Singh Polo School and Academy. Itâs the only one of its kind and itâs doing very well. We have 50 students, which is our maximum capacity, and for the last three years, we have had a waiting list,â Padmanabh says.âUnfortunately, we canât accommodate more because we have a limited number of horses, but itâs in the heart of the city and subsidised by the polo club. I donated some of my horses to the academy and I go there all the time to mentor them. Whenever someone is doing well, I pull them out to play with us,â Padmanabh says.Padmanabh says Jaipurâs experience of playing after dark goes back more than a century. He describes a brass night polo ball, with a small candle inside, used by women who played at night.At Rambagh, playing under floodlights requires a change in the horsesâ routine. Matches fall at what would ordinarily be their dinner time.âI would not say that it changes much. We just have to adjust the feeding time. Now, they have to have dinner a little bit later. So we just have to adapt our schedules,â Padmanabh says.The horses, he says, have settled into the later hours without trouble.âWe know that if the horse is not happy, it wonât eat, or it will stop drinking water, or it will stop laying down. None of that happens. In fact, it is better for them because they donât have the heat of the day.â

World.title: Surrender before December 1: Supreme Court cancels bail of expelled JD(U) leader Anant Singh in Dularchand Yadav murder case
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The

on Friday cancelled the bail granted to expelled JD(U) MLA

in the murder case of Dularchand Yadav and directed him to surrender before the authorities on or before December 1, 2026.

A bench of Justices MM Sundresh and PV Varale observed that the Patna High Court had erred in granting Singh bail without adequately considering the nature of the offence and his criminal antecedents. The top court suspended the High Court's order and cancelled the relief granted to Singh.

The verdict comes days after the ruling Janata Dal (United) expelled Singh and his wife, former MLA Neelam Devi, from the party for six years over alleged anti-party activities.

Singh had openly defied the party leadership by campaigning for Jan Suraaj candidate Anuj Kumar Singh instead of the JD(U)'s official nominee, Neeraj Kumar, in the Patna Graduates' constituency Legislative Council elections. He also reportedly made remarks against senior party leaders and questioned the functioning of the party leadership.

Following the expulsion, the Bihar government stripped Neelam Devi of her position on the State-Level Programme Implementation Committee, withdrawing her minister of state rank and entitlement to an official bungalow.





On October 26, the state government's Building Construction Department issued an eviction notice directing her to vacate her official residence at 1, Mall Road in Patna.

The JD(U) has also approached Bihar Assembly Speaker Prem Kumar seeking Singh's disqualification under the anti-defection law. The petition was filed under the direction of party state president Umesh Singh Kushwaha.

Murder case and legal proceedings

Dularchand Yadav, a regional strongman, was murdered on October 30, 2025, during a clash in Mokama Tal while campaigning for the Bihar Assembly elections was underway.

Yadav was backing Jan Suraaj candidate Piyush Priyadarshi when his supporters allegedly clashed with Singh's convoy.

According to the FIR registered at Ghoswari police station, Singh and his aides allegedly dragged Yadav out of his vehicle, shot him in the leg, assaulted him and ran over him with an SUV.

Singh, however, claimed that the incident was part of a political conspiracy orchestrated by a rival politician.

He alleged that Jan Suraaj supporters had attacked his convoy first.

Bihar Police arrested Singh on November 1, 2025, and lodged him in Beur Central Jail. Despite being in custody, he contested and won the Mokama Assembly seat on a JD(U) ticket.

The Patna high court granted him bail on March 19, 2026, following which he was released from prison. The bail order was subsequently challenged in the Supreme Court in October by Neeraj Kumar, the grandson of Dularchand Yadav.

World.title: 'Everyone understands who will suffer consequences': Congress's Imran Masood on Owaisi's INDIA bloc alliance offer
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Uttar Pradesh Congress working president Imran Masood has ruled out the possibility of an alliance between the INDIA bloc and

's AIMIM, criticising the latter's political statements and his remarks on the '80:20 formula'.

Reacting to Owaisi's offer to form an alliance, Masood said the decision on any electoral tie-up rested with the Congress leadership but maintained that the two sides had fundamentally different political positions.

"Whether an alliance should be formed or not is a party decision. However, Asaduddin Owaisi's speeches and statements do not align with our views. Our fight is for secularism and against the 80:20 formula that he talks about," Masood said in an X post.

Masood accuses Owaisi of encouraging polarisation

The Congress leader also cautioned against making political appeals that could deepen divisions between communities. He argued that targeting one community and calling for its consolidation could prompt the other community to unite in response.

"The biggest issue is that when you target one community and talk about uniting it, the other community will naturally unite as well.





Everyone understands who will suffer the consequences," he said.

Warning that such polarisation could benefit the BJP electorally, Masood said the people Owaisi claims to represent could ultimately bear the consequences of a BJP government coming to power.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

"A BJP government would be formed, and those who you claim to represent would bear the brunt. Why are you opening the way for them to be beaten? Instead, talk about protecting them," he said.

Uttar Pradesh is set to go to Assembly elections in 2027, with polling expected in FebruaryâMarch, although the Election Commission of India is yet to announce the official schedule. The five-year term of the current 403-member Assembly, constituted in May 2022, ends on May 22, 2027.

Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath will be seeking a second consecutive term for the BJP-led government, while the Samajwadi Party, Congress and other opposition parties are expected to challenge the ruling alliance.

World.title: India calls for protecting freedom of navigation, global trade at UN amid maritime security threats
World.content:
India on Thursday strongly condemned attacks against commercial vessels, advocating freedom of navigation and unimpeded maritime commerce at the

.

India' permanent Representative to the United Nations, Harish Parvathaneni, stressed the need to protect seafarers in accordance with international law.

Speaking at the UN Security Council's open debate on emerging technologies and maritime security on Thursday, Parvathaneni said disruptions at critical maritime choke points could have consequences far beyond their immediate geographical locations.

âRecent attacks against commercial shipping have demonstrated how disruptions at critical maritime choke points can have consequences far beyond their immediate geography,â he said, adding that such incidents threaten seafarers, disrupt supply chains and disproportionately affect developing countries through higher costs and economic uncertainty.

Parvathaneni also highlighted the growing role of emerging technologies in maritime security, noting that artificial intelligence, autonomous systems, satellite-based surveillance and advanced cyber capabilities offered opportunities to strengthen security but could also create new vulnerabilities if misused.

The Indian representative said AI-enabled analysis of satellite imagery, radar and vessel-tracking data could improve maritime domain awareness, help detect suspicious activities and support search and rescue operations.





He cited India's Information Fusion Centre â Indian Ocean Region, located near New Delhi, as an example of the value of cooperation and information sharing in strengthening maritime security.

The representative said India's approach was guided by the vision of Sagar (Security and Growth for All in the Region) and its broader commitment to inclusive maritime cooperation.

Parvathaneni also flagged the risks arising from increasing digitalisation and automation, which expose ports, vessels, communication networks and undersea infrastructure to cyber threats.

The proliferation of autonomous systems, he said, raised complex questions relating to attribution, accountability and unintended escalation. He called for appropriate safeguards, meaningful human oversight and clear responsibility in the deployment of emerging technologies.

He said the UN Charter and international law, including the law of the sea as reflected in the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (Unclos), provided the essential framework for state conduct.

The Security Council, he added, should focus on technological developments with demonstrable implications for international peace and security, while encouraging practical cooperation, confidence-building and resilience.

Parvathaneni said India had identified artificial intelligence and maritime security as important priorities for its candidature to the Security Council for 2028â2029.

âOur objective is clear: technology must strengthen human security, not undermine it; it must expand opportunity, not inequality; and it must make our shared maritime commons safer, not more contested,â he said.

World.title: CEC row LIVE updates: INDIA bloc's 'public impeachment' of CEC Gyanesh Kumar postponed
World.content:
The Indian National Developmental Inclusive Alliance (INDIA) bloc proposed “public impeachment” of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar has been postponed to October 31 due to unfavourable weather conditions in New Delhi, sources said on Friday (October 30).

Congress MP Rahul Gandhi is expected to address the media.

The INDIA bloc said its planned “public impeachment” over alleged electoral manipulation through the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls will avoid imagery that could be seen as mocking Parliament as an institution.

Follow live updates here:

World.title: INDIA bloc’s ‘public impeachment’ of CEC Gyanesh Kumar postponed to Oct. 31
World.content:
INDIA bloc’s ‘public impeachment’ of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar scheduled to be held on Friday (October 30, 2026), has been postponed to Saturday (October 31, 2026).

The ‘impeachment’ proceedings were scheduled to be held at Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge’s residence in New Delhi, However, sources told The Hindu the event has been postponed due to weather conditions with the lawns getting muddy due to rains in New Delhi.

Keep track: CEC row key highlights - October 30, 2026

Earlier, INDIA bloc was to hold the “public impeachment”, with former Lok Sabha Speaker Meira Kumar chairing the proceedings, Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge moving the “motion” and Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi making the concluding remarks.

INDIA bloc leaders had met on Thursday (October 29, 2026) to give the final shape to the “public impeachment” proceedings.

Besides Mr. Kharge and Mr. Gandhi, one person from each party was likely to speak at the “public impeachment” of the CEC.

World.title: Cyclone Arnab: 10,000 in relief camps in flood-hit Ichchapuram in Andhra; NH-16 still under water
World.content:
It is a nightmare for thousands of people in Ichchapuram and nearby villages in Andhra Pradesh’s Srikakulam district, such as Loddaputti, Korigam and Rattakanna, which were hit by flash floods in the Bahuda river after Cyclone Arnab.

Although the government had sent around 10,000 people to relief camps set up at several schools in Ichchapuram, many people remained in their flooded homes. Moving them out became a major challenge because of the strong flow of water in the villages. Restoring power supply is another challenge, since APEPDCL could not take up repairs because of waterlogging in several places.

Srikakulam Collector Swapnil Dinakar Pundkar and other officials monitored the relief operations on Thursday (October 29, 2026) night and in the early hours of Friday. Food packets were given to those in relief camps and taken to villagers in boats brought by NDRF teams, they said.

“We have taken special care for elderly people, pregnant women at the special camps. The medical and health department ensured deliveries to many women in different places in spite of inclement weather and floods to Bahuda and other rivers,” Mr. Pundkar told The Hindu.

“The district administration is capable of handling one lakh cusecs of water. Around 89,000 cusecs of water was discharged. We are hopeful that normalcy would be restored in a day as flood water is receding fast,” he added.

Vehicles are yet to be allowed on National Highway 16 (Kolkata-Chennai) because the six-lane road is under floodwater.

People living in low-lying areas along the Nagavali and Vamsadhara rivers are also suffering. As many as 113 villages have been affected by floods in the Vamsadhara. About 79,820 cusecs of water was released from the Gotta barrage on the Vamsadhara.

According to initial estimates, crops on 21,519 hectares were damaged in the district, along with horticulture crops on 383 hectares. Eleven houses collapsed and 121 were partly damaged in the rain and floods. Of the 36 routes where road traffic was disrupted, 14 have been reopened.

Gales brought down 528 electric poles. Power supply has been restored in several places, except in the Ichchapuram constituency. The Chief Minister’s Office enquired about the situation and directed the district administration to speed up relief work and restore normalcy.

World.title: Plea in Madras High Court seeks probe into nationality of Cockroach Janata Party co-convenor Saurav Das
World.content:
The Madras High Court on Friday (October 31, 2026) ordered notice to the Centre on a public interest litigation (PIL) petition, which sought a direction to the Union Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) to probe into the nationality of Saurav Das, co-convenor of the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP), and cancel his passport and Aadhaar card if he is not found to be an Indian.

The First Division Bench of Chief Justice Sushrut Arvind Dharmadhikari and Justice G. Arul Murugan also ordered notice to Mr. Das on the PIL petition filed by R. Ganesh Kumar, a businessman from Chennai, who has also sought to block the X and Instagram handles of Mr. Das and prevent him from making derogatory statements against Supreme Court judges.

In an affidavit filed through his counsel B. Jagannath, the PIL petitioner alleged that “the actual name of Mr. Das was Yogesh Sharma” and that he has “roots in Nepal.” The litigant accused the CJP leader of having concealed those details to “fraudulently” obtain an Aadhaar card, passport, and voter ID in India. He claimed that the material facts had been deliberately suppressed.

“The said Respondent No. 06 [Mr. Das] has no genuine work. He is a jobless person self-styled to be a representative of the CJP and has used his social media handle to spread hatred amongst the youth with false and unsubstantiated allegations. One does not know how many passports the said Saurav Das is in possession of. In the interest of the nation, a deeper probe... needs to be undertaken,” the affidavit read.

Listing several social media posts in which Mr. Das had criticised the judiciary, the litigant said that he, “most definitely”, must be receiving funding from abroad and that only an investigation would reveal his sources of funding. The petitioner further accused the CJP leader of having used his social media handles “only for the purpose of creating chaos, anarchy, disenchantment, and hatred against the ruling establishment.”

“The Twitter [now X] handle of the said person along with the Instagram feed is only about abuse of judiciary and has radical communist leaning glorifying the radical leftists which highlight the fact that the said Yogesh Sharma [Mr. Das] is a Communist. Furthermore, he has called during the said Jantar Mantar protest to ‘storm the Parliament’ on the back of a protest called as reform in education,” the litigant added.

World.title: Kerala HC strikes down Abkari rule provision prohibiting employment of women in toddy shops
World.content:
The Kerala High Court has struck down a provision of the Kerala Abkari rules which prohibited employing women in toddy shops.

The court recently held that the provision violated the constitutional rights to equality, to carry on any trade and the right against discrimination and right to life.

Justice P. Gopinath reiterated a Supreme Court observation that although the State was obligated to ensure that women were protected from harassment and must have a safe environment at work, this responsibility could not be achieved by prohibiting women from working in whatever industry they chose.

Sophy, a Thrissur native, had approached the High Court aggrieved by the denial of employment solely on account of a provision in the Kerala Abkari Shops Disposal Rules, 2002, prohibiting employment of women in any capacity in a toddy shop.

She argued that initially, the Rules prohibited the employment in foreign liquor shops as well, and that the High Court had struck down the portion relating to such shops. A similar rule in the Foreign Liquor Rules, 1953 had also been struck down by the High Court, she stated.

State’s contention

The State contended that the rule was intended to protect women from being exploited in workplaces. It pointed out that toddy shops were often situated in very remote places and that the rule intended to ensure their safety and well-being.

The State cited a Supreme Court order stating that men and women could not be treated as equals in all occupations, since the requirement of a particular employment, the sensitivities of either sex, the peculiarities of different social sectors and the handicaps of either sex may warrant differential treatment.

World.title: Balasubrahmanyam takes over as Vice-Chairman and Managing Director of APSRTC
World.content:
Senior IPS officer N. Balasubrahmanyam formally assumed charge as Vice-Chairman and Managing Director of the Andhra Pradesh State Road Transport Corporation (APSRTC) on Friday.

Executive Director (Administration) K. S. Brahmananda Reddy and others greeted him at the RTC House. Interacting with them, Mr. Balaaubrahmanyam insisted that top priority would be given to passenger safety, punctuality, cleanliness and improvement of services. He emphasised the need to strengthen public transport and enhance the quality of services provided to passengers.

Also Read: Retired IPS officer and former APSRTC chief N. Balasubramanyam dies

He also highlighted the need to introduce eco-friendly electric buses to improve operational efficiency and ensure financial stability of the APSRTC. Mr. Balasubrahmanyam appealed to the officials and employees to work with dedication and discipline ensuring team work to strengthen APSRTC and to provide better services to the public.

APSRTC Executive Directors A. Appala Raju (Operations) and G. V. Ravi Varma (Engineering), Chief Personnel Manager V.V. Sreedhar, senior officers, supervisors and representatives of various associations were present.

World.title: Retired IPS officer and former APSRTC chief N. Balasubramanyam dies
World.content:
Former IPS officer and former Vice-Chairman and Managing Director of the Andhra Pradesh State Road Transport Corporation (APSRTC) N. Balasubramanyam died late on Thursday (October 29, 2026) night while undergoing treatment in the United States.

Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu condoled Mr. Balasubramanyam’s death. In a post on X, he said: “Deeply saddened by the passing of retired DGP (Rank officer) N. Balasubramanyam garu. An officer of uncompromising integrity, he earned respect for his firm decisions, progressive ideas and unwavering commitment to public service. Throughout his distinguished career in policing, intelligence, transport and public administration, he championed reform, innovation and the use of technology to serve people better. He encouraged out-of-the-box thinking and involved his team in decision-making, fostering a spirit of shared responsibility.

Deeply saddened by the passing of retired DGP Shri N. Balasubramanyam garu. An officer of uncompromising integrity, he earned respect for his firm decisions, progressive ideas and unwavering commitment to public service. Throughout his distinguished career in policing, intelligence, transport and public administration, he championed reform, innovation and the use of technology to serve people better. He encouraged out-of-the-box thinking and involved his team in decision-making, fostering a spirit of shared responsibility. Andhra Pradesh continued to benefit from his experience and dedication until just a few months ago. He fought his illness with extraordinary courage and determination. His passing is a profound loss, but his contributions and the inspiration he gave the police force will endure. My heartfelt condolences to his family, friends and colleagues. Om Shanti. — N Chandrababu Naidu (@ncbn) October 30, 2026

Expressing grief over his death, APSRTC Chairman Konakalla Narayana Rao said Mr. Balasubramanyam’s death was a great loss to the organisation and to the officers and employees who had worked with him. He recalled his contributions to the corporation during his tenure as its Vice-Chairman and Managing Director, particularly in strengthening administration, improving passenger services and promoting employee welfare.

Describing him as a dedicated and disciplined officer with strong administrative skills, Mr. Konakalla said his services to the public transport sector would remain memorable. He also recalled Mr. Balasubramanyam’s commitment to public service and his humane approach towards employees. He conveyed his heartfelt condolences to the bereaved family and prayed for the departed soul to rest in peace.

Education and IT Minister Nara Lokesh also expressed shock over Mr. Balasubramanyam’s death and paid tributes to his memory. Describing him as a straightforward person who discharged his duties with dedication and integrity, Mr. Lokesh said his services would remain memorable. He conveyed his deepest condolences to the family members and prayed for strength to them in this hour of grief.

He was a 1994-batch IPS officer of the Andhra Pradesh cadre and known as a ‘no-nonsense’ officer.

Mr. Balasubramanyam, fondly referred to as Balu by his contemporaries, served as Superintendent of Police for Nalgonda and Mahbubnagar districts, now in Telangana.

He also worked as Inspector-General (Intelligence), Transport Commissioner and Director-General of Police (Organisation) in Andhra Pradesh. He also served as chief executive officer of e-Pragati and the Real Time Governance Society (RTGS). He was appointed Vice-Chairman and Managing Director of the APSRTC in early 2026.

World.title: Marco Rubio hosts G20 Foreign Ministers as Iran, Ukraine wars divide members
World.content:
U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio will host his G20 counterparts, including Russia's Sergei Lavrov, for talks on Friday (October 30, 2026) that are expected to be fractious, with wars in Ukraine and Iran and surging energy prices fanning discord.

The Foreign Ministers' meeting in Atlanta, Georgia, taking place just days before crucial U.S. midterm elections, will set the stage for a December G20 leaders' summit in Miami at President Donald Trump's Doral resort.

Few breakthroughs are expected this week from the Group of 20 economies, which include China, India, Russia, Japan, Germany and France, as officials face divisions over Moscow's war on Ukraine and fallout from conflict with Iran.

Russia has been shunned by most of the West after its 2022 invasion of Ukraine, and Mr. Lavrov himself remains under international sanctions.

Mr. Rubio's encounter with Mr. Lavrov, whose presence adds an additional layer of tension, will be closely watched as Washington pursues diplomacy on Ukraine while seeking Moscow's cooperation on reining in fuel prices, a key campaign issue in the midterms.

"The G20 is no longer really a forum where Foreign Ministers can reach agreement on a statement," a diplomatic source said.

The source added that the U.S. G20 presidency intends for Miami's summit to serve "more as a demonstration of American power, and of U.S. commitments to growth, deregulation, trade and business, rather than as a summit with grand ambitions on substantive issues."

Instead of a final declaration, the source expects a chair summary drafted by the United States to be published from this week's meeting.

The Trump administration, which is set to hand the rotating G20 leadership to Britain, sees the platform as having strayed from its core mission.

Washington has pledged to return the grouping to its goal of driving economic growth, arguing that security and economic prosperity are "inextricably linked."

"Conversations in Atlanta will provide an opportunity to discuss energy and supply chain challenges as well as identify ways to collectively address the impact of geopolitical tensions on economic security," a U.S. State Department official said.

They stressed the importance of energy access, necessary for tech like artificial intelligence, and flagged a "shared resolve to confront urgent crises and keep critical sea lanes open to commerce without threats or tolls."

Test case

Global energy prices have rocketed since U.S.-Israel strikes on Iran from late February triggered Tehran's blockage of the Strait of Hormuz.

"This is the last test case the G20 has, at least under the U.S. G20 presidency, until Miami," Alisha Chhangani of the Atlantic Council told AFP. Its outcomes will affect how the December summit shapes up.

She expects Washington will seek to argue that security shocks are also economic shocks.

It will likely push for agreement on what "freedom of navigation" means within and beyond Hormuz, a crucial waterway for oil and gas transit, she said.

But this could face objections from China, which dissented against wording on free navigation in Hormuz and worldwide at an earlier gathering of Finance Ministers.

China's top diplomat Wang Yi will not be in Atlanta, and is instead sending his deputy, the U.S. State Department said.

Meanwhile, the possibility of further escalation in West Asia is mounting, with Israel threatening to strike Iran and Trump signalling he could attack after Tuesday's (November 3, 2026) midterm elections.

Lavrov attendance

In Atlanta, Mr. Rubio is also due to cross paths with Mr. Lavrov, who has already reached Atlanta according to Russian state media.

It comes ahead of fresh negotiations between Moscow, Kyiv and Washington in November.

The appearance of Mr. Lavrov, who plans to argue against international sanctions at the gathering, will likely frustrate European Ministers, Ms. Chhangani said.

It is not surprising, however, as Washington has welcomed Russian officials to this year's G20 events, while excluding member South Africa, and Mr. Trump has invited his Russian counterpart Vladimir Putin to Miami in December.

Mr. Trump has eased some sanctions on Moscow recently while touting a deal for Russia to sell diesel as prices soared, squeezing Americans.

The diplomatic source stressed that Russia's G20 presence "in no way legitimises its actions."

All eyes will also be on U.S. engagement with Brazil, whose Foreign Minister will be in attendance, after Washington granted entry to Flavio Bolsonaro following his defeat in Sunday's (October 25, 2026) presidential election.

World.title: DPM Dar, Singaporean FM discuss ways to enhance cooperation in trade, investment
World.content:
Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar on Friday held talks with Sin­ga­porean Foreign Minister Vivian Balakrishnan, who is visiting Islamabad, and discussed ways enhance cooperation in trade and investment, the Foreign Office (FO) said.

Balakrishnan arrived in Islamabad earlier in the day. He called on DPM Dar at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

The FO said in a statement that the two leaders reviewed the “longstanding and friendly relations” between Pakistan and Singapore as the two countries marked 60 years of diplomatic relations.

They underscored the importance of sustained high-level exchanges and discussed ways to further enhance cooperation in trade, investment, connectivity and skills development, while promoting business-to-business exchanges and people-to-people contacts, the statement added.

Dar and Balakrishnan also discussed cooperation at multilateral fora and Pakistan’s enhanced engagement with the Association of Southeast Asian Nations, particularly in the context of Singapore’s forthcoming chairmanship of the body in 2027.

Moreover, exchanging views on regional and global developments, Dar emphasised the importance of dialogue and diplomacy in resolving disputes and advancing lasting peace and stability, the statement said.

Later, their opening remarks from delegation-level talks between the two sides were televised, with Dar saying that the depth of diplomatic relations between Pakistan and Singapore was not reflected in economic ties.

He said his focus had been on “economic diplomacy” after joining the Foreign Office, adding: “If we work together, […] I am sure we can reach a new level of economic relations.”

The DPM further suggested the Board of Investment in Pakistan could work with its counterpart in Singapore.

He said the two countries had “great cooperation” on multilateral issues and Singapore’s interest in regional issues was “greatly appreciated”.

“You remain in touch, and we keep sharing developments with you.”

He added that the two had also discussed Palestine and Kashmir issues, among other matters, in a restricted meeting.

“So I think this friendship and great cooperation will continue from our side, and I am sure you will always reciprocate, rather go a mile ahead of us,” the DPM said.

For his part, the Singaporean foreign minister recalled that Pakistan was one of the “early countries to recognise Singapore post independence”. He pointed out that Singapore was 61 and was commemorating 60th anniversary of diplomatic ties with Pakistan.

Prior to Balakrishnan’s visit, the FO had said a memorandum of understanding (MoU) on cooperation in disaster management between Pakistan’s National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA) and Singapore’s Civil Defence Force (SCDF) would also be exchanged during trip.

“Pakistan and Singapore maintain cordial bilateral relations based on mutual respect and longstanding friendship. The visit underscores the shared commitment of the two countries to deepening and diversifying their bilateral partnership,” the statement had added.

World.title: Netanyahu's bloc finishes ahead in Israel election, but well short of majority
World.content:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s camp finished ahead of the opposition but remained well short of a majority, final results from general election showed on Friday, setting the stage for tough coalition talks or potentially another vote.

Netanyahu’s coalition of right-wing and far-right parties won 53 of the Knesset’s 120 seats, with his Likud party remaining the largest faction with 27 seats.

The opposition bloc, led by centrist Gadi Eisenkot, secured 48 seats.

The results from the Central Elections Committee also cemented the emergence as potential kingmakers of the Arab party groupings Raam and the Joint List, with the two winning a combined 19 seats.

The fragmented outcome sets the stage for difficult negotiations to form a government that could last weeks, with no single bloc able to reach the 61-seat threshold needed and the prospect of another election remaining if talks fail.

The final tally came after Netanyahu’s camp spent Thursday amplifying unproven allegations that Arab-Israeli groups received foreign funding to influence the vote, accusations rejected by both Arab-majority lists and Qatar.

Israel’s Shin Bet domestic security service said it was investigating suspected irregularities, but stressed the probe was not intended to “cast aspersions or place blame on an entire sector that went out to vote in a democratic and lawful manner”.

The electoral commission also sought to calm tensions, with its acting director general Dean Livne saying any suggestion of widespread issues was “entirely groundless”.

Political earthquake

The controversy centred on allegations that Raam received money from Qatar, the energy-rich Gulf powerbroker that has channels to Hamas, to finance vote-buying operations.

“The Raamgate scandal is a political earthquake. Israel’s elections have been stolen!” Netanyahu’s Likud party alleged on Thursday.

Raam leader Mansour Abbas denied any wrongdoing and welcomed an investigation, while the Joint List accused Netanyahu and his allies of conducting a “campaign of incitement” out of fear of Arab voters’ growing political influence.

Government officials have so far provided no evidence to back the allegations.

Opposition figures accused Netanyahu of attempting to undermine confidence in the results after failing to secure a governing majority.

“He is trying to challenge the election results,” left-wing candidate Yair Golan said.

Eisenkot said he was briefed by the Shin Bet and the election committee, adding it was “too early to understand what happened, and whether anything happened at all”.

But he continued: “It’s already clear that Likud and Netanyahu have embarked on a coordinated, organised campaign seeking to delegitimise the results of the election.”

Netanyahu himself has long been under the cloud of allegations related to Qatar after the arrests last year of two of his aides for allegedly receiving payments from the Gulf state.

Qatar called the latest accusations “ridiculous and dangerous”.

Kingmakers under pressure

Yousef Jabareen, head of the Joint List, told AFP that he is willing to cooperate with the opposition to bring down Netanyahu but without joining it in a government.

Netanyahu had tried during the voting to raise allegations of fraud, saying that Arab parties were caught with envelopes of cash, and Likud peddled the accusations throughout Thursday.

Police said they arrested three suspects but the election commission called it an isolated local case.

World.title: Crypto exchange Binance freezes assets after $6.3 billion security breach
World.content:
Binance, the world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange, said a security breach had resulted in an estimated $6.3 billion impact that analysts said could amount to the biggest crypto heist ever and might make investors rethink the risks of owning digital assets.

Binance said it had worked with partners to freeze the affected assets, with about $3bn located so far. It gave no update on the status of the remaining $3.3bn as Binance co-founder Yi He said the company would cover “all hacking losses”.

An initial investigation suggested the breach may have started with a hacked laptop belonging to one of its engineers, which let an attacker gain access to one of its systems and make unauthorised withdrawals, Binance said.

Later, US blockchain ​analysis firm TRM Labs said North Korean hackers were ​behind the raid on Binance.

“An ⁠attacker moved approximately $6.36 bn out of ​Binance wallets on 10 blockchains, most of it ​in about 20 ​minutes,” TRM Labs said ‌in ⁠a blog post on its website.

“TRM attributes the attack ​to TraderTraitor, ​North ⁠Korea’s elite hacking unit, ​based on robust ​on ⁠and off-chain intelligence. We make this ⁠judgement ​with high ​confidence,” the blog said.

‘Biggest hack in history’

Markets reacted immediately to Binance’s hacking in early Asian trading on Friday.

Bitcoin dropped more than 3 per cent to a six-week low of $76,368 and ether fell more than 3pc to a two-month low of $2,178. BNB, a token originally launched as Binance Coin that can be used to pay Binance fees, was down 5pc over the past 24 hours at $709.70, according to market aggregator CoinGecko.

Shares in crypto exchange Coinbase Global slid 4.8pc while those of bitcoin buyer Strategy fell nearly 6pc in extended US trading.

The incident could be the world’s biggest crypto heist, according to analytics firm Chainalysis and other industry experts.

“It’s the biggest hack in history,” said Aravind Srinivasan, head of large crypto market maker GSR’s systematic OTC business.

Beyond the potential loss of assets, the security breach was likely to have wider ramifications for crypto, which had already been under pressure lately due to higher US interest rates and softer demand from exchange-traded fund buyers, analysts said.

“It may further dampen risk appetite and prompt investors to reassess the safety of assets held on centralised exchanges, as well as counterparty, solvency and liquidity risks,” said Tim Sun, senior researcher at HashKey Group, based in Hong Kong.

Binance, which allows users to buy, sell and trade digital assets, has 335 million registered users globally and had about $162.8 billion in assets under custody as of the exchange’s 2025 annual report.

“User funds remain safe,” Binance said in a statement.

“As a precaution, all deposits and withdrawals are temporarily suspended while our security teams conduct checks, secure wallet infrastructure, and trace affected assets, with the close support of our law enforcement and industry partners.”

Binance has secure asset fund

Binance runs a secure asset fund for users, which is a reserve held entirely in bitcoin that is intended to protect user assets in cases of security breaches, according to its website.

“It’s becoming very hard to counter hacks as AI can find vulnerabilities faster than you can fix them,” said Bernardo Brites, CEO of Trace Finance, a payments and stablecoin infrastructure company.

“My view is that users will move away from smaller and medium-sized exchanges, (it is) becoming too risky to park your money somewhere that couldn’t cover a hack of meaningful size.”

Stablecoin issuer Tether said it had frozen nearly $1.57 billion in assets linked to the incident, while Circle froze more than $800 million.

World Liberty Financial, a crypto company linked to US President Donald Trump and his family, said on Thursday it had worked with cryptocurrency custodian BitGo to freeze funds stolen in what it described as a Binance hack. Binance’s Yi said $27 million in stablecoins and about $2 million worth of World Liberty tokens had been frozen.

Crypto firm Ripple also froze roughly $200 million in funds, Yi said. Jack McDonald, senior vice president of stablecoins at Ripple, said the company was closely monitoring reports of a potential exploit involving Binance and was freezing affected funds and coordinating with relevant parties.

Incident adds to string of crypto thefts

Miguel Morel, CEO of blockchain intelligence firm Arkham, said data indicated that billions of dollars appeared to have been hacked from Binance by an unknown actor.

The incident adds to a string of crypto thefts. Last year, attackers stole $2.9 billion worth of cryptocurrency across nearly 150 attacks, according to researchers at TRM Labs. In September, cryptocurrency exchange Bitget said roughly $350 million in crypto had been stolen from its platform, underscoring the industry’s vulnerability to hackers.

Authorities have warned that organised crime groups are increasingly using cryptocurrencies to move funds across borders outside the traditional financial system.

Binance.US, a separate cryptocurrency exchange, said it was not affected by the security incident.

Coinbase said it was unaffected and was monitoring the situation.

In an unrelated incident earlier on Thursday, prediction market operator Polymarket temporarily halted trading after a security incident involving a third-party provider. It later resumed trading and said it would fully reimburse affected traders.

World.title: LHC directs Noreen Niazi’s counsel to file separate plea for medical treatment, family meetings
World.content:
LAHORE: The Lahore High Court on Friday directed the counsel for Noreen Niazi, sister of former prime minister and PTI founder Imran Khan, to file a separate miscellaneous application seeking medical treatment and family meetings.

On Wednesday evening, Noreen was shifted to the Punjab Institute of Cardiology (PIC) following her deteriorating health conditions, on the recommendation of the doctors of the Kot Lakhpat Jail, where she has been detained.

Justice Abher Gul Khan issued the direction while hearing a petition filed by Sakeena Niazi challenging the extension of the preventive detention of PTI founder Imran Khan’s two sisters, Noreen and Dr Uzma Khan.

The judge asked the petitioner’s counsel whether an application had been filed seeking permission for medical treatment and meetings with family members.

Advocate Rana Mudassar Umar, counsel for the petitioner, replied that an application to this effect had been submitted to the deputy commissioner.

The judge directed the counsel to also file a separate civil miscellaneous application with the court. The counsel argued that there was no lawful justification for extending the detention of the two women.

He said Noreen, 70, had never suffered from a heart ailment before.

Questioning the circumstances that led to her hospitalisation, Advocate Umar asked what kind of pressure had been exerted on her during detention that she had to be taken to hospital.

He argued that the fresh detention orders were replicas of the previous ones, with only the dates changed. He further argued that suspending the detention notification would pave the way for the women’s release.

PTI Secretary General Advocate Salman Akram Raja, who was also present in court, claimed that Noreen was ill and had been shifted to the hospital’s intensive care unit.

However, neither her family members nor her lawyer had been allowed to meet her, he added. He said he was unaware whether she was still in hospital or had been shifted back to jail.

Asked whether the home secretary, who was abroad, had returned to the country, Additional Advocate General Nasir Chohan said he would check and inform the court.

Another petition, filed by Shahrez Khan challenging the detention of his mother, Aleema Khan, is yet to be fixed for a hearing.

Imran’s sisters were detained by authorities in September, under Section 3 of the MPO, as the PTI geared up for a planned protest march towards Islamabad.

Their detention was ordered for 30 days and would have expired on Oct 19 for Aleema and Oct 20 for Uzma and Noreen. However, they remained in jail, and the government later informed the LHC that their detentions had been extended on Oct 7.

On Sept 24, the LHC had turned down a request to immediately suspend the preventive detention notifications issued against Noreen and Dr Uzma.

Earlier this month, Imran’s cousin, Qasim Zaman, was also taken into custody when he went to Adiala jail to meet the ex-prime minister.

World.title: 'You are disgusting': Trump lashes out at reporter as he cancels weekend rallies ahead of midterm polls
World.content:
US President Donald Trump is scrapping two of his last midterm election rallies, his Republican Party said Thursday, as the 80-year-old leader lashed out at a reporter who asked if he was “sick of travelling”.

“You’re sick to ask that question. You are sick,” Trump told the reporter after returning to Washington from a campaign trip to South Carolina.

“I feel perfect. You are disgusting. Put yourself in shape, you look like hell.”

Trump told reporters he did not “feel like I have to go to Kansas,” a Midwestern state where Senator Roger Marshall, a fellow Republican, is in an unexpectedly competitive race with Democratic challenger Adam Hamilton.

“He is doing very well,” Trump said of Marshall.

“We are going to have a strong Tuesday night.”

Later on Thursday, the Republican National Committee said in a statement that it would also cancel a planned rally in Iowa, home to several competitive congressional races.

Instead of the events in Kansas and Iowa, Trump will hold a “large number” of virtual “telerallies” in a series of states, the Republican National Committee said.

The canceled in-person rallies were set for Salina, Kansas, on Saturday, and Dubuque, Iowa, on Sunday.

Republicans are fighting to keep control of Congress in the November 3 midterms. Trump has urged the party to “pretend I’m on the ballot” to maximise turnout despite his poor approval ratings.

“With Republicans in a strong position in Kansas and Iowa, previously planned in-person rallies in those states will no longer take place as scheduled,” the RNC statement said.

The president is still expected to travel to rallies in several states before Tuesday’s election. Trump’s final election rally is now set to be in Florida on Friday.

Despite being the oldest elected president in US history, Trump has kept up a gruelling schedule of near-daily rallies throughout October to help Republicans in the midterms.

Since October 1, Trump has hosted 25 rallies in 19 states, often speaking for his party in rural areas of Republican-friendly states. Tuesday’s midterm elections will determine whether Republicans retain narrow control of the US Senate and House of Representatives.

MAGA Inc, a campaign funding group aligned with Trump, said on Thursday it would host a series of “tele-rallies” with the president in at least 19 states, including Kansas and Iowa, before Election Day.

Trump has noted that his recent series of more than hour-long campaign speeches has been challenging. Sounding hoarse in Mississippi on Monday, Trump said, “God didn’t make your vocal cords to do a rally every day.”

On Thursday, after campaigning for Senator Darline Graham in South Carolina, Trump ridiculed a Reuters reporter who asked how he felt after weeks of rallies and whether he was sick of travelling.

“You’ve been following me for two weeks,” Trump said before boarding his motorcade back to the White House.

“I feel perfect.”

World.title: Cop martyred in KP's Bajaur as terrorists attack police post: official
World.content:
BAJAUR: A police officer was martyred after terrorists attacked a police post in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s Bajaur district, officials said on Friday.

The attack on the police post in Silai Pati area in the remote Barang tehsil, bordering Malakand district, occurred late on Thursday night.

Mansoor Khan, a spokesperson for the district police, while confirming the attack, told Dawn that a group of Fitna al-Khawarij terrorists targeted the Silai Pati police post, prompting the personnel to retaliate bravely and courageously.

Fitna al Khawarij is a term the state uses for terrorists belonging to the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan.

The official said that the police official embraced martyrdom after putting up a brave resistance.

He added that the attackers fled after an effective response by the personnel deployed at the post.

Later, funeral prayers for the martyred cop were held at the Police Lines in Khar, which were attended by Deputy Commissioner Adnan Farid Afridi, DPO Khan Zeb Mohmand and elders of the area.

A large number of police officials and political and social activists also attended the funeral prayers before the body was dispatched to his native area in Barang tehsil for burial.

No group has claimed responsibility for the attack.

On Thursday, Bajaur district administration banned pillion riding for 10 days by invoking Section 144 of the Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC), owing to the security situation. The notification said the measure was taken in view of reports from intelligence agencies and the police department.

Earlier, the authorities imposed a 15-day ban on pillion riding in Bajaur on September 5, citing the security situation back then as well.

KP has been witnessing terrorist attacks and security challenges for a long time. According to a recent report from the Centre for Research and Security Studies, Pakistan recor­ded a sharp 83 per cent increase in violence-linked fatalities during the third quarter of 2026, re­­versing a declining trend reported in the first and second quarters as terrorism and counter-terrorism deaths surged nationwide.

Balochistan and KP remained the epicentres of violence, jointly accounting for 98pc of all fatalities during the period. Balochistan recorded 829 deaths, nearly 59pc of the national total, while KP reported 556 fatalities, accounting for more than 39pc.

World.title: Lawmakers voice alarm over KP situation, seek electoral reforms
World.content:
• Achakzai questions govt’s handling of Tehran diplomacy, Afghanistan ties

• Senate resolution seeks coordinated national action to curb population growth

ISLAMABAD: Lawmakers in the National Assembly and Senate on Thursday raised concerns over the political situation in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and alleged human rights violations, while both houses also discussed electoral reforms and the need to strengthen parliamentary institutions.

National Assembly Opposition Leader Mehmood Khan Achakzai criticised the government for failing to take parliament into confidence over recent diplomatic developments in Tehran.

“How can four people decide the future of the whole nation?” he asked, warning that such decisions could push the country towards “anarchy and civil war”.

Mr Achakzai also opposed the suspension of trade with Afghanistan, describing Afghans as traditional friends of Pakistan and criticising the country’s past policies towards its neighbour.

PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan said the parliamentary proceedings and the prevailing political situation in KP were creating a negative impression among the public. He also called for an end to hereditary politics in the country.

Rights concerns raised

Meanwhile, speaking on a point of order in the Senate, PTI parliamentary leader Barrister Syed Ali Zafar accused the government of undermining constitutional protections through the imposition of emergency and governor’s rule in KP.

He argued that fundamental human rights could not be suspended or compromised, regardless of the political situation. “There is one thing that cannot be broken, suspended or compromised: the fundamental human rights of the people of Pakistan,” he said.

Mr Zafar expressed concern over the detention of Noreen Niazi, sister of jailed PTI founder Imran Khan, claiming that she had suffered a heart attack and was hospitalised but her family was not being allowed to meet her.

Responding to the concerns, Adviser to the Prime Minister on Political Affairs Rana Sanaullah said Noreen Niazi had been provided medical treatment in Lahore and was in satisfactory condition.

On allegations that her family was being denied access, Mr Sanaullah assured the house that details would be sought and the matter addressed according to the circumstances.

He defended her detention, alleging that she had sought to create unrest by mobilising people for a protest march towards Islamabad.

Senate Opposition Leader Allama Raja Nasir Abbas also criticised the government’s actions in KP, alleging that the province had been “snatched from the people”.

He also questioned the imposition of emergency and governor’s rule in KP, arguing that democratic institutions could not function without respect for the law.

Population growth resolution

Separately, the Senate passed a resolution calling for urgent and coordinated national action to address the challenges posed by the country’s rapidly growing population.

The resolution, moved by PPP Vice President Senator Sherry Rehman, called for a comprehensive national response to population growth and its impact on public services and socioeconomic development.

Ms Rehman said Pakistan’s population was projected to reach approximately 390 million by 2050 at the current growth rate, placing unprecedented pressure on national resources.

Published in Dawn, October 30th, 2026

World.title: New provinces to carry heavy cost
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: A private think tank has found more fiscal faults than benefits of the much-discussed creation of new provinces, advising priority to stronger local governments instead of new provinces if public service delivery was actually intended.

In its latest market analysis release on Thursday, Policy Research Institute of Market Economy (Prime) highlighted the additional annual recurring cost of Rs47 billion to Rs57bn in case of creation of two more provinces — South Punjab, Bahawalpur and remaining Punjab — and up to Rs730bn if 30 divisional units were to upgrade to provincial status.

“Any proposal for creating new provinces should include a formal fiscal costing exercise before constitutional or legislative changes are pursued”, the think tank said, adding that the costing should estimate the recurring expenditure required for the governor, chief minister, provincial assembly, secretariat, high court and other core institutions, together with the likely NFC resource envelope of each proposed unit. This would make it possible to assess whether the expected administrative benefits justify the additional recurring burden,” it said.

If the number of provinces increases to six, South Punjab receives an illustrative allocation of Rs1tr under the existing NFC, while Bahawalpur receives Rs537bn. In case of 30 provinces, allocations differ considerably, ranging from Rs7201bn for Lahore and Rs691bn for Karachi to Rs46bn for Loralai and Rs50bn for Zhob. Thus 11 of the 30 proposed units receive less than Rs150bn per annum.

Think tank puts annual recurring bill at Rs47-57bn for two provinces and up to Rs730bn for 30

The estimated annual recurring cost of a new provincial government is Rs22.4bn under the low-cost scenario and Rs25.9bn under the high-cost scenario, therefore Rs47-56bn per annum for two and Rs610-730bn for 30 provinces.

Using a 10pc fiscal sustainability benchmark based on the low recurring-cost estimate, 16 of the 30 proposed provinces would remain at or below the threshold, while 14 exceed it. The burden is particularly high in the smallest units: the core provincial structure would absorb around 49pc of Loralai’s allocation, 45pc of Zhob’s and 37pc of Rakhshan’s even under the low-cost estimate.

Every proposed province with a population below 1.2 million would require more than one-third of its NFC allocation to finance the core provincial government structure.

The findings therefore show that the fiscal implications of restructuring depend strongly on the number and size of the provinces created. Limited restructuring involving relatively large units produces a much smaller recurring burden, whereas several smaller division-based provinces would face disproportionately high administrative costs relative to their expected NFC resources.

Therefore, at the fiscal level, creation of new provinces will put additional pressure on fiscal resources of smaller provinces, especially those with lower NFC allocations and constrained revenue generation capacity. A greater portion of their available resources would be consumed by ongoing government expenses, resulting in reduced fiscal room for other provincial spending, such as public service provision and developmental expenditure, the analysis showed.

Therefore, the think tank emphasised that provincial restructuring should be evaluated not only in political and administrative terms, but also through a clear fiscal framework.

Published in Dawn, October 30th, 2026

World.title: Ramisa rape and murder: Sohel Rana mentions new name as charges framed
World.content:
A new name has surfaced in the Ramisa rape and murder case, with prime accused Sohel Rana telling reporters today that a man called "Dollar" was responsible for the rape and murder of the eight-year-old girl.

However, no further details about the person were immediately available.

Sohel made the claim while being escorted to the courtroom of the Dhaka Metropolitan Children Violence Suppression Tribunal.

"I am at fault, and Dollar is also at fault. I am not the only culprit," he told reporters.

Standing in the courtroom's dock, he shouted at the lawyers present in the courtroom after the hearing, and said, “I did not commit the rape; I only dismembered the body. A man named Dollar committed the rape. I have sinned, so punish me for that sin.”

At that time, Sohel further claimed that Dollar had promised to pay him Tk 2 lakh if he could bring the girl to him.

However, police officers present immediately stopped him from speaking further.

Sohel also claimed that his wife, Swapna Khatun, was innocent.

Earlier in the day, Sohel and Swapna were brought to the lock-up of the Metropolitan Sessions Judge's Court in Dhaka.

Later, Judge Masrur Salekin of the tribunal framed charges against the couple in the case over the rape and murder of Ramisa in Dhaka's Pallabi area.

Both accused pleaded not guilty after the charges were read out, said Bench Assistant Pankoj Peter Gomes.

The judge also fixed tomorrow for the start of the trial, with the victim's father, Abdul Hannan Mollah, scheduled to testify first, he added.
