World.title: Political analyst: ‘If Aliyev has to choose between Russia and Turkey, he will choose Russia’
World.content:
Tensions between Azerbaijan and Turkey

Political analyst Arastun Orujlu has discussed the reasons for the recent tensions between Azerbaijan and Turkey, as well as their possible consequences, in an interview with Meydan TV.

In his view, one of the main reasons for the disagreement between Baku and Ankara is Azerbaijan’s growing closeness to Israel.

– Mr Orujlu, what do you think is the main reason for the tensions that have emerged between Turkey and Azerbaijan in recent days?

– The tensions between Turkey and Azerbaijan have nothing to do with Islam or religious values. These factors serve merely as a pretext, primarily for official Baku, which uses them to provoke conflict. However, I do not rule out personal motives either. Experience shows that personal considerations often lie behind the Azerbaijani authorities’ strong reactions to the actions of other countries.

Ilham Aliyev views every issue through the prism of his personal interests. Nevertheless, I believe the current tensions are primarily political. They reflect Azerbaijan’s desire to distance itself from neighbouring countries and pursue a foreign policy oriented towards Tel Aviv and Washington. This trend is now clearly visible.

– You link these tensions to Azerbaijan’s foreign policy. In Turkey, however, people have criticised the Azerbaijani authorities both over their policies on the hijab and over their relations with Israel. To what extent does this criticism reflect political considerations? Are there genuine disagreements between Ankara and Baku on these issues?

– These are separate issues, so let me address them one by one. The hijab has always been a matter of principle for Turkey’s Justice and Development Party (AKP). For a long time, it sparked heated political debates in Turkey. The country experienced serious upheaval and a painful period over this issue. Therefore, if the current Turkish government, led by the AKP, had failed to respond to what was happening, it would undoubtedly have damaged its standing among its own voters.

In fact, the first reaction did not come from the AKP leadership. It began on Turkish social media, where journalists and individual users started protesting. Only later did the AKP leadership respond, and not at government level. The response came from Oktay Saral, an adviser to Recep Tayyip Erdoğan on party affairs.

As for Israel, the problems here are genuinely serious and entirely political. Turkey and Israel are engaged in an intense struggle for influence in the South Caucasus, the Middle East and the eastern Mediterranean. Israel is effectively seeking regional dominance. Turkey, meanwhile, believes it should take the leading role because it has stronger moral and historical claims to it, as well as greater military capabilities than Israel. Turkey’s strong reaction to the genocide unfolding in Gaza also plays an important role.

We know these problems have existed for quite some time. There is no doubt that Israel is trying to expand its influence in Central Asia through Azerbaijan and the South Caucasus. Central Asia is one of Turkey’s key foreign policy priorities, and Israel has already begun strengthening its position there. The two sides have very sharp disagreements over this issue.

It is also well known that the Azerbaijani authorities maintain exceptionally close relations with Israel. After the United States, Azerbaijan may well be Israel’s closest partner.

– In this context, how do you assess Azerbaijan’s decision to declare 31 Turkish citizens persona non grata? How might this decision affect relations between the two countries?

– As far as I can tell, Ilham Aliyev is trying to weaken Turkey’s influence in Azerbaijan. I do not mean its influence over the government, but rather Turkey’s role in Azerbaijani society. Although no opinion polls have been conducted, the situation clearly suggests that Turkey became the most popular country among Azerbaijanis after the 44-day war. Deep historical, cultural and ethnic ties explain this. Perhaps this is precisely what worries Ilham Aliyev.

He effectively signalled that a conflict was brewing at the New Azerbaijan Party (YAP) congress. For some reason, many observers overlooked his remarks. In his speech, Ilham Aliyev addressed not only economic and social problems but also put forward three political arguments with an underlying message.

First, he stated directly that nobody had provided Azerbaijan with free support, and that even weapons and ammunition had been sold at global market prices. Azerbaijanis immediately thought of Turkey when they heard these words. Yet Ilham Aliyev himself has repeatedly said that Azerbaijan would have found itself in a difficult position without Turkish support. At the Victory Parade following the 44-day war, he stood alongside Recep Tayyip Erdoğan on the main podium. Now, suddenly, he has made this statement. It is quite clear that he directed it specifically at Turkey.

Second, in the same speech, he stressed the need to improve the quality of education. But if Ilham Aliyev genuinely wants to improve education, he should appoint professionals to senior positions in the sector. Today, Azerbaijan’s education system is run entirely by brokers, shopkeepers and traders who have nothing to do with education.

The third point concerned strengthening patriotic sentiment. Aliyev was effectively saying: “I will fight against Turkey, and your first homeland is Azerbaijan.” That was the message behind his words.

Look at who took part in all the disputes and conflicts that followed. They included media outlets linked to the Azerbaijani authorities, individuals, influencers, media platforms, experts and even people who call themselves opposition party leaders. They all joined the campaign. It was carefully planned.

Let me repeat: it appears that Ilham Aliyev has set himself the task of weakening Turkey’s standing and influence in Azerbaijani society. Alternatively, someone may have assigned him that task.

– We have previously seen the Azerbaijani authorities use similar rhetoric and pressure tactics when relations with other countries deteriorated. For example, when relations with Europe worsened, independent NGOs and media representatives became targets. When tensions with Russia escalated, authorities targeted the Sputnik news agency and several politicians. During tensions with Iran, they put pressure on religious believers. Now we see a similar approach towards Turkey. Which specific issue, in your view, lies at the heart of the disagreement between Azerbaijan and Turkey?

– I believe the issue concerns foreign policy alone. As I have already said, Azerbaijan is moving closer to Israel, and this process is advancing very rapidly. Moreover, Azerbaijani media have featured not merely people who support Israel, but individuals with direct links to Israeli organisations. They have accused Turkey of wrongdoing while defending the Azerbaijani authorities’ position.

For example, the English-language Azerbaijani website News.Az published an article by a certain Roman Gurevich. After reading it, I noticed that subsequent events in Azerbaijan unfolded according to the scenario described in that article. This shows that Israel has considerable influence over Azerbaijani media.

All the websites and media outlets that belong to Global Media Group also have links to Israel. People in Turkey can see this and understand that Azerbaijan is moving away from them. Relations between Israel and Turkey have deteriorated to such an extent that Azerbaijan has effectively found itself having to choose a side. Ankara can clearly see that Azerbaijan — or, more precisely, Ilham Aliyev and his family — are choosing Israel. I believe this is the main reason for the current conflict.

But what measures can they take against Turkey? Turkey has no levers of influence within Azerbaijan. Western countries, for example, once had some influence over certain NGOs and media outlets. The authorities arrested their representatives on fabricated charges. When relations with Iran deteriorated, they arrested religious believers. During tensions with Russia, they detained IT specialists whom the Azerbaijani authorities themselves had invited into the country.

Turkey has no comparable resources in Azerbaijan. Taking such steps against Turkey would also carry serious risks. Azerbaijan itself has considerable leverage in Turkey, including a network of lobbyists it funds and media resources. In addition, Azerbaijani investments in Turkey amount to around $20 billion.

Nevertheless, I do not think relations will deteriorate to the point of a complete break. Recep Tayyip Erdoğan’s phone call was more than an invitation. It was also a warning with a clear message: “Stop this process.” The Azerbaijani authorities had been orchestrating an extremely dirty campaign against Turkey, including at the military leadership level. Perhaps even Russia and Iran have not faced attacks this harsh.

– How might the current tensions affect the future of relations between the two countries?

– These tensions have already affected relations. The relationship between Azerbaijan and Turkey rests on several distinct foundations, unlike Azerbaijan’s ties with other countries.

The first is the relationship between the two states. The second is the personal relationship between Ilham Aliyev and Recep Tayyip Erdoğan, which brings together various interests. For example, companies close to the AKP operate in Azerbaijan. The third foundation is the connection between the two societies. This is the most reliable pillar of their relationship.

The concept of “One nation, two states” is more than a slogan. The relationship between the two peoples has deep historical roots stretching back at least 120 to 130 years. This third pillar has suffered the damage.

Various groups hostile to Turkey have become more active in Azerbaijan and taken advantage of the situation. They have effectively received a signal that they can now criticise, insult and accuse Turkey. As a result, they have dealt a significant blow to the most important foundation of relations between the two countries.

– At what level will the two countries maintain their political and strategic alliance after this?

– That will depend on many external factors. The results of elections in Israel and the political situation in the United States will play an important role, for example. Recently, an American researcher published a book alleging that large sums of money had been transferred to Donald Trump’s son-in-law through Azerbaijan. This should not surprise us, because Azerbaijan conducts much of its foreign policy through lobbying and financial mechanisms.

Future developments will depend on these factors. For example, if the Republican Party loses the US midterm elections and Trump’s influence weakens, Ilham Aliyev will have to realign himself with either Russia or Turkey.

I say this with full responsibility: if Aliyev has to choose between Russia and Turkey, he will choose Russia. Around 70% of people in Azerbaijan’s current leadership have ties to Russia, while 30% have ties to Israel. There are virtually no people in the Azerbaijani leadership who look to Turkey.

Tensions between Azerbaijan and Turkey

World.title: Georgia’s new gambling tournament law raises ombudsman concerns, draws Patriarchate response
World.content:
International gambling tournaments in Georgia

Georgia‘s parliament has passed a bill in its second reading that would allow casinos to organise international gambling tournaments. The initiative provides for permits to hold such tournaments, the introduction of relevant fees and fines for violating permit conditions.

Under the bill, an “international gambling tournament” is defined as a competition organised by a casino in which the prize fund is guaranteed in advance by the organiser and at least 80% of participants are foreign nationals.

Georgian government representatives have justified the move by citing its potential to boost tourism and economic activity. However, the country’s ombudsman has criticised the fast-tracked legislative process and the lack of a proper assessment of potential social harm.

Metropolitan Anton of Vani and Baghdati said the Georgian Patriarchate would discuss the issue on 30 October and present its unified position to the public following the meeting.

What will change?

Under the bill, organisers will be exempt from paying fees for the use of gaming tables used exclusively for international gambling tournaments if the prize fund exceeds 3 million lari. Organisers will also be allowed to generate revenue from holding such tournaments.

International gambling tournaments may be held both at licensed casino premises and at other venues.

The annual permit fee for organising such tournaments will be 100,000 lari (approximately $39,000). Violating permit conditions will carry a fine of 50,000 lari, while organising or holding an international gambling tournament without the required permit will result in a fine of 150,000 lari.

According to the bill’s authors, the amendments aim to improve the legal framework governing gambling and establish clear regulations for organising international gambling tournaments.

The bill’s sponsors note that existing legislation neither defines the term “international tournament” nor contains provisions regulating such events. They argue that this creates uncertainty for businesses and regulatory authorities.

What does the ombudsman say?

Following the bill’s first reading, Georgia’s ombudsman called on parliament to halt its further consideration and adoption.

According to the ombudsman, the fast-tracked consideration of an issue affecting the public interest is particularly problematic, especially without a proper expert assessment or comprehensive analysis of potential human rights risks.

The ombudsman argues that the bill lacks an assessment of its impact on public health and a proper analysis of potential social harm and the costs of preventing it. Furthermore, relevant experts and organisations were not involved in drafting the legislation, while international experience was not taken into account.

The ombudsman also notes that the bill’s explanatory memorandum claims the proposed changes will not affect children’s rights but provides no justification for this conclusion.

“When considering bills of this kind, it is crucial to conduct a comprehensive and thorough examination of the issue, including by ensuring broad participation of experts in the relevant field,” the ombudsman stressed.

The ombudsman emphasises that discussions of the proposed amendments should not focus solely on potential economic benefits. Instead, their impact on public health and social well-being, as well as the associated risks, must be given due consideration.

What does the Patriarchate say?

According to Archpriest Andria Jaghmaidze, head of the Georgian Patriarchate’s public relations department, no prior discussions were held on the issue, and the Patriarchate itself has not yet examined the bill in detail.

Jaghmaidze noted that the Patriarchate has been actively involved in developing regulations governing gambling since 2017. He also said that the Patriarchate had reviewed the ombudsman’s position and largely shared the arguments presented.

“The Patriarchate cannot remain on the sidelines of such a process. We hope that dialogue with the bill’s sponsors will lead to a positive outcome,” Jaghmaidze said.

Metropolitan Anton of Vani and Baghdati said the Georgian Patriarchate was examining the legislative initiative concerning international gambling tournaments and preparing its official position on the matter.

According to the metropolitan, the Patriarchate will hold a discussion on 30 October to examine potential risks associated with the bill, after which it will formulate and publicly announce its unified position.

“Judging by what is apparent so far, I see certain risks. We have not yet fully examined the details — I have only heard some discussions about the issue on television. Of course, we will study the details and express our opinion. Frankly, much remains unclear, although we may still receive further explanations,” Metropolitan Anton said in an interview with InterPressNews.

He added that the Patriarchate intended to discuss the issue with government representatives and formulate its position on the bill in consultation with other senior clergy.

“Of course, we cannot remain indifferent,” the metropolitan said.

How has government policy on gambling changed?

In recent years, the Georgian Dream party’s gambling policy has primarily focused on tightening restrictions and limiting the number of people allowed to gamble.

During the early years of Georgian Dream’s rule, parliament twice rejected legislative initiatives aimed at banning gambling s and tightening regulations, in 2013 and 2019. In 2013, one of the arguments against such measures was the potential damage to the advertising industry, while Bidzina Ivanishvili warned of the risk of creating an unfavourable investment climate.

The situation changed significantly in late 2021, when parliament adopted a comprehensive package of gambling regulations. According to the government, the measures were intended to restrict access to gambling and limit its advertising.

Major restrictions came into force in March 2022:

The minimum gambling age for Georgian citizens was raised to 25.

Socially vulnerable individuals, public officials and people included in a designated register were banned from gambling.

Gambling s were banned on television, outdoors and on Georgian websites, with limited exceptions for certain forms of sponsorship.

Taxation and regulatory oversight were tightened.

The minimum gambling age for foreign nationals remained 18.

Subsequent changes revealed a distinct approach: maintaining strict restrictions for the local population while encouraging the development of the gambling industry targeting foreign customers.

According to an industry review published in June 2026, the government introduced a bill to establish preferential licensing and tax arrangements for online gambling companies targeting overseas customers.

The initiative proposed incentives for operators serving foreign markets, while maintaining a higher tax burden on the segment of the industry catering to Georgian citizens.

World.title: Armenian parliament ratifies framework agreement on Trump Route (TRIPP) project
World.content:
Armenia ratifies agreement on TRIPP project

The parliament of Armenia has ratified a framework agreement on strategic co-operation under the Trump Route for International Peace and Prosperity (TRIPP) project. The parties initialled the document during Marco Rubio’s visit to Yerevan on 26 May 2026 and signed the final version remotely just a few days later.

TRIPP (Trump Route for International Peace and Prosperity) is a road that will connect Azerbaijan with its Nakhchivan exclave through Armenian territory. The project also aims to reopen regional transport links. As a result, Armenia will gain access to third countries via Azerbaijan. For several years, Yerevan and Baku could not agree on this issue. Azerbaijan demanded a road that it called the “Zangezur corridor”. Armenia’s authorities said they were ready to reopen all transport routes but rejected the term “corridor”, arguing that it implied a loss of Armenian control and sovereign rights over the territory. The two sides reached an agreement only on 8 August in Washington. Under the deal, the road will remain under Armenia’s sovereign control, while the US will join the project as a business partner. The initiative took the name “Trump Route” after the US president, who mediated the agreement.

Parliament ratified the agreement with 63 votes in favour and 32 against. Only MPs from the ruling faction supported it.

The parliamentary opposition had announced in advance that it would vote against ratification of the framework agreement. Opposition MPs argued that the document took US and Azerbaijani interests into account but failed to protect Armenia’s interests.

MPs from the ruling faction, by contrast, believe the project will reopen regional transport links on the basis of reciprocity. In their view, this would benefit Armenia economically. The opposition disagrees, pointing to the lack of any financial assessments.

Debates on ratifying the TRIPP project began in parliament the previous day. MPs had only two hours for the discussion. However, opposition lawmakers managed to raise all their concerns and put forward several proposals.

Opposition MP on the interests of the US, Armenia and Azerbaijan

Anna Grigoryan, head of the opposition Armenia faction, noted that Armenia and the United States had signed a bilateral document concerning the implementation of TRIPP. However, she said, the document also refers to a third party — Azerbaijan.

“Azerbaijan’s interests are actually reflected in this document more directly and clearly than the interests of the Republic of Armenia.”

Grigoryan also outlined what she believes each side stands to gain from the project.

“The US gains a direct presence in the region, particularly along the border with Iran, in a strategically crucial area. Azerbaijan secures a link between Nakhchivan and the rest of the country — a goal that both Azerbaijan and Turkey have long pursued.”

When asked what Armenia stands to gain, she said the question was harder to answer.

“When the political majority tries to answer this question, the first word they use is ‘unblocking’. But on the ground, no transport links are being reopened and no borders are opening. So that part of the answer does not reflect reality.”

Should the launch of TRIPP be linked to the signing of a peace treaty?

Narek Karapetyan, leader of the opposition Strong Armenia faction, is concerned that Azerbaijan may lose its incentive to sign a peace treaty once the Trump Route begins operating.

“Azerbaijan gets what it set out to achieve, while what we are supposed to get — peace — could be postponed for five to ten years. Why would they sign a peace treaty with Armenia if they are already getting a link to Nakhchivan?”

Official Yerevan has not ruled out the possibility that the Trump Route could begin operating before Armenia and Azerbaijan sign a peace treaty.

The MP argues that the two important issues should not be treated separately. He proposes linking the implementation of the Trump Route to the signing of a peace treaty.

Deputy Speaker of the National Assembly Ruben Rubinyan disagreed. In his view, it is a positive development that TRIPP can proceed without depending on the signing of a peace treaty.

“If you argue that we should not implement this project in order to secure the signing of a peace treaty, you are saying that TRIPP is a bad initiative for Armenia. But TRIPP is by no means a bad initiative for Armenia.”

The ruling party representative welcomed the prospect of “elements of peace taking shape on the ground” independently of the peace treaty. By “elements of peace”, Rubinyan means both the launch of the Trump Route and the ongoing process of delimiting and demarcating the border between the two countries.

Background to the Trump Route project

The Trump Route offers Armenia a real opportunity to reopen regional transport links. For Azerbaijan, it provides the shortest route connecting the country with Nakhchivan.

The project envisages using the railway along a stretch of about 43km through Armenian territory. A motorway, energy infrastructure and digital communications links will also run through the area.

All infrastructure located on Armenian territory will remain under Armenia’s sovereignty and jurisdiction.

The ratified framework agreement provides for the establishment of TRIPP Development Company, which will oversee the project’s development and implementation.

Initially, the US will own 74% of the company’s shares and Armenia will hold 26%. After 49 years, if the parties extend their co-operation for a further 50 years, Armenia’s stake will rise to 49%. Armenia will grant TRIPP Development Company exclusive rights to use and develop land, along with other necessary powers within the areas allocated to the project, for 49 years.

Armenia and the US still need to agree on and adopt the company’s charter and shareholder agreement.

It also remains unclear what border-crossing arrangements will apply to Armenian citizens travelling through Nakhchivan.

Foreign Minister Ararat Mirzoyan said the two sides had yet to agree on the technical details of travel through Azerbaijani territory.

“We still need to discuss these issues with Azerbaijan. They fall within the framework of Armenia–Azerbaijan relations.” Armenia–Azerbaijan relations.”

Armenia ratifies agreement on TRIPP project

World.title: ‘Like a black cat in a dark room’: Georgia’s opposition ban case enters sixth day of hearings
World.content:
What happened at Georgia’s opposition ban hearing

On 28 October, Georgia’s Constitutional Court held the sixth day of hearings on a lawsuit filed by the ruling Georgian Dream party seeking to ban five opposition parties. The court is currently hearing submissions from the parties involved. On Tuesday, it heard arguments from representatives of the Coalition for Change.

The lawsuit names the United National Movement, Coalition for Change, Lelo – Strong Georgia, Gakharia for Georgia and the Federalists. Georgian Dream argues that these parties have violated Article 23 of the Constitution, which prohibits political parties whose aims include overthrowing or forcibly changing the country’s constitutional order. One of the arguments is that the parties refuse to recognise the legitimacy of the current authorities. The lawsuit also accuses them of organising attempts to overthrow the government. The United National Movement faces additional accusations of undermining Georgia’s independence and violating its territorial integrity. The lawsuit holds the party responsible for the August 2008 war with Russia over South Ossetia, when it was in power. All five opposition parties reject the accusations. Hearings are scheduled to continue through 30 October. The court must deliver its final ruling by 24 June 2027. A simple majority is required to uphold the claim, meaning at least four of the seven judges must vote in favour.

The Coalition for Change is represented in court by Nika Gvaramia, Tengo Tevzadze, Maia Kopaleishvili, Giga Lemonjava and Marika Arevadze. None of their motions was granted.

Constitutional Court President Revaz Nadaraia clashed twice with the coalition’s representatives, over their citation of a European Parliament resolution and their reference to the “Russian doctrine”.

The hearings will resume on 29 October at 11 a.m.

Judge Nadaraia: “European Parliament resolution is irrelevant to this case”

Giga Lemonjava presented an 8 October 2026 European Parliament resolution at the hearing. The resolution compared the Georgian ruling party’s bid to ban opposition parties with the Russian and Belarusian models, describing it as part of a strategy to eliminate political pluralism and turn Georgia into a one-party state.

Constitutional Court President Revaz Nadaraia interrupted the presentation and asked how the resolution was relevant to the proceedings. Lemonjava replied that it was not directly relevant to the case but that the public should be informed about it.

Nika Gvaramia commented: “Public hearings mean that participants are speaking not only to the court but also to the public.”

Nadarაიa responded: “Public hearings mean that everyone can follow the proceedings, not that someone can make political statements here.” He also reprimanded Gvaramia, saying: “You are interrupting me and disrupting the proceedings.”

Judge Nadaraia says comparison with Russia’s new doctrine is irrelevant to court proceedings

Constitutional Court President Revaz Nadaraia raised a similar objection for a second time during Giga Lemonjava’s address.

The opposition representative drew attention to two claims in the lawsuit against the opposition: that the previous government, when the United National Movement was in power, artificially restored the borders of the former South Ossetian Autonomous Region in 2007 and started the war with Russia in 2008.

Lemonjava argued that these claims closely matched Russia’s new foreign policy and security doctrine. If the court accepted them, he said, a Georgian state institution would be giving legal legitimacy to Russia’s version of events for the first time. “You need to be aware of this danger,” he told the judges.

Lemonjava also argued that giving legal force to these claims would contradict Article 78 of Georgia’s Constitution, which obliges state institutions to take all measures to ensure the country’s full integration into the European Union and NATO.

Nadaraia did not allow Lemonjava to continue with this line of argument, describing his remarks as “demagoguery” and saying he had gone beyond the scope of the proceedings. The judge again told him not to interrupt.

Judge Gotsiridze: “Do not look for a black cat where there is none”

Maia Kopaleishvili, representing the Coalition for Change, and Constitutional Court judge Eva Gotsiridze previously served together on the court’s panel. At the hearing, they clashed over a section of the lawsuit concerning an alleged attempt to enter parliament.

Kopaleishvili questioned whether Gotsiridze had studied the ruling party’s lawsuit thoroughly enough. The judge called the remark inappropriate.

“Perhaps this issue simply needs clarification. Do not look for a black cat where there is none,” Gotsiridze replied.

Opposition representative Kopaleishvili tells ruling party lawyers: “You were my students”

Maia Kopaleishvili addressed Archil Gorduladze and Tornike Cheishvili, who are representing the ruling party in court.

“You said opposition parties should be banned to protect future generations from a threat. You were my students. What threat do my colleagues and I pose to the country’s future?” Kopaleishvili asked.

Gvaramia warns of return to Soviet-style one-party elections

Nika Gvaramia noted that 28 October marked 36 years since Georgia held its first multiparty elections in 1990, as the Soviet Union was breaking apart.

“And now we are going back to where we started,” he said.

Gvaramia also described as a “distorted reality” the attempt to remove Lelo opposition party leader Badri Japaridze from politics, despite his being one of the signatories of Georgia’s 1991 Act of Restoration of State Independence.

Opposition assesses court hearing

Tornike Artkmeladze, a member of Lelo, said after the hearing that banning opposition parties in a single move would destroy what had been painstakingly built over the past 35 years.

“This is preparation for the first stage of clearing the political field — first of parties, and then they will move on to banning any active political activity. Georgian Dream wants to be the only force on the political scene. But they fail to understand that there are at least a million people in this country who will not give up their freedom,” Artkmeladze said.

News in Georgia

World.title: Nar CEO leads digital technology training (PHOTO)
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 30. Affordable mobile operator Nar has organized a training session entitled “How the Digital World Works: Understanding the Internet” for beneficiaries of the DOST Centre for Inclusive Development and Creativity and participants in the Volunteer DOST programme, as part of its ongoing cooperation with the Centre. Led by Nar CEO Ozgur Genc, the session provided young people with a deeper understanding of how the internet works and the opportunities offered by digital technologies. Approximately 100 people attended the training.

During the session, participants learned how the internet operates, how devices connect to networks, how data is transmitted over the internet and how web pages are displayed on screens. Key technological innovations that have shaped the development of the internet, the distinction between the web and the internet, and the functions of the Domain Name System (DNS) and servers were also explained through simple, accessible examples. The interactive format encouraged participants to explore the subject and engage in discussions.

Before the training session, Elnara Ansari, Director of the DOST Centre for Inclusive Development and Creativity, introduced Nar CEO Ozgur Genc, and company representatives to the Centre’s activities. During the visit, the guests explored the facilities available in the training studios, learned about the activities conducted there, and observed the training process.

Nar considers inclusivity one of its core priorities and recognizes the importance of ensuring that young people from vulnerable groups can benefit from digital opportunities. Through its initiatives, the company contributes to the development of digital knowledge and skills and helps expand access to information and technology. Its partnership with the DOST Centre for Inclusive Development and Creativity also aims to help children from vulnerable groups become more familiar with the digital world, acquire new knowledge and gain greater opportunities for personal development.

Currently serving 2.2 million subscribers, Nar has been Azerbaijan's leading mobile operator in terms of the Customer Loyalty Index for the past seven years. This achievement reflects Nar's consistently customer-focused strategy. The mobile operator provides its customers with reliable, high-quality telecommunications services, a range of internet packages and modern eSIM technology at affordable prices.

World.title: European Parliament delegation visits Kazakhstan's Kuryk port
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 30. A delegation of the European Parliament visited Kazakhstan's Kuryk port in the Mangystau region to learn about its infrastructure, operational capacity, and role in the development of the Trans-Caspian International Transport Route (Middle Corridor), Kazakhstan Railways national company announced today.

The delegation was received by Bakytkerey Alibekov, Deputy Director for Operations at Kuryk Port LLP, who briefed the visitors on the port's activities, production facilities, infrastructure and logistics potential.

Particular attention was paid to the port's role in developing the Middle Corridor and prospects for strengthening international transport and logistics cooperation.

Located on the eastern coast of the Caspian Sea, south of the port of Aktau, Kuryk port is situated in a natural bay that provides more favorable weather conditions for cargo handling operations, particularly the loading and unloading of railway wagons onto ferries.

The port's ferry complex is designed to handle grain, oil products, fertilizers, chemicals and other types of cargo.

In the first six months of 2026, Kuryk Port LLP handled 884,800 tonnes of cargo. Of this volume, 475,500 tonnes were transported by rail, including 242,300 tonnes of exports and 233,200 tonnes of imports, while road transport accounted for 306,200 tonnes, comprising 151,400 tonnes of exports and 154,800 tonnes of imports. A further 104,100 tonnes of grain were handled through the port's grain terminal.

In 2025, the total volume of cargo handled through Kuryk port amounted to 1.956 million tonnes.

World.title: Azerbaijan-Georgia Economic Cooperation Commission holds 11th meeting (PHOTO)
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 30. The 11th meeting of the Joint Intergovernmental Commission on Economic Cooperation between Azerbaijan and Georgia was held in Sighnaghi town, Kakheti region of Georgia, co-chaired by Prime Ministers Ali Asadov and Irakli Kobakhidze.

This was reported by the Azerbaijani Cabinet of Ministers.

According to the report, the meeting included an exchange of views on the current state and future development prospects of the strategic partnership between Azerbaijan and Georgia, as well as on expanding cooperation in areas such as trade and economy, investment, energy, transport and transit, agriculture, culture, and humanitarian affairs.

Asadov noted that high-level political dialogue and reciprocal visits play a decisive role in the development of bilateral relations. In this context, it was highlighted that the agreements reached during the state visit of the President of the Republic of Azerbaijan Ilham Aliyev to Georgia in April of this year, as well as the visit of the Prime Minister of Georgia to Azerbaijan in May, have reaffirmed the strategic nature of the cooperation between the two nations and provided fresh impetus for the expansion of collaboration across various sectors.

During the meeting, it was emphasized with satisfaction that Azerbaijan and Georgia cooperate effectively within the framework of international organizations, demonstrating mutual support, particularly regarding issues of state sovereignty and territorial integrity.

The positive dynamics of trade and economic cooperation were highly commended. At the meeting, it was highlighted that Georgia is one of Azerbaijan’s key trading partners. The meeting noted that in the first nine months of the current year, trade turnover between the two countries increased by 42%, surpassing the total figure for the previous year and approaching $1 billion.

The meeting also remarked that cooperation in the investment sphere is developing successfully, with Azerbaijan being one of the largest investors in the Georgian economy.

Emphasizing the positive momentum in the implementation of joint investment projects, the opening of a new hotel in Tbilisi, realized by an Azerbaijani investor, was cited as a prime example of this cooperation.

During the meeting, it was stressed that the energy sector is one of the key pillars of the strategic partnership between Azerbaijan and Georgia. The meeting highlighted that large-scale joint energy projects, such as the Baku-Tbilisi-Ceyhan oil pipeline and the Southern Gas Corridor, have played a significant role in ensuring energy security for both the region and Europe.

The meeting emphasized the successful ongoing cooperation in the electric power sector, highlighting that Azerbaijan provided prompt assistance in response to a request from the Georgian side following a crisis in Georgia’s energy system in July this year.

During the meeting, special attention was devoted to the prospects for cooperation in the field of renewable energy. The importance of ongoing efforts to establish a corridor for the transport of green energy to Europe, involving both Azerbaijan and Georgia, was underscored.

Cooperation in the transport and transit sector was also a primary topic of discussion. The meeting noted that Azerbaijan and Georgia serve as key partners in the development of international transport corridors, with particular emphasis on the importance of joint efforts to enhance the competitiveness and transit potential of the Middle Corridor. Issues regarding the expansion of border-crossing capabilities within the framework of transport infrastructure development were also reviewed.

The significance of the project to establish a joint border-crossing point, "Silk Road (Aghstafa) – Abreshumis Gza (Gardabani)", on the Azerbaijan-Georgia state border was highlighted. Confidence was expressed that the document intended for signing during the meeting, concerning the practical implementation of this project, would contribute to accelerating the relevant work.

The meeting emphasized significant potential for developing cooperation in the agricultural sector. Confidence was expressed that the bilateral documents to be signed during the meeting, covering plant quarantine and protection, as well as veterinary matters, would help simplify relevant control procedures and increase the mutual trade of agricultural products.

The meeting also addressed issues related to environmental protection and the efficient use of water resources. Emphasizing the strategic importance of the Kura river basin for both countries, the necessity of increasing joint efforts toward the protection, prevention of pollution, and sustainable management of transboundary water resources was noted.

The meeting noted that cultural and humanitarian cooperation constitutes an important component of Azerbaijan-Georgia relations. The special role of interaction in the fields of culture, education, and humanitarian affairs in preserving and developing the historical ties of friendship between the two peoples was stressed.

Members of the delegations delivered reports regarding the issues on the agenda.

At the conclusion of the meeting, Prime Ministers Ali Asadov and Irakli Kobakhidze signed the Protocol of the 11th meeting of the Joint Intergovernmental Commission on Economic Cooperation between Azerbaijan and Georgia.

World.title: Kazakhstan, Texas discuss trade, investment, economic cooperation
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 30. Consul General of Kazakhstan in Houston Gabdulla Ospankulov met with Texas Secretary of State Robert Howden at the Texas State Capitol, according to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Kazakhstan.

During the meeting, the parties discussed prospects for developing cooperation between Kazakhstan and Texas, focusing on expanding trade and economic ties, attracting investment, and strengthening business contacts.

Ospankulov noted that Texas, one of the largest U.S. states in terms of economic potential, was of significant interest to Kazakhstan in developing trade and economic relations.

The meeting also highlighted the role of the Consulate General in facilitating economic ties and expanding cooperation between Kazakhstan and Texas. Information was also shared about the upcoming launch of consular services in Houston.

The parties expressed interest in further strengthening their partnership, including through expanded cooperation in education, culture and humanitarian affairs.

The meeting took place amid broader efforts to expand Kazakhstan-U.S. cooperation. On October 19, 2026, Kazakh Foreign Minister Mukhtar Tleuberdi met with U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio in Samarkand. The two officials discussed prospects for further developing the enhanced strategic partnership, with a focus on trade, economic, and investment cooperation.

Trade turnover between Kazakhstan and the United States reached $3.2 billion in 2025. In the first quarter of 2026, it exceeded $1 billion, up around 10% compared with the same period of the previous year.

Kazakhstan’s President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has also received an invitation to attend the G20 summit, scheduled to take place in Miami in December 2026.

World.title: Russia’s Nordwind Airlines to connect Kazan and Uzbek Fergana from Nov. 25
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 30. Russia’s Nordwind Airlines will launch direct scheduled flights between Kazan and Fergana, Uzbekistan, on November 25, 2026, expanding its presence in the country.

According to Uzbekistan Airports, the airline will operate one flight per week, on Wednesdays, using Airbus A321 aircraft. The flight will take approximately three hours and 30 minutes.

The launch of the new route follows negotiations between Uzbekistan Airports and Nordwind Airlines, including talks held on the sidelines of the international aviation forum NETWORK 2026 in Moscow on September 16-18. During the discussions, the parties explored opportunities to launch additional flights to regional airports in Uzbekistan and expand existing routes.

Fergana will become the fourth Uzbek city connected to Kazan by Nordwind Airlines. Since the start of the 2026 summer season, the carrier has operated flights from Kazan to Tashkent, Samarkand and Namangan.

The new route will offer passengers from Russia’s Tatarstan region and Uzbekistan’s Fergana Valley a direct travel option, eliminating the need for connecting flights. It is also expected to facilitate family visits, business trips and tourism between the two destinations.

Nordwind Airlines is a Russian carrier operating domestic and international passenger services. The addition of Fergana to its route network further expands air connectivity between Russia and Uzbekistan.

World.title: Brent crude could reach $131 per barrel amid Middle East escalation - OIES
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 30. The price of Brent crude could rise to $131 per barrel if the conflict in the Middle East escalates.

This was stated in the Oxford Institute for Energy Studies (OIES) Oil Monthly report.

According to the report, the risks surrounding Brent crude oil prices remain skewed to the upside. The additional upside potential relative to the baseline forecast is estimated at $2.9 per barrel in 2026 and $5.8 per barrel in 2027.

The report said that the new escalation of the conflict in the Middle East in Q4 2026, accompanied by attacks on oil infrastructure and/or disruptions to transit through the Strait of Hormuz and the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, could lead to a partial halt in the recent recovery of supplies and exacerbate constraints on oil transportation.

"Against the backdrop of depleted inventories, in such a scenario, the price of Brent could rise to $131 per barrel in Q4 2026 and to $96 in 2027. This is $19 and $9 higher than the baseline forecast, respectively.

Another scenario assumes a slower recovery in liquid hydrocarbon supplies from the Middle East amid ongoing operational and export constraints, as well as the absence of a long-term resolution to the conflict. In this case, a slowdown in inventory buildup could push the Brent price up to $117 per barrel in the fourth quarter of 2026 and to $96 in 2027.

More resilient demand, supported by a recovery in the availability of petroleum products, could raise the 2027 Brent price forecast by $3.50 to $90 per barrel,” the institute’s report noted.

At the same time, the OIES also considered scenarios in which prices could fall.

“A diplomatic breakthrough in the fourth quarter of 2026, leading to the lifting of the U.S. blockade of Iranian ports and a relaxation of sanctions enforcement, could contribute to increased oil exports, lower transportation costs, and reduced risks of supply disruptions.

“As a result, the price of Brent could fall to $83 per barrel in 2027,” the report remarked.

Besides, a full or near-full recovery in production in the Middle East by the end of 2027 could accelerate the replenishment of inventories and lead to a decline in the average annual price of Brent to $83 per barrel.

"OIES considers weakening demand to be the most significant downside risk. The prolonged impact of high fuel prices and pressure on industrial activity could limit oil consumption. Under this scenario, the price of Brent could fall to approximately $75 per barrel in the second quarter of 2027, with the annual average dropping to $79.

Overall, according to OIES’s assessment, the aggregate range of possible average annual Brent prices is $95–$105 per barrel in 2026 and $71–$109 in 2027,” the institute’s report added.

World.title: Kyrgyzstan's Transport Ministry receives over 50 new road machinery units
World.content:
Photo: Press Service of the Cabinet of Ministers of Kyrgyzstan

BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 30. Kyrgyzstan's Ministry of Transport and Communications has received more than 50 units of new specialized machinery for the country's road sector.

According to the press service of the Cabinet of Ministers of Kyrgyzstan, First Deputy Prime Minister and Head of the Presidential Administration Adylbek Kasymaliev handed over the keys to the new machinery at Turdakun Usubaliev Square during events marking the professional holiday of road transport and road infrastructure workers.

Transport and Communications Minister Talantbek Soltobaev presented the new specialized machinery, which includes dump trucks, motor graders, and loaders.

Adylbek Kasymaliev noted that upgrading the fleet of specialized machinery would strengthen the material and technical base of the country's road sector, support road construction, and improve the quality and efficiency of repair works.

Furthermore, Adylbek Kasymaliev then proceeded to the Toktogul Satylganov Kyrgyz National Philharmonic, where he attended a ceremony dedicated to the professional holiday of road sector workers.

Kyrgyzstan's road transport and road infrastructure sectors are overseen by the Ministry of Transport and Communications, which is responsible for the development, construction, maintenance, and repair of the country's road network.

Road infrastructure is an important component of Kyrgyzstan's transport system, connecting domestic regions and providing access to international transport corridors. The development of the road network is also relevant to the country's role in regional trade and transit transportation.

World.title: EU highlights Turkmenistan's role in regional methane reduction efforts
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 30. The European Union has praised Turkmenistan's participation in international efforts to reduce methane emissions and reaffirmed its readiness to support the country and other Central Asian states in addressing this issue.

According to a press release published by the press service of Turkmenistan, the remarks were made by Maciej Adam Madalinski, Deputy Head of the Delegation of the European Union to Turkmenistan, at the regional conference titled “From Methane Data to Action: Strengthening Methane Emissions Management, Mobilizing Capital and Advancing Regional Cooperation in Central Asia,” held in Ashgabat on October 29-30.

“Turkmenistan is one of the first countries in the Central Asian region to have expressed its commitment to international efforts to reduce methane emissions. This once again confirms the importance of this issue,” the diplomat said.

Madalinski expressed confidence that Turkmenistan would continue to strengthen its efforts in this area, noting that practical measures to reduce methane emissions could have a positive impact on the planet's ecosystems.

He also recalled the recent participation of a European delegation in the Oil and Gas of Turkmenistan 2026 (OGT 2026) international conference in Ashgabat. In this regard, he welcomed the participation of state concerns Turkmengaz and Turkmennebit in the United Nations' Oil and Gas Methane Partnership 2.0 (OGMP 2.0), an initiative aimed at systematically monitoring and reducing methane emissions in the energy sector.

The EU representative reaffirmed the readiness of European countries to support Turkmenistan and other countries in the region through the promotion of advanced technologies and clean energy standards.

World.title: Breaking: Australians potentially impacted by Spain rail disaster, DFAT says
World.content:
Australian authorities are working to confirm the wellbeing of two Australians after the deadly train crash in Spain earlier this week.

A statement from the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade says consular assistance is being provided to the family of two Australians in connection with the collision.

"Our heartfelt condolences are with the families and loved ones of those killed, with those injured and all affected by the train collision in Spain," a spokesperson said.

The crash in central Spain on Wednesday killed at least 69 people.

Transport Minister Oscar Puente said the security system on a stretch of track stopped working due to a computer malfunction, causing all trains on that stretch to stop.

Minutes after the order to stop was given, a train from state operator Renfe was told by central command it could run again without speed restrictions, leading it to collide with a train operated by the private Spanish company Iryo.

The resulting collision has become one of Europe's deadliest train disasters. Spain has since begun three days of mourning.

Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez, who faces a general election on November 29, pledged to establish the cause of the crash.

"We are working day and night not only to support the victims' families, but also to establish every last detail of this tragedy and strengthen safety measures to ensure it never happens again," he said.

World.title: Court hears suspended Torrens to Darlington contractor still awaiting $2m
World.content:
The labour hire company at the centre of a controversy surrounding alleged bikie threats is still awaiting a payment of about $2 million from the lead contractor of the South Australian government's Torrens to Darlington project, a court has heard.

The company, Career Boss Australia, had its contract to supply workers on the $15.4 billion South Road upgrade suspended on October 18 after it was revealed in the media it was the subject of a civil dispute in the Supreme Court.

That claim, lodged by businessman Robert Cammarano, alleges that bikie Jamie Brown "coerced the transfer" of shares in the company, without Mr Cammarano's authority, by making "express threats of physical harm".

Mr Cammarano's claim also alleges other shareholders were threatened to transfer their shares.

Brown is yet to file a defence but has reportedly told 7News he had "never threatened any shareholder and allegations to the contrary are simply false".

At a hearing on Friday, barrister Tim Kentish, for Mr Cammarano, sought a freeze on a bank account connected to Career Boss Australia.

He said the company was still expecting a payment "around the $2 million mark" from John Holland, the lead contractor on the Torrens to Darlington project.

"That was the vast bulk of the revenue that's been coming in to this company — there's not a lot else," Mr Kentish said of the South Road contract.

"There's a final payment coming in, that's due to come in from John Holland for work performed, they pay in arrears, in the order of a couple million dollars."

The Torrens to Darlington project is expected to cost about $15 billion and is the most expensive infrastructure project ever carried out in South Australia. (Supplied: SA Government)

Subpoena sought for recording of meeting

Mr Kentish also asked for the judge to subpoena a recording he alleges police have obtained of a meeting between "various parties" where the alleged "expropriation of the shares" was discussed.

A Crown solicitor, appearing on behalf of the acting commissioner of SA Police, asked this request to be adjourned so police could consider the "scope of the orders and whether or not to agree".

Associate Justice Graham Dart agreed to defer consideration of the subpoena request.

He also ordered a temporary freeze on the bank account connected to Career Boss Australia.

Outside court, Mr Cammarano said "we had a good win today" but did not comment further.

The matter was adjourned until November 16.

'No payments being made', govt says

The case surrounding Career Boss Australia and involvement in South Australia's largest-ever infrastructure project has triggered an escalating political crisis for the Malinauskas government.

Mr Kentish notified Transport Minister Joe Szakacs's chief of staff and Child Protection Minister Alice Rolls about the allegations at a meeting on September 11.

Mr Szakacs's office passed on the claims to the South Road project team, which investigated the claims.

Robert Cammarano is a shareholder in Career Boss Australia. (ABC News: Daniel Taylor)

"The shareholders of Career Boss were looked at, as I am advised, by the Torrens to Darlington alliance and they had no red flags," Mr Szakacs told parliament on Wednesday.

The government asked the alliance to suspend Career Boss's contract when the civil case was reported by the Sunday Mail on October 18.

Lawyer Dominic Agresta, representing a listed shareholder of Career Boss, said the contract had "not been cancelled, it's been suspended".

"There's no evidence that it's going to be cancelled," Mr Agresta said.

"There is still an opportunity or a possibility of being renewed once this matter is resolved."

Associate Jusstice Dart replied: "Possibly, given the publicity, the government might be a little shy about it."

Police Minister Michael Brown, speaking at an unrelated press conference roughly an hour after the court hearing, said the Career Boss contract "remains suspended at the moment".

"There’s no reason to lift that suspension," he said.

"The important thing to note is it’s currently suspended – there are no payments being made to that company."

Stumps were just five minutes from being called.

Temba Bavuma had battled for 114 balls to stay in the middle.

If he was there in the morning, could South Africa build a good lead, anchored by their talismanic little skipper?

But on the 115th delivery he faced, for the first time in the match, he saw red and swung his bat wildly at Nathan Lyon.

The ball beat him, middle stump went back, and the Proteas' skipper had to depart with his side's hopes in tatters.

You've played a certain way. And that's cricket. It happens. "We've got two very capable batters at the crease and still a lot of batting to come. So there are going to be casualties along the way."

When all is said and done, will South Africa look back on that decision from their own little maestro as the turning point?

World.title: Man fined over Neo-Nazi stickers may face prison time for Nazi salute
World.content:
Warning: This story contains offensive content.

A Canberra man who stuck white supremacist stickers across an Indigenous learning centre at the Australian National University (ANU) has been fined $5,000 and could face prison time for performing the Nazi salute.

Zachary James Hook left stickers promoting the National Socialist Network and white supremacist slogans around the ANU's Tjabal Indigenous Higher Education Centre on two occasions last year.

The then-18-year-old pleaded guilty to offensive behaviour on Commonwealth premises, which carries a maximum penalty of $6,600.

He has also admitted to twice performing the Nazi salute in public, a Commonwealth charge introduced in 2024 which mandates at least 12 months' imprisonment.

But the ACT Magistrates Court today heard his penalty could exceed that once it goes before the territory's superior ACT Supreme Court next month.

Serious, targeted and clearly offensive conduct

Zachery Hook initially pleaded not guilty to the offences. (ABC News: Callum Flinn)

Court documents show Hook displayed stickers across the ANU campus on two occasions in August and September 2025 which bore slogans including "National Socialist Network", "Australia for the white man", and "White revolution is the only solution".

The National Socialist Network is a Neo-Nazi group that was banned earlier this year under the Australian government's hate speech laws, and is currently appealing that decision in the High Court.

The stickers were on a poster encouraging multiculturalism and on a cabinet and door inside the university's Black, Indigenous and People of Colour department building.

In sentencing, Magistrate James Lawton said social media had "no doubt had an impact" on Hook's behaviour.

Even if it was a form of protest, Magistrate Lawton said, Hook's conduct was serious, targeted and clearly offensive.

Zachery Hook was unable to be sentenced over the Nazi salutes in the ACT Magistrates Court because the possible prison sentence is more than it has jurisdiction to impose. (ABC News: Callum Flinn)

He said that even though Hook had acknowledged the impact of his behaviour, it was "somewhat troubling" he had not necessarily demonstrated a change in his views.

The magistrate imposed a $5,000 fine to account for Hook's guilty plea, clean criminal record and letter of apology.

But he could not sentence Hook for the second charge of performing a Nazi salute because of an "unusual" and "unique" sentencing dilemma.

Sentence for salute to be decided by ACT Supreme Court

The Commonwealth charge carries a minimum mandatory sentence of 12 months' imprisonment, but the ACT Magistrates Court did not have jurisdiction and could not impose a sentence of more than 12 months for the offending.

Because Hook's conduct was "not at the lower end of the scale," the magistrate committed the matter to the ACT Supreme Court, which is able to consider more severe penalties.

Zachery Hook will remain on bail until his case is heard in the ACT Supreme Court next month. (ABC News: Luke Stephenson)

The maximum penalty is five years' imprisonment.

"This court is not empowered … to impose an adequate penalty," the magistrate told the court today.

He referred to a recent matter in the NSW District Court where an 18-month sentence was imposed against a man who performed the Nazi salute on a Discord broadcast.

The magistrate said he regarded Hook's offending as "more serious" than the NSW case.

Hook, who spent three nights in custody after being arrested on Christmas Eve last year, will remain on bail until his matter is heard in the ACT Supreme Court next month.

World.title: Mouse welfare debate amid plan for NSW plastics recycling factory
World.content:
The welfare of mice used in medical research could be a key factor in plans for a plastics recycling factory in the NSW Southern Highlands.

RePoly has sought to overturn the Independent Planning Commission's rejection of the development at Moss Vale, prompting a 10-day hearing in the Land and Environment Court.

Opponents of the plan include the nearby Garvan Institute Australian BioResources (ABR) facility that breeds specialised laboratory mice used to study diseases such as cancer, diabetes and heart disease.

Laboratory mice bred at Garvan's Moss Vale facility are central to the factory dispute. (Supplied: Australian BioResources)

The Garvan Institute's barrister, Bora Kaplan SC, told the court the impact of smoke from plastic recycling and vibrations from truck movements had to be considered.

"It's an area where the mice live, breed at night, and sleep during the day," he said.

"The applicant, in our submission, has not proffered any credible information that would enable this court to perform the task of assessing the likely impacts of the proposed development.

"First of all, vibration impacts affecting mouse wellbeing and husbandry, and secondly, vibration impacts affecting microinjection."

Mr Kaplan told the court the microinjection process used on the mice was "extremely sensitive to vibrations".

He said adverse effects from the proposed development could jeopardise the medical research facility's future.

"There could be suspension of Garvin's accreditation and withdrawal of the supplier's license and ability to perform animal-based research," Mr Kaplan said.

The Australian BioResources facility is known locally as the "mouse house". (Supplied: Moss Vale Matters)

RePoly's barrister, Nick Eastman SC, argued it had not been possible to measure "a vibration criteria limit for the health of or comfort of the mice within their mouse pavilion".

"Do you want to give us a bunch of experimental mice and we will disrupt them until they cannibalise each other or some other bad event occurs?" he said.

" What is the testing that would necessarily need to occur? "

Mr Eastman argued the factory's environmental impacts could be adequately managed through strict conditions of approval, but acknowledged that a blaze sending smoke towards the research facility could have serious consequences.

"There is no dispute between the experts that a consequence of a fire that is uncontrolled, that's plumed and goes towards the ABR and requires evacuation for more than two days, will be dire," he said.

"The question is the likelihood of that."

Southern Highlands residents have opposed the plastics factory proposal for almost six years. (ABC Illawarra: Justin Huntsdale)

Questions over assessments

The Independent Planning Commission (IPC) argued there were gaps in the assessment of noise, traffic, lighting and other environmental impacts.

Its barrister, Naomi Sharp SC, questioned noise modelling based on trucks travelling around the site at five kilometres an hour, without accounting for braking or acceleration on roads with gradients.

The factory is expected to generate at least 100 heavy vehicle movements a day, with deliveries and collections restricted to weekday daytime hours.

"If, as the consent authority, you do not feel equipped to make an assessment of the likely impacts, then the appropriate course is to refuse the consent," Ms Sharp said.

RePoly argued the assessments were sufficient for this stage of the planning process and further detailed studies and enforceable conditions could address outstanding issues.

Community opposition

More than 500 people gathered at the RePoly appeal hearing in Moss Vale. (ABC Illawarra: Justin Huntsdale)

The court also heard the development could have significant social impacts on the Southern Highlands community.

Turvey To SC, representing the second respondent community member Samantha Woods, argued the prolonged planning dispute had damaged community trust.

"The community doesn't consider it to be listened to, or its concerns taken seriously," the barrister said.

RePoly has maintained that the factory is a permissible industrial development and that its environmental and social impacts can be managed through appropriate safeguards.

The commissioner has reserved his decision.

World.title: Adelaide Crows star avoids jail for running red light and hitting pedestrian
World.content:
Adelaide Crows defender Josh Worrell has been assured he will not be sent to jail after pleading guilty to hitting a pedestrian with his car.

The 25-year-old appeared in the Adelaide Magistrates Court today and pleaded guilty to an aggravated charge of driving without due care over the crash on July 10, 2026.

He was also facing a charge of failing to stop, assist and present to police but it was dropped by the prosecution.

The court heard that Worrell had been driving along Port Road, on his way to training, when he ran a red light and collided with the victim.

"The footage does show his vehicle entering that pedestrian crossing at a somewhat considerable speed, although we don't allege he was exceeding the speed limit against a red traffic signal that had been displayed for several seconds," prosecutor Phoebe Foster-Richardson said.

"We submit … that Mr Worrell was either inattentive or distracted."

Worrell (centre) has played for Adelaide since 2020. (Getty Images)

Ms Foster-Richardson said she accepted Worrell was remorseful and did not assert that a period of imprisonment was necessary.

Instead, she said the prosecution was asking a conviction to be recorded and Worrell be sentenced to a short, good behaviour bond or be ordered to undertake community service.

Magistrate Rodney Oates agreed that a term of imprisonment was inappropriate and said it was not his "intention" to impose one.

Defence Barrister Andrew Culshaw, for Worrell, said his client was "embarrassed and remorseful" and made a "human mistake".

"He certainly should've done better," Mr Culshaw told the court.

"He is incredibly embarrassed and remorseful … to say nothing of relieved because he is acutely aware that this could have been worse."

Mr Culshaw also said his client prioritised getting his victim help and spent three hours with him.

"Rather than simply call for help and move on with his commitments he, I submit, really went above and beyond to assist the victim," he told the court.

"He took him to hospital, he stopped past the victim's house to get some tissues … for the cut to his head."

Worrell will return to court on Tuesday to be sentenced.

World.title: Anger after Google cuts 500 hectares of trees for data centres in Finland
World.content:
Finnish police have launched a criminal investigation into suspected breaches of environmental law at the construction site of a planned Google data centre.

The Oulu Police Department said on Thursday it had launched an investigation into Google's Finnish subsidiary, Tuike, over work conducted in Muhos in northern Finland.

Tuike cleared about 330 hectares of forest in Muhos and nearly 200 hectares at a second site in Kajaani before mandatory environmental impact assessments were completed.

Google recently announced a US$15 billion ($21 billion) investment in artificial intelligence infrastructure in Finland, described by the company as its largest investment in Europe.

The clear cutting has seen the US tech giant's plans mired in controversy, sparking criticism from citizens concerned about their impact.

How did the logging unfold?

Documents seen by Finnish newspaper Helsingin Sanomat (HS) revealed that logging at the Muhos site began in March and continued for months.

Finland's Supervisory Agency (LVV) responded to correspondence from Tuike in May, saying environmental impact assessments had to be completed before logging could begin.

In September, Google announced its plans to invest $21 billion over two years to build data centres in Finland.

A week later, Finnish news agency STT reported on allegations by an environmental organisation that Google had cleared forest illegally at the Muhos and Kajaani sites.

In early October, LVV ordered Google to halt work at both sites.

Google's Finland country manager, Antti Järvinen, apologised for the clearances and said the company believed the clear cuts complied with the law.

What is Google being investigated for?

The case was being investigated as "environmental degradation", police said, adding that additional criminal classifications would possibly be specified later in the investigation.

"We are investigating whether the company's operations have breached the water act and resulted in environmental damage," Detective Superintendent Kari Pakanen told Reuters news agency.

About 330 hectares of forest were cut in Muhos before appropriate environmental assessments were completed. (STT/Lehtikuva via Reuters: Ville Honkonen)

Preliminary information showed ambiguities and shortcomings in the drainage and water management at Tuike's site, police said in a statement.

Police said an update on the case would be given in December, but the investigation would extend into 2027.

Will Google face consequences?

A guilty finding in the investigation could lead to a corporate fine, Detective Pakanen said.

It is up to the regulator to decide on any permits to restart the work at the sites, he said.

Detective Pakanen declined to say whether any individuals could become a target of the investigation.

A Google spokesperson said the company was "actively responding to enquiries from LVV and other authorities".

What is happening at the data centre sites now?

LVV said the works would be halted temporarily until the mandatory environmental impact assessments had been completed.

An LVV spokesperson said it was unclear how long it might take before the agency grants the relevant permits.

Google's AI push

Google has data centres in 36 locations across four continents, with 31 more in development.

While data centres are expanding rapidly across the world, powering and cooling their servers requires large amounts of water and electricity.

New data centres set to escape rules Dozens of approved but yet-to-be-built AI data centre projects are expected to escape the federal government's proposed restrictions around energy and water use.

Finland's cool climate, low-carbon electricity and the government endorsement of AI projects have contributed to making it one of Europe's main destinations for data centre investments in recent years.

Google's planned investments in the Nordic country include data centres, electricity grid improvements and clean energy and battery projects to power services such as Google's AI Gemini, Search, Maps and YouTube.

There are concerns over an increased electricity demand pushing up power prices, but Finland Prime Minister Petteri Orpo last month played down those concerns and said the Google deal would boost the economy.

Speaking in parliament on Wednesday, Mr Orpo continued to back the investment by Google, but said the corporation would have to "learn" from the incident and follow the law.

More than 98,000 people have signed a petition demanding the Finnish government enact tougher regulations on data centres.

Similar concerns over the impacts of data centres are being echoed in communities around the world, including in Australia and the United States where the issue has become central in the country's crucial midterm elections.

ABC/wires

World.title: Minister concedes Alice Springs school upgrade funding inadequate
World.content:
An aging school needing a major makeover. And a merger just months away.

The Northern Territory education minister has conceded the $500,000 allocated to upgrade Alice Springs's only public high school is inadequate after touring its aging facilities.

Centralian Middle School and Centralian Senior College will begin merging into Alice Springs College next year, with years 11 and 12 relocating to the Gillen campus in 2028.

Jo Hersey says the merger between Centralian Middle School and Centralian Senior College will be ready by term one in 2027. (ABC News: Pete Garnish)

Education Minister Jo Hersey met with both school councils yesterday, and acknowledged the funding was insufficient to prepare the campus.

"Obviously we know the 500 is not going to cut it even just for what we need to do now," she told ABC Alice Springs.

" I have a commitment from the department that the money will be there to make the changes that need to happen for the start of the year. "

Ms Hersey said classroom modifications, lighting upgrades and replacement carpets should be completed before the 2027 school year.

Centralian Middle School does not have an operational lift. (Supplied)

Asked whether the campus was currently fit for purpose and equitable, she replied: "Not as I saw it yesterday, no."

Parents call for greater investment

Centralian Senior College School Council treasurer Elliat Rich described the initial $500,000 allocation as a "band-aid", saying the merger was an opportunity to invest properly in public education.

She said the proposed works represented the bare minimum needed to accommodate students, rather than the broader upgrades required to deliver a quality school environment.

Elliat Rich says the merger must deliver a quality school environment. (ABC News: Chris Murrkarany Fitzpatrick)

Ms Rich also criticised the merger process, describing it as "very opaque" and calling for clearer timelines, funding commitments and greater involvement from the school community.

She warned continued underinvestment in public education "will have far-reaching implications".

Long-term funding uncertain

Ms Hersey said she had expected upgrade works to have started already, after a decision to delay the merger by a year.

Construction is now expected to begin about November 24, with the minister guaranteeing the campus would be ready for the new school year.

She said a broader master plan was needed but could not confirm how far planning had progressed.

Asked what a comprehensive upgrade might cost, Ms Hersey suggested about $30 million, but acknowledged funding of that magnitude was unlikely in the next two territory budgets.

She has promised to provide both school councils with an updated plan within two weeks.

World.content:
LifestyleFashionDerby Day This AFL star has some style advice for men this Derby Day Courtney Thompson October 30, 2026 — 7:00pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items.
